summary:
The web entry is a case-upload console, not a knowledge hub. base.html's sidebar (10 items, last extended 2026-08-06) and index.html's header ("Dashboard / LIGGGHTS 파일을 업로드하고 DEM 분석을 실행하세요") tell a first-time visitor nothing about what the project is, that there are two independent pipelines (webapp = DEM contact-network; kit = MPM/STEP3 voxel), what STEP1–5 means, or that a ledger of retracted numbers governs every value on screen. There is no link anywhere in the entry or nav to CLAUDE.md, docs/reviews/claims.json, wiki/index.md, or any live track (Phase A, the manuscript hold, CL-81) — while deep pages in the same app (eis.html:29, viewer3d.js:6194/6210, seminar.html:206) do carry ledger pointers, so the discipline exists everywhere except at the front door. The good news: the ban sweep is clean (`check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` → "철회값 누수 없음 ✓", 844 files, and webapp/templates/*.html is in its scan roots), and the MPM regime badges were retro-fitted on 2026-08-25 with the CL-04 reservation in their tooltips. The bad news is that the reservation lives only in a hover tooltip: the same toolbar's 📊 공극률 CSV export ships the retracted "cross-validated = two independent models agree" verdict and the repo's explicitly do-not-expose `use_porosity_pct` column with no caveat at all (P0). Beneath that, the ranking UI — the entry page's only quality signal — is built on three divergent grading paths: list_cases uses the static 82-case corpus with the `bn_median_norm` axis, /api/all-grades uses the static corpus without it, and the case page uses the dynamic corpus, so the score on the dashboard is not the score on the case page, the carbon What-if silently drops a weighted axis, silently mixes overridden and baseline scores in one ordering while tagging every row 🧪, and silently loses the 🧫 "not comparable" unit-cell warning. The whole ranking rides on the analytic carbon what-if that single.html已 retired in favour of the GPU run. Add the name-fragment tier filter (2 mAh, 3.18 mAh and every unnamed timestamp case are invisible), a warning tooltip that renders `
` literally, a sort action that leaves the list silently filtered, and a nav that vanishes entirely below 768 px, and the entry page is roughly one month behind the work and four months behind the epistemology.

findings.locator: L69-70 (📊 공극률 CSV button) → webapp/app.py L7868-7998 (/porosity-corpus.csv)
findings.claim: The entry page's CSV export ships the retracted "DEM↔MPM agreement = cross-validation" verdict and the repo's explicitly do-not-expose `use_porosity_pct` column, framed as a "raw per-case dump", with no retraction notice anywhere in the file — while the badge two pixels away carries that notice.
findings.evidence: index.html:69-70 — `href="/porosity-corpus.csv" ... title="모든 케이스의 MPM/DEM 공극률 + 조성(AM:SE)·P:S·반경·SE-rich/SE-poor regime를 한 줄씩 CSV로 (form/외삽 아님 — raw per-case 덤프)"`. app.py:7938-7940 emits `regime = ('SE-poor' if _graw > 4.0 else 'SE-rich' if _graw < -4.0 else 'cross-validated')`; app.py:7952-7955 comment `cross-validated  : two independent models agree → use MPM.  ±2.4`; app.py:7986-7991 fieldnames include `'regime', 'use_source', 'use_porosity_pct'`; the response (app.py:7993-7998) is a bare CSV with no header comment or caveat column. CONTRADICTED BY (a) CLAUDE.md §"MPM scaffold porosity 신뢰성 regime map": "★★ 정정 2026-08-12 — '일치 = validity 증명서' 는 hold 시대에 성립하지 않는다 … 씨앗이 정답을 인코딩한다 … ⇒ 일치를 증명서로 쓰면 순환이다"; (b) claims.json CL-04 (live) verdict "h0·h1 둘 다 빗나갔다 — 정착 실측 1.13 %" vs experiment 15.6 %; (c) ledger CDX-16 rejected ("shared scaffold", not independent cross-validation); (d) CLAUDE.md §설계→구조 ML: "★ use_porosity_pct 는 학습·노출 금지 열" and "REJECT 1 = use_porosity_pct .397"; (e) the same webapp already says it: seminar.html:206-207 — "⚠ 철회된 주장 — '독립 보정된 두 모델이 1 %p 이내 일치' 는 독립 교차검증이 아니다"; (f) the "raw" framing is contradicted by scripts/ml_design_structure.py:563 ("`use_porosity_pct` 는 regime-gate 가 … 고른 **스위치된** 양") and :885 ("raw DEM/MPM 아님").
findings.proposed_action: Emit a caveat as the CSV's first line (or a `caveat` column on every row) naming CL-04 and the 2026-08-12 correction; rename the `cross-validated` regime value to a neutral `gap_le_4`; drop `use_porosity_pct`/`use_source` from the export or rename them to `gated_porosity_pct_DO_NOT_REGRESS` with the ban cited; and change the button tooltip so it no longer calls a gate-switched quantity a raw dump.

findings.locator: L548-587 (list_cases grade block) vs L729-818 (_build_dynamic_corpus_rows / _grade_engine_result), consumed by index.html L125-127 and L256-302
findings.claim: The score and grade a visitor sees in the dashboard ranking are computed against a different corpus than the score and grade shown when they open that same case, so the entry page's ordering does not match the case pages it links to.
findings.evidence: list_cases (app.py:569-575) hard-codes the static baseline: `corpus_csv = os.path.join(..., 'docs', 'data', 'se_diagnostics_82.csv')` … `build_overall_grade(_inject_input_params(m, results_dir), corpus_csv, se_aux, case_id=case_id)`, and index.html:125-127 renders that as `data-overall-score` / `data-overall-grade`. The case page goes through app.py:5824 `build_overall_grade_table(metrics, results_dir)` → `_grade_engine_result` (app.py:794) `corpus_rows = _build_dynamic_corpus_rows(static_csv)` → `build_overall_grade(..., corpus_rows=corpus_rows)`. The dynamic path's own docstring (app.py:733-738) states the point: "Corpus for percentile-ranked grade axes = static baseline … ∪ every live case's SE-diagnostics … This makes corpus-relative grades reflect the growing dataset" — the entry page opts out of exactly that.
findings.proposed_action: Route list_cases through `_grade_engine_result` (or pass `corpus_rows=_build_dynamic_corpus_rows(...)`) so the dashboard, /api/all-grades and /single all grade against one corpus; until then, label the dashboard badge "static-82 corpus" so the mismatch is visible.

findings.locator: L279-282 (carbonTag) with L322-326 (applyRanking fallback) and webapp/app.py L3702-3703
findings.claim: When the carbon What-if is on, any case missing from the override map keeps its baseline score but is still tagged 🧪 "carbon override 적용", so one ordered list silently mixes two scenarios and mislabels which rows were re-computed.
findings.evidence: index.html:279-282 — `const carbonTag = overrides ? '🧪' : '';` — the tag is keyed on `overrides` being non-null, not on this row's `ov`. index.html:322-326 — `const sa = scoreOverrides && scoreOverrides[a.dataset.caseId]?.score; … const va = Number.isFinite(sa) ? sa : parseFloat(a.dataset.overallScore);` — missing rows silently fall back to the baseline score. Rows go missing whenever /api/all-grades skips a case: app.py:3702-3703 `except Exception:` / `continue` (and app.py:3665-3671 `continue` when full_metrics.json is absent or unreadable).
findings.proposed_action: Gate `carbonTag` on `ov` (per-row), and either exclude non-overridden rows from the What-if ranking or mark them explicitly (e.g. a grey 'baseline' chip) so a single list never blends the two scenarios.

findings.claim: Flipping the carbon What-if silently deletes a weighted grade axis for every case — the `__bn_median_norm` (백본 두께, weight 0.7) axis — because /api/all-grades builds its se_aux without the key that list_cases includes, so scores and the displayed n_axes move for a reason that has nothing to do with carbon.
findings.evidence: list_cases (app.py:559-566) builds `se_aux = { 'n_percolating': …, 'articulation_points': …, 'n_bn_below_threshold': …, 'n_perc_edges': …, 'bn_median_norm': _aux.get('se_bn_median_norm') }`. /api/all-grades (app.py:3676-3684) builds the same dict but stops at `'n_perc_edges': _aux.get('se_n_perc_edges'),` — no `bn_median_norm`. grade_engine.py:825-830 resolves that axis only from `aux.get('bn_median_norm') or aux.get('se_bn_median_norm')`, and grade_engine.py:131-137 gives it `'weight': 0.7`. The badge advertises the axis count that changes: index.html:296 `gb.title = \`${nAxes}개 평가축에서 가중평균 ${scoreStr}점\``. The canonical path (app.py:766-772) does include `bn_median_norm`.
findings.proposed_action: Add `'bn_median_norm': _aux.get('se_bn_median_norm')` to the /api/all-grades se_aux (and to /case/<id>/grade, app.py:3752-3760, which has the same omission), or better, have all three call the single `_grade_engine_result` helper.

findings.claim: The 🧫 "unit cell — not directly comparable to full cells" warning disappears in exactly the view where cases are ranked against each other, because the client throws away the flag the server sends.
findings.evidence: index.html:339 — `map[c.case_id] = { score: c.score, grade: c.grade, n_axes: c.n_axes };` (no `is_unit_cell`), while app.py:3695-3699 does return it: `'n_axes': r['composite']['n_axes'], 'is_unit_cell': r['composite'].get('is_unit_cell', False), …`. index.html:283-288 then reads `const isUC = overrides ? overrides[tr.dataset.caseId]?.is_unit_cell : (tr.dataset.unitCell === 'true');` → always `undefined` under overrides, so the tag whose own title reads "단위셀 (particulate / 박막 / am_perc=0) — 전체 cell과 직접 비교 부적합" is never rendered in the What-if ranking.
findings.proposed_action: Copy `is_unit_cell` (and `rve_area_um2`/`base_case` if the badge ever needs them) into the override map, or fall back to `tr.dataset.unitCell` when the override lacks the field.

findings.claim: The entry page re-orders the whole corpus with the analytic carbon what-if that the rest of the app has already retired, and presents it as a ranking with no "indicative only" label — while the model's own author comment says it is a back-of-the-envelope that a real run must replace.
findings.evidence: index.html:90-96 — `🧪` … `title="ON이면 랭킹이 carbon-additive 시나리오로 재계산됩니다"`. The model: grade_engine.py:1594-1596 — "This is a back-of-the-envelope: full simulation requires placing a secondary phase in the DEM and re-solving. Useful only as an indicative direction." CONTRADICTED BY the same app's case view, single.html:1008-1009 — "(recalcAdditives removed — this panel is recipe-zip-only; σ/porosity analysis lives in the MPM viewer after the GPU run. The analytic /whatif-additives route is kept server-side but no longer called here.)", and by the fact that the literature-anchored successor `whatif_additives` (app.py:3830-3866) exists and is not used by the ranking.
findings.proposed_action: Either drop the carbon toggle from the ranking or put the grade_engine caveat verbatim in the UI ("방향 지시용 back-of-envelope — σ 는 GPU 런에서"), and point to the MPM viewer / additive recipe kit as the real path.

findings.claim: The badge's visible text says "MPM ✓" in certificate green for a state whose own tooltip retracts the certificate, and the identical string "MPM ✓" is also used for the opposite state ("porosity 비교 불가"), so the glyph a reader scans carries the meaning the canon withdrew.
findings.evidence: index.html:130 — `{% elif case.mpm_regime == 'cross-validated' %} MPM ✓{% elif case.has_mpm %} MPM ✓`. CONTRADICTED BY the tooltip's own citation (claims.json CL-04, live: "h0·h1 둘 다 빗나갔다"), CLAUDE.md 2026-08-12 correction ("일치를 증명서로 쓰면 순환이다"), and ground-truth CL-80/CL-82 ("scaffold-run porosity must never be read as evidence of successful compaction").
findings.proposed_action: Rename the labels so the visible text carries the state, not a verdict: `MPM gap≤4 ⚠` (green→neutral) for the gate, and `MPM payload` for the payload-only case; keep the CL-04 sentence but move its first clause into the visible label.

findings.locator: L10463-10470 (/docs/full-report), reachable only by typed URL
findings.claim: A live download route hands out a report that declares the retired FORM X the final scaling law, four months after the production form was replaced.
findings.evidence: app.py:10463-10470 — `@app.route('/docs/full-report')` … `send_file(path, as_attachment=True, download_name='Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md')`, serving docs/Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md (last commit 2026-04-24), whose line 6 reads `**Final Formula**: FORM X — σ = C × σ_grain × (φ_SE - φc)^¾ × CN × √cov / √τ`, line 303 `**결론**: FORM X가 최종 확정`, line 405 `FORM X = final champion`. CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md §"Ionic-conductivity scaling-law reconciliation — RESOLVED (2026-05-27)": "**FORM X (v4++)** … is the OLDER, inferior model — kept only as a legacy toggle / predictor fallback", and by §"σ_ionic form FINALIZED — T1 production" (2026-05-28, LOOCV ≈ 0.975, 5 live params).
findings.proposed_action: Either retire the route (410 Gone with a pointer to the current form) or prepend a HISTORICAL banner to docs/Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md naming the superseding section; same check for /scaling-report and /docs/formula-catalog.

findings.claim: OUT OF ASSIGNED SCOPE (found while checking whether the nav's deep pages carry ledger pointers): the viewer still labels σ_SDCP = 250 S/cm an "anchor", the exact word CL-61 retracted; the same webapp elsewhere uses the correct label.
findings.evidence: viewer3d.js:6194 — `'전도상: AM + VGCF/SuperP + SDCP(250 S/cm 앵커).'`. CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md §CL-47/CL-61 correction: "★ **정정 2026-09-03 (CL-61)**: 옛 표기 \"σ_SDCP = 재료 앵커\" 는 **철회**. ref [35](Patil 1987 …)은 3-치환 폴리티오펜(EDOT 없음)이라 … 재료 출처가 못 된다" and by the correct label already in the same app, seminar.html:209 — "단 σ_SDCP=250 S/cm 는 측정 대기 가정이고".
findings.proposed_action: Change the viewer string to `SDCP (250 S/cm — Assumed, 저자 지정, S-PEDOT class; CL-61)`; grep the rest of webapp/static for '앵커' applied to SDCP.

findings.claim:
Multi-warning tooltips on the entry page render as one run-on string with literal `
` markers instead of line breaks, because the HTML entity is escaped a second time by Jinja — and the same app already has the correct implementation.
findings.evidence:
index.html:130 — `title="{{ case.warning_msgs | join('
') }}"` (no `|safe`). Verified render with the same autoescape settings: input ['warn A','warn B'] → `title="warn A&#10;warn B"`, i.e. the browser shows the text `warn A
warn B`. CONTRADICTED BY the identical tooltip built client-side in group.html:372 — `title="${escHtml((c.warning_msgs||[]).join('\n'))}"` — which produces real newlines. (Same defect also at group.html:51 and single.html:25.)
findings.proposed_action: Join with a real newline and let autoescape handle it: `{{ case.warning_msgs | join('\n') }}` (Jinja emits a literal LF inside the attribute, which browsers render as a line break in tooltips).

findings.claim: After using 🏆 랭킹, clicking 이름순 or 최신순 leaves the list silently filtered to graded cases only — with the rank badges still attached — so the sort button says "all cases, newest first" while rows are hidden.
findings.evidence: applyRanking hides rows: index.html:328-329 — `tbody.querySelectorAll('tr').forEach(tr => tr.style.display = 'none'); rows.forEach(tr => { tr.style.display = ''; … });`. sortCases only re-appends: index.html:214-219 — `rows = [...originalRows]; … rows.forEach(r => tbody.appendChild(r));` with no `display` reset and no `clearRankBadges()`. The intent is documented by the sibling path that does reset it, index.html:389-394 — `tbody.querySelectorAll('tr').forEach(tr => { … tr.style.display = ''; })`. This is the repo's own named blind spot: CLAUDE.md 작업 규율 ⑤ "부분집합 필터로 훑으면 조용히 초록이 된다".
findings.proposed_action: Have sortCases call `clearRankBadges()` and reset `tr.style.display=''` (or set `currentFilter='all'` and delegate to filterCases) before re-ordering.

findings.claim: The tier filter classifies cases by substring of the display name, so whole campaigns that exist in the corpus (2 mAh, 3.18 mAh SDCP) and every case uploaded without a name land in an unreachable 'other' bucket with no button — the list looks complete while silently dropping them.
findings.evidence: index.html:129 — `data-tier="{% if '1mAh' in case.name %}1mAh{% elif '6mAh' in case.name %}6mAh{% elif '8mAh' in case.name %}8mAh{% elif 'particulate' in case.name %}particulate{% elif case.name.startswith('input_S_') %}S{% else %}other{% endif %}"`, and the tier bar (L76-87) offers only 전체/6mAh/8mAh/1mAh/particulate/S — no 'other'. Cases in the forgotten buckets are real: `grep -rho "input_2mAh[a-zA-Z0-9_]*" docs/` returns input_2mAh_a5_p00 … input_2mAh_a7_50_ps_sweep (20+ names), CLAUDE.md names `input_2mAh_real_9`, `2mAh_real_6/11`, `2mAh_real_16` and the "3.18mAh base/SBE/DBE" SDCP campaign. Unnamed uploads are guaranteed to fall through: app.py:5142 `case_id = datetime.now().strftime('%y%m%d_%H%M%S') + '_' + str(uuid.uuid4())[:6]` with app.py:5195 `'name': case_name or case_id` — exactly the ID form used throughout docs/data/dem_design_points.csv (132 rows, e.g. `260418_172642_6968ef`). CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md 작업 규율 ⑤: "이름 조각 필터가 `--dilate-z`·`--k-carbon`·`--i0-a-m2` 를 후보에서 뺐다 … ⇒ **필터를 버리고 실물을 잡는다** … ★ 교훈 한 줄 — '후보를 고르는 코드' 가 곧 사각지대다."
findings.proposed_action: Derive the tier server-side in list_cases from a real field (areal capacity parsed once, with an explicit `other` value), render one button per tier actually present, and always include an '기타(N)' button so no case can be invisible.

findings.claim: The per-row half of 전체 취소 is dead code: it looks for a link the page never renders, so individually-running cases are never cancelled even though the button reports success.
findings.evidence: index.html:657-660 — `const caseId = row.querySelector('a[href*="/results/"]')?.href?.split('/results/')[1]; if (caseId) fetch(\`/analyze-cancel/${caseId}\`, …)`. The only per-row anchor is index.html:152 — `결과 보기`; there is no `/results/` page route in app.py (only sub-resources such as `/results//figures/`, L6605). The function nonetheless reports success: index.html:668 `showToast('재분석 취소됨 — 새로고침 하세요');`.
findings.proposed_action: Use the row's own `data-case-id` (already present, index.html:122) instead of parsing an href, and only claim cancellation for cases whose /analyze-cancel call returned ok.

findings.claim: The entry page's only quality signal fails open: any exception in grading is swallowed and rendered as an em-dash, so a systematic grade_engine breakage would look like "these cases just aren't graded" with no error anywhere.
findings.evidence: app.py:580-587 — `except Exception:` → `meta['overall_score'] = None; meta['overall_grade'] = '—'; meta['overall_n_axes'] = 0; …`, surfaced by index.html:126 `data-overall-grade="{{ case.overall_grade or '—' }}"`; and app.py:3702-3703 `except Exception:` / `continue`. CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md §"살아있는 회귀 (2026-08-12 발견·수정)": "`--fibre` 로드가 UnboundLocalError 로 실패하고 `except` 가 삼켜 **선분 스탬프가 조용히 꺼졌다** … `25375fa5` 에서 수정 + fail-closed + 규칙 F 로 승격" — the repo promoted exactly this pattern to a standing rule.
findings.proposed_action: Narrow the except to the expected I/O and value errors, record the exception message into `meta['grade_error']`, and render '—' with a ⚠ tooltip carrying that message so a silent global failure is visible on the page.

findings.locator: L6-9 (page header) with base.html L14-15 (title + version chip) and L50 (footer)
findings.claim: The entry page still describes the product as "upload LIGGGHTS files and run DEM analysis", which has not been the whole of the app since MPM/EIS/STEP5/litdb/seminar were added, and is silent on the fact that the DEM webapp and the MPM/STEP3 kit are two separate pipelines whose results are not interchangeable.
findings.evidence:
index.html:7-8 — `

Dashboard

` / `

surviving_p0p1.corrected: /porosity-corpus.csv (webapp/app.py:7868-7998), linked from the entry page (index.html:69-70), is a surface that commit 470c8c2d4's caveat policy missed. surviving_p0p1.locator: L548-587 (list_cases grade block) vs L729-818 (_build_dynamic_corpus_rows / _grade_engine_result), consumed by index.html L125-127 and L256-302
surviving_p0p1.claim: The score and grade a visitor sees in the dashboard ranking are computed against a different corpus than the score and grade shown when they open that same case, so the entry page's ordering does not match the case pages it links to.
surviving_p0p1.evidence: list_cases (app.py:569-575) hard-codes the static baseline: `corpus_csv = os.path.join(..., 'docs', 'data', 'se_diagnostics_82.csv')` … `build_overall_grade(_inject_input_params(m, results_dir), corpus_csv, se_aux, case_id=case_id)`, and index.html:125-127 renders that as `data-overall-score` / `data-overall-grade`. The case page goes through app.py:5824 `build_overall_grade_table(metrics, results_dir)` → `_grade_engine_result` (app.py:794) `corpus_rows = _build_dynamic_corpus_rows(static_csv)` → `build_overall_grade(..., corpus_rows=corpus_rows)`. The dynamic path's own docstring (app.py:733-738) states the point: "Corpus for percentile-ranked grade axes = static baseline … ∪ every live case's SE-diagnostics … This makes corpus-relative grades reflect the growing dataset" — the entry page opts out of exactly that.
surviving_p0p1.proposed_action: Route list_cases through `_grade_engine_result` (or pass `corpus_rows=_build_dynamic_corpus_rows(...)`) so the dashboard, /api/all-grades and /single all grade against one corpus; until then, label the dashboard badge "static-82 corpus" so the mismatch is visible.
surviving_p0p1.corrected: Correct in substance; two details are wrong, and both make the defect worse rather than better. (1) The dashboard corpus is not "static-82" — docs/data/se_diagnostics_82.csv is an untracked generated artifact (produced by scripts/extract_se_network_diagnostics.py:432; `git ls-files | grep -c se_diagnostics_82` returns 0) and is absent from the repo, and app.py:571-572 nulls the path when it is missing. So on a fresh checkout list_cases grades against an EMPTY corpus, dropping all three corpus-relative axes (weights 1.2+1.2+0.7) out of the composite, while the case page still scores them off the live-case corpus. The proposed mitigation label "static-82 corpus" would therefore itself be inaccurate in that state; the label must reflect whichever corpus actually loaded. (2) The mismatch has three sites, not two: /api/all-grades (app.py:3652-3655), which supplies the ranking overrides for the carbon What-if toggle, is also on the static path, and its se_aux dict (app.py:3679-3684) additionally omits bn_median_norm, so the 백본 두께 axis silently drops out of the ranking whenever the toggle is on — a divergence from both list_cases (560-566) and _grade_engine_result (805-811). The fix should route all three call sites through _grade_engine_result / a shared corpus_rows builder with an identical se_aux payload.

refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:

(1) NOT RETIRED. /case/<id>/whatif-carbon is live at app.py:3778-3810 and still calls whatif_carbon_additive. The case view itself still builds a full "What-if 도전재 carbon black" panel (single.html:2693-2800), fetches that route at single.html:2761, and offers its own ON toggle that recalculates that case's entire grade table. grade_engine.py carries no deprecation marker on the function (grep deprecat|retired|supersed|legacy → zero hits). The ranking is therefore consistent with the case view, not stale relative to it.

(2) WRONG CONTRADICTING SOURCE. single.html:1008-1009 retires `recalcAdditives` and the `/whatif-additives` route — a DIFFERENT function (whatif_additives, grade_engine.py:1665) on a DIFFERENT panel (the VGCF/SuperP/PTFE additive recipe-zip panel). It says nothing about /whatif-carbon. The auditor conflated the two routes because both contain "whatif".

(3) SUCCESSION INVERTED. whatif_additives is not a "literature-anchored successor" the ranking should be using: it is the estimator the UI removed (replaced by recipe-zip → GPU MPM run), and it is itself labelled "PURE ANALYTIC (no sim) — a full MPM-additive run on the GPU is the cross-check" with `_SIGMA_C_MSCM = 1000.0  # ⚠§F1 ANALYTIC what-if hook (NOT measured)`. summary: The single-case dashboard is a nine-panel page (page-header badge strip + warning banner + trust card; 분석 요약 tabs 입자정보/접촉요약/배위수/네트워크지표/취성파괴/종합등급 with ~90 hover tooltips and a What-if carbon panel; Figures; 3D 전극 구조; MPM 파이프라인 with the additive+operating-condition kit builder, GPU command cards and the MPM 결과 파라미터 table; 2D 대표 미세구조; image modal). Its DEM half is healthy: the Phase-1 frozen triad (σ_ionic/σ_e/σ_thermal), Stage-E gates, Auerbach fracture, trust card and warning rules all match canon, and `check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` passes clean — the template contains zero machine-registered banned literals. Its problem is chronological. `single.html` last changed **2026-08-07**, six days before the 2026-08-13 SR-01 retraction cascade and a month before CL-61/CL-72/CL-80/CL-81/CL-82/CL-86; every sibling in the chain has moved past it (viewer3d.js 09-01 now carries inline `CL-24` retraction banners, mpm_lab_register.py 09-07 added the STEP3 convention label, app.py 09-01). The result is a page whose MPM/STEP3 half is a museum of retracted framings that the machine ban-sweep cannot see because they are *words*, not numbers: it labels vox 0.4 µm "σ 검증값" (CL-21 says that grid is unconverged in both channels), can only emit point-stamped SDCP kits at 4.31× true volume (CL-25/CL-37), prints a green "cross-validated" badge for DEM↔MPM porosity agreement (CL-07 calls that circular), prints the target press pressure as if achieved while `settled_over_target` sits unread in the same JS object (CL-80/CL-82), attributes σ_grain to a "Cronau 2022" measurement the litdb card proves does not exist, and cites a phantom "Wang 2022" reference in a visible table column. Overall health: **structurally sound, epistemically one month stale on every axis the ledger moved in August–September.**

findings.evidence: app.py:6937-6940 `_vox = request.args.get('vox','0.4')` / `if _vox not in ('0.4','0.25','0.2'): _vox='0.4'` / `cmd += ['--step3-vox', _vox]`, and `--step3-sdcp-sphere-d` appears 0× anywhere under webapp/ (grep) although scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py:864 defines it. Contradicted by claims.json CL-25 (live) measured "SDCP 표현부피/참부피 … 4.311(vox 0.4) · 1.866(0.3) · 1.090(0.25) · 0.238(0.15)"; CL-37 (live) "구 스탬프가 SDCP 를 참부피의 0.986배로 그린다 (점 스탬프는 0.238배)"; and CLAUDE.md SR-01 §다음 ① "게이트가 `d/vox ≥ 2` 라 Ø0.30 SDCP 는 **vox ≤ 0.15** 에서만 구 스탬프가 허용된다" — so at every value this UI offers, SDCP is drawn at 1.09×–4.31× its true volume and the sphere path is geometrically impossible.
findings.proposed_action: Add 0.15 to the whitelist; when `sdcp > 0` pass `--step3-sdcp-sphere-d 0.30` automatically (and refuse, or loudly banner, an SDCP kit at vox ≥ 0.2 with the represented-volume multiplier for that grid printed in the UI).

findings.locator: line 2386-2389, 2406, 2576 (Stage-E SE-size-factor tooltips and the paper-label alias)
findings.claim: The dashboard attributes σ_grain = 3.0 mS/cm and the SE-size correction to 'Cronau 2022' as measured LPSCl grain-size-dependent conductivity; that paper measured neither LPSCl, nor a single crystal, nor any size dependence, and the year is wrong.
findings.evidence: single.html:2386 `title: 'σ_ionic — SE size factor (Cronau 2022)'`, :2388 "LPSCl (Cronau 2022) 의 *grain-size-dependent ionic conductivity* **측정값 기반**", :2406 "intrinsic σ_grain = 3.0 mS/cm @ T_ref 25 °C (Cronau 문헌 상수)", :2576 alias 'σ_ionic correction — SE-size factor (Cronau 2022)'. Contradicted by docs/lit_cronau2021_stack_pressure_ionic_conductivity.md §0(A): "3.0 mS/cm 이 본문/그림/표에 직접 나오는가? ✗ 아니오 … single-crystal Li₆PS₅Cl 을 측정했는가? ✗ 아니오 … 측정한 argyrodite는 **Li₆PS₅Br (Br!)** … 연도 'Cronau 2022' 가 맞는가? ✗ 틀림", and §0(B) "본 논문은 **입자 반경(particle radius) r 의 함수로 σ 를 측정하지 않았다**". The card supplies a verbatim replacement string, and docs/digest_model_application_backlog.md:50 books the fix as done — but only for "bib @Cronau2022→@Cronau2021 … main.tex 인용 전부 재배선", never the webapp.
findings.proposed_action: Paste the litdb card's prescribed re-attribution into all four strings: 'σ_grain = 3.0 mS/cm — LPSCl grain-interior 프로젝트 채택값. 근거: Cronau 2021 (µC-Li₆PS₅Br 고압 plateau ~2.0–2.4 mS/cm) + cold-press/소결 LPSCl 문헌 1–6 mS/cm 종합. ⚠ single-crystal LPSCl 직접측정 아님', and rename the size factor to a crystallinity-class extrapolation. Same edit is needed in scripts/se_material.py:78-82 and webapp/templates/group.html:1295.

findings.locator: line 683-684 — the green branch of the MPM↔DEM regime badge in `fillMpmTable`
findings.claim: The page certifies a DEM↔MPM porosity agreement within 4 %p as 'cross-validated' and instructs the user to use the MPM value; the ledger holds that this agreement is arithmetically forced and therefore circular.
findings.evidence: single.html:683-684 `_txt = \`🟢 cross-validated — DEM ${_dp.toFixed(1)}%와 일치 (|gap| ${Math.abs(_gap).toFixed(1)} ≤ 4) → MPM ${_mp.toFixed(1)}% 사용.\`;`. Contradicted by claims.json CL-07 (status live, 2026-08-12): claim "DEM↔MPM porosity 일치는 정당성 증거가 아니다 (순환)", asserted "플래튼을 DEM 높이에 두면 ε_sphere 는 산술적으로 DEM porosity 를 돌려준다", bridge "반례가 P:S 1차 런 자신이다 — 운동학 정지 확정인데 |gap| ≤ 0.7 %p", verdict "h1 채택. ⇒ 증명서 역할을 판별력 있는 검사로 이전: 갭-예측 정지 프레임 · 정착 wallP vs target · 속도 사다리 수렴"; and CDX-16 (rejected) verdict "REJECT independent cross-validation label; retain same-geometry consistency only."
findings.proposed_action: Rename the green state to '≈ 같은 값 (기대됨 — 순환, CL-07)' and replace the certificate wording with the three discriminating checks CL-07 names (gap-predicted stop frame, settled wallP vs target, sub-step ladder convergence), all three of which are already in the payload.

findings.locator: line 665-668 — the single-stage branch of the `#mpm-prov-badge` pressure line
findings.claim: For every ordinary (non-restart) MPM run the badge prints the requested target as the pressure the bed is at, while the payload it is reading carries a field whose own author's comment forbids exactly that reading — and the page never displays that field.
findings.evidence: single.html:666-667 `\`🗜 ${(gp * 1000).toFixed(0)} MPa = 제작압(압밀) 1단 · protocol ${m.protocol || '?'}\`` where `gp = +m.target_GPa`. Grep confirms `settled_over_target`, `stop_mode`, `quasistatic_violation`, `descend_probe_route` and `platen_mach_V_over_cP` appear 0× in all of webapp/ — yet scripts/mpm3d_compaction.py writes all of them into the same `mpm_metrics` dict the badge reads, with :3414 stating "settled_over_target 은 최종 정착 응력 / 목표 — 1 근처가 아니면 '목표 압력 상태' 라고 부르면 안 된다 (실측: 옛 경로 real_14 = 0.021, P:S 킷 = 0.009~0.049)". Contradicted further by claims.json CL-80 (live) "두 런 다 목표 압력에 도달하지 못했고 … 플래튼이 목표 응력이 아니라 **운동학적으로** 멈춘다" and CL-82 (live) "scaffold `hold` 런에서 `settled_over_target` 은 침대를 재는 양이 **아니다**".
findings.proposed_action: Print `settled_over_target` next to the target on the same line ('요청 300 MPa · 정착 도달 s/t = 0.02 = 운동학적 정지'), render `quasistatic_note` verbatim when present, and show `stop_mode` / `descend_probe_route` so a 'legacy_moving' or 'extrapolated' stop is visible rather than inferred.

findings.locator: line 22 — the E_SE badge title in the page header
findings.claim: The E_SE badge credits the 24 GPa bulk value to Wang 2020 and describes the 18× softening as a physical fact about pellet stiffness; canon assigns 24 GPa to Sakuda 2013 and forbids treating the softening as a measured material property.
findings.evidence: single.html:22 title="… 괄호 안 24 GPa는 LPSCl 단결정 벌크 문헌값(**Wang 2020**) — 참고 상수. cold-press pellet의 grain boundary + 잔존 porosity로 실효 강성이 벌크의 ~5.6%까지 떨어진 **물리적 사실**을 반영." Contradicted by docs/stage2_model_audit_vs_literature.md:203-205 "★ **Tier-2 Sakuda 2013 — E_SE=24 origin 확정** … E_eff 1.35/1.53 = **측정값의 18× softening**(자유파라미터 아님, frame[2])", by scripts/build_literature_reference.py:16 which assigns 'Wang 2020 JPS 470, 228413 — NCM hardness measurement' (E_AM = 140 GPa, not E_SE), and by claims.json CL-53 (live) "⛔ 쓸 수 없는 것: '우리 1.35 가 실측 2.19 와 일치/검증됐다' … '일치'·'검증'·'교차검증' 금지".
findings.proposed_action: Change the citation to Sakuda 2013 and restate the softening as frame[2] lumping (missing granular rearrangement / GB sliding / micro-fracture folded into an effective modulus), not as a measured pellet stiffness.

findings.locator: line 1790 vs line 2388 — τ_Lap_eff formula string vs the Stage-E tooltip

refuted_p0p1.claim: The 2D microstructure auto-tune reports achieved-vs-target coverage without the label the ledger mandates for exactly this code path.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
REFUTED — the auditor's quotes are accurate, but "exactly this code path" is wrong: CDX-25 cites a function the 자동보정 button never reaches.

1) CDX-25's location is scripts/extract_2d_microstructure.py:484-501, which lies inside `slice_microstructure` (AST: lines 295-539) — the real-DEM-slice extractor. Its h1 ("uncovered pixels are promoted until the supplied 3D target count is reached") describes the `target_coverage_frac` promotion block that exists ONLY there (lines 489-501: `n_promote = n_target - am_covered.sum()` → `am_covered[uy[sel], ux[sel]] = True`).

2) The 자동보정 button follows a different chain: single.html `load2DAuto()` → app.py:9138 `/2d-auto.png` → `_synth_2d_auto` (9108) → `ex2d.synthesize_calibrated` (1031) → `synthesize_microstructure` (542-1015). That function's coverage block (~930-953) carries the explicit comment "AM-SE coverage — GEOMETRIC: ... **No pinning; the value falls out of the actual adjacency.**" There is no promotion code in it; its `target_coverage_frac` (line 594) is annotated "combined (reporting)" and feeds only the reported target field (1002-1003). The covP/covS the report prints come from `_phase_cov` (950-953) = honest perimeter-adjacency measurement.

3) `slice_microstructure` has NO webapp caller at all — repo-wide callers are scripts/export_comsol_2d.py:733 and extract_2d_microstructure.py's own CLI main (1351). webapp/app.py never imports or calls it; the other 2D button (`load2DViewer` → `_synth_2d`) also uses `synthesize_adaptive`. So the pinned/promoted path is unreachable from single.html.

4) Internal proof the numbers are not pinned: synthesize_calibrated computes nonzero residuals ep/es = target − achieved (1052-1053), breaks only if |ep|,|es| ≤ cov_tol (1060), and nudges generator knobs off_p/off_s by ep/220 (1065-1066). If pixels were promoted to the target count, ep/es would be identically ~0 and the whole loop would be dead code.

5) No mandate exists mechanically for this string: claims.json `quotation_ban` (22 entries) contains no coverage/2D/CDX-25 entry, so `--ban-sweep` imposes nothing here; check_review_findings.py has no "rejected"-status enforcement tying a label to a source location. CDX-25's "label it target-conditioned rendering" is a verdict on a scientific claim at the slice path, not an enforced UI-string requirement.

6) The proposed remediation would actively inject a FALSE statement into the UI — "3D coverage 를 목표로 픽셀을 승격시킨 결과" — for a path whose code says the opposite ("No pinning").

Residual (does not rescue the finding): the auto loop does fit generator knobs toward the 3D coverage and keeps the best-scoring iteration, so "achieved → target" agreement is a fit outcome, not an independent prediction. That is a different and much weaker concern (parameter tuning, not pixel promotion), it is not what CDX-25 as written covers, and it would rate P3 at most.

summary: The group comparison view is a large, well-built comparison surface — 36 table columns, 48 selectable plots, a free parameter picker, a Markdown report and a Fitting Report — whose *machinery* is broadly current but whose *labels* are 3-15 months behind the science they describe. group.html last changed 2026-08-07 and generate_comparison_plots.py's registry text 2026-07-28, so every form revision since spring 2026 is un-propagated: the σ_electronic plots are labelled \"Stage 15\"/\"Stage 21\"/\"Stage 22\" and their descriptions walk the reader through the four terms Stage 22.5 zeroes; the σ_ionic fixed-form descriptions still print the retired v29 exponents (CN^1.5, cov^0.4, φ−0.19) beside code that computes the T1 SAT-blend; the σ_thermal plots hard-stamp \"R²=0.90\" onto a figure without ever fitting it, for a power law the finalized Stage T1 screen bounded at LOOCV 0.59. No quotation_ban pattern leaks into this scope and there is no SR-01/SDCP content here at all — the risk is entirely in the transport-scaling-law layer. Four items rise to P0: (1) σ_thermal values from before and after the CL-12 fix are co-plotted with nothing in full_metrics.json to tell them apart, so a purely code-driven 5.7× AM-AM edge change reads as a material difference; (2) the σ_AM(e) input's tooltip claims to set the σ_e form's material anchor when app.py only forwards it as a y-axis ceiling, and attributes 10/5 mS/cm to a Trevisanello measurement retracted on 2026-06-30; (3) the downloadable Fitting Report repeats that retracted attribution verbatim plus the pre-fix single/poly label swap; (4) the fabricated thermal R². Below that, a cluster of P1 mislabels — most consequentially R_brug_over_full presented as \"σ_brug/σ_network (Bruggeman)\" in the plot, the grade axis and the table, exactly the quantity CL-81 elevated today to the repo's stored measure of the missing Holm-constriction term. Two mechanical defects also surfaced: the multi-group table's best-value highlighter marks the *highest* AM Vulnerable % as best (its lower-is-better set is keyed on label strings that no longer exist), and the three production Stage T1 thermal plots are both unreachable from the UI and would raise a KeyError if requested. Nothing here is unfixable; almost every finding is a text edit against a source of truth that already exists in the same repository.

findings.claim: The AI analysis prompt used by /group/report hard-codes AM_P = 6 µm and AM_S = 2 µm as facts about the compared cases, and forbids the model from questioning them, although a third of the corpus uses different sizes and the sizes are not in the table the model receives.

findings.evidence: OFFENDING (:3546): `아래는 bimodal AM (AM_P: 대립자 6μm, AM_S: 소립자 2μm) + SE (고체전해질) 복합 양극의 DEM 분석 비교 데이터입니다.` — and the `display_keys` list assembled for `data_table` (:3513-3532) contains no r_AM_P / r_AM_S / r_SE column, so the model cannot correct the premise. CONTRADICTING (docs/data/case_master.csv, value counts): `r_AM_P` = {5.0: 37, 6.0: 84} and `r_AM_S` = {2.0: 85, 2.5: 35, 3.0: 15, 4.0: 3} — 37/121 cases have r_AM_P ≠ 6 and 53/138 have r_AM_S ≠ 2. (Radius/diameter is also unstated: `_sat_g_smooth` treats these as radii with `r_cut = 3.5 µm` as the AM_S/AM_P midpoint.)
findings.proposed_action: Add r_AM_P / r_AM_S / r_SE (with an explicit "radius, µm" unit) as per-case columns in the prompt's data table and delete the hard-coded sizes from the preamble.

findings.claim: The AI analysis prompt instructs the model to rank Tortuosity as the single most important ionic metric and does not mention SE-SE coordination at all, inverting the repo's own measured ablation ordering for the production σ_ionic form.
findings.evidence: OFFENDING (:3562): `6. **핵심 지표 우선순위**: Tortuosity > SE-SE Total Area > Percolation > Porosity > AM-SE Total (ionic transport limited 시스템 기준)`. CONTRADICTING (CLAUDE.md, σ_ionic ablation, 2026-05-28): "Term-by-term ablation (`section 8` of nested_cv_sat.py) on the full base (LOOCV 0.9622) shows: CN²=−0.307, (φ_eff)^0.5=−0.134, cov^0.5=−0.033, f_p³=−0.015, C_blend(τ)=−0.0057, Cronau=−0.0043. CN² and the percolation φ term carry ~90% of the fit" — i.e. the tortuosity prefactor is the second-weakest term measured, and SE-SE CN (absent from the prompt's ranking) is by far the strongest. findings.proposed_action: Replace principle 6 with the measured ablation ordering (CN² ≫ φ_eff > cov > f_p > C(τ)) and cite it, or delete the ranking and let the model reason from the data.

findings.claim: The /group/report route pins a model identifier string in committed source, which the repo's stated convention keeps out of pushed artifacts.
findings.evidence: OFFENDING (:3588): `                model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",`. summary: The predictor page is two models bolted together, and they are in very different health. The newer half — `structure_predictor.py` + the "설계 → 구조 예측" card + the Shapley/Pareto card (2026-08-03 / 2026-08-25) — is exemplary: nested-CV verdicts, REJECT targets suppressed, `use_porosity_pct` blacklisted, porosity derived from the closure identity with a *measured* out-of-fold residual band, physical PI clipping that announces itself, extrapolation gating, 19/19 selftest passing. The older half — `predictor_engine.py`'s Stage-2 physics, essentially untouched since 2026-04-24 — is a museum of superseded forms: the σ_thermal card is a compact power law that the canon screened and explicitly rejected ("DO NOT try to simplify to compact analytic form"; power-law LOOCV ceiling 0.59 vs Ridge 0.90), the σ_electronic card is a screening-script 2-regime form using σ_AM = 50 mS/cm — the exact value the Stage 22.5 UI-separation bug fix exists to keep out of the form (LOCKED σ_S = 10 / σ_P = 5) — and the additive/PTFE numbers are cited to "Bielefeld 2023", a paper that appears nowhere else in the repository, with a C65 4 wt% value ~50× above the repo's own LPSCl+C65 anchor (Reisacher 2023, 1.36 mS/cm at 4 wt%). On the specific issues the brief named: the GPR-CV vs nested-CV comparability caveat **is** present and correctly worded, but it lives in a 4-second toast and understates the defect (the reported score is max over 6 kernels *and* the RF), while the *reverse* leak is uncaveated — the σ-triad `.975/.953/.90` sits directly beside the structure model's nested table, which is exactly the certification reading ledger claims CDX-09/10/11 reject. The "Not Trained" state is only half-fixed: the sklearn-missing guidance the route was written to return lands under key `error` while the JS reads `data.message`, so the documented deploy state shows a bare "Training failed". Separately and most consequentially, the corpus behind the good half's `n = 291` badge and its nested R² contains 34 bit-identical duplicate pairs (the same DEM case entered under both a case-ID name and an `input_*` name) and 40 rows carrying a nonphysical `d_am = 0 µm`; the nested folds are a random permutation with no grouping, so ~12 % of held-out rows have their own answer sitting in the training fold.

findings.locator: status()/predict_structure() serve docs/data/structure_model.json; badge rendered at predictor.html:1352-1358 ('n' column) and 1356 ('nested' column, bolded as the verdict basis)
findings.claim: The n = 291 badge and the nested R² that drives every USABLE/WEAK/REJECT verdict are computed on a corpus containing 34 bit-identical duplicate pairs, and the nested folds are an ungrouped random permutation — so for ~12 % of rows the held-out point's exact answer is in the training fold.
findings.evidence: Measured on docs/data/design_performance_corpus.csv: 34 groups (68 rows, 23.4 % of 291) are identical in all six design knobs AND in phi_se/phi_am/tau/cn/thickness/f_perc to full float precision, differing only in `use_source`/`has_mpm`/mpm_* columns. Example pair — `260421_192558_1d6404` vs `input_particulate_7`: phi_se 0.5544350584880933 both, cn 7.003021893308665 both, thickness 136.11700000000002 both, se_of_solid_pct 59.37 both. The mechanism is documented in scripts/rebuild_cases_from_csv.py:131 ('⚠⚠ 2026-08-25 실측 — design_performance_corpus.csv 의 name 열은 섞여 있다: MPM 이 채워진 169행은 name 이 케이스 ID 이고 나머지는 input_* 이름이다'). scripts/ml_design_structure.py:270-273 folds with `rs = np.random.default_rng(seed); order = rs.permutation(n); te = order[f::folds]` — no grouping — and load_corpus (same file) applies no dedup. The repo's other loader knows better: webapp/predictor_engine.py:334-341 comments '중복의 진짜 원인은 같은 케이스가 results/ 와 archive/ 에 둘 다 있는 것이므로 이름으로 지우는 것이 정확하다' and dedupes.
findings.proposed_action: Dedupe the corpus on the (design knobs + DEM targets) identity before training, or group the outer folds so twins never straddle a fold. Retrain and republish structure_model.json; until then, label the badge with the deduplicated count (~257) and mark the nested column 'contains duplicate rows — upward biased'.

findings.locator: lines 64-66 (header block) and 722 ('# Ionic conductivity — v12-clean v3 (FINAL, R²=0.9813)'), both blame 2026-05-27
findings.claim: The engine declares v12-clean v3 the FINAL PRODUCTION σ_ionic model and quotes n=57 metrics; the production form was replaced the next day by T1, which the dashboard actually runs, so the webapp and the dashboard return different σ_ionic for the same design — most visibly for sub-µm SE, where the webapp has no Cronau factor at all.
findings.evidence: Code: '# ═══ Ionic scaling law — v12-clean v3 (FINAL PRODUCTION MODEL, 2026-04-18) ═══ / σ_ionic = C_blend(τ) × σ_grain × √(φ−φc) × CN^(3/2) × cov^(2/5) × f_p³ / #   R²=0.9813, LOOCV=0.9791 (n=57)'. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md §'σ_ionic form FINALIZED — T1 production (2026-05-28)': 'σ = σ_grain · Cronau(r_SE) · (φ_eff)^½ · CN² · cov_Hertz^½ · f_p^3 · exp[a + b·ln τ + c·(ln τ)² + β_P2·P2 + β_F·log f_intact]' … 'FINAL production: LOOCV ≈ 0.975, 5 fit params, n=88', and by the live code scripts/generate_comparison_plots.py:4263 `SE_CN_EXP = 2.0; SE_COV_EXP = 0.5` with `_sat_baselog` applying `SE_SG * _cronau_factor(r_SE_um)`. CLAUDE.md's own Cronau table gives factor 0.33 at ≤30 nm and 0.65 at 0.1–0.3 µm, while the d_SE slider (predictor.html:137) reaches 0.3 µm — the webapp applies 1.0 there.
findings.proposed_action: Port T1 (Cronau(r_SE), φ_eff SAT-blend with frozen φc_P/φc_S/δ, CN², cov_Hertz^½, P2, f_intact) into predictor_engine, or state on the card that the webapp σ_ionic is the legacy v12 law and differs from the dashboard. Also update docs/ionic_scaling_law_experiments.md line 122, which is the stale source this comment cites.

findings.locator: line 779, `FORM X: ${(cond.sigma_ionic_formX||0).toFixed(4)} | v3: … | GPR: …`; engine key at predictor_engine.py:950
findings.claim: The conductivity card labels the primary v12/logpoly2 value 'FORM X', which the canon defines as a different and inferior legacy model kept only as a fallback — so the on-screen 'FORM X vs GPR' comparison is not comparing what it says it is.
findings.evidence: Template renders `sigma_ionic_formX`; predictor_engine.py:733-740 sets that variable from `predict_ionic_v12(...)` whenever `ionic_v12` is fitted and only falls back to the FORM X expression otherwise, then returns it at line 950 as `'sigma_ionic_formX'`. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md §'Ionic-conductivity scaling-law reconciliation': '**FORM X (v4++)** `C·σ_grain·(φ−0.185)^¾·CN·√cov/√τ` (R²≈0.96) is the OLDER, inferior model — kept only as a legacy toggle / predictor fallback', and by CLAUDE.md's own standing note 'plot titles still say "FORM X v32 / v29_FINAL" while docs/predictor say "v12-clean v3" — same model, 3 names. Unify the label to stop confusion.'
findings.proposed_action: Rename the key and the label to what is actually computed (e.g. 'physics (v12 logpoly2)'), and if the FORM X fallback fires, say so explicitly rather than reusing the same label for two different formulas.

findings.locator: lines 891-892 (`Q_theo = 200`, `rho_AM = 4.8`), and the same literal at 1044, 1136, 1411
findings.claim: Every capacity-derived number on the page (1C current, utilization curve, Performance Score ranking, energy density) uses 200 mAh/g while the repository unified on C_am = 175 mAh/g — a 14 % overstatement of the applied current.
findings.evidence: Code: `Q_theo = 200  # mAh/g` … `i_app = c_rate * Q_vol * T_cm`, and `Q_per_cm2 = 200 * 4.8 * phi_am_val * T_pred * 1e-4` (sweep_optimal), `200 * 4.8 * phi_am_v * thick_v * 1e-4 * 3.7 * util_1c / 1000` (heatmap and pareto). Contradicted by scripts/grade_engine.py:973 `return (wt_pct / 100.0) * 175   # NMC811 C_am=175 mAh/g — STEP4 x-window(|Δx|·275≈177) 정합`, :983 `rho_am, rho_se, C_am = 4.8, 2.0, 175   # 정본 밀도(additives.DENS) + STEP4 x-window 정합 C_am (감사 F4)` and :1209 `C_am   = 175    # mAh/g, NMC811 STEP4 x-window 정합 (Q_volumetric과 통일)`, and by CLAUDE.md's 2026-07-23 additive-audit entry listing '물리 3 (grade 밀도 조화평균 +13%편향 제거·4.8/2.0·C_am175 통일)' as an adopted fix.
findings.proposed_action: Import the constant from grade_engine (or se_material) rather than re-typing it, so the two paths cannot drift again. Note that the Optimal Design table is sorted by Performance Score = σ × util@1C, so the ranking itself moves with this constant.

findings.locator: lines 883-889, `j0 = 0.01e-3  # A/cm² (0.01 mA/cm², ASSB NCM/LPSCl interface)` with `# Ref: Sakuda (2017), Kato (2016)`
findings.claim: The utilization model's exchange current density is 20× below the repository's other default for the same NCM811/LPSCl interface, and its two cited references appear nowhere else in the repo.
findings.evidence: Code: `j0 = 0.01e-3  # A/cm²` = 0.1 A/m², feeding `nu_sq = a_s * j0 * F_const * T_cm**2 / (kappa_eff * R_const * T_kelvin)` — i.e. ν ∝ √j0, so the whole 'Utilization by C-rate' row and the Performance Score scale with it. Contradicted by scripts/step4_dyn.py:36: '· i0: --i0 (기본 2 A/m² = v1 훅)' — 2 A/m² vs 0.1 A/m² is a factor 20 on the same interface. A repo-wide grep for 'Sakuda (2017)' returns only this file; 'Kato (2016)' likewise has no card or doc. STEP4 additionally labels its own value a hook (unanchored, §F1), so neither side is anchored and the page presents its value without that qualifier.
findings.proposed_action: Pick one i0 convention, put it in a single shared constant with its provenance, and label the utilization row as convention-dependent (or as relative-ordering-only) until an anchor exists. Note kim2025's R_ct(T) anchor is already wired into STEP4 (step4_dyn.py:863) and is the closest thing the repo has to a real measurement.

findings.locator: lines 452-454, `PHYSICS_TARGETS = {'f_perc': lambda r: min(100, max(0, (r.get('phi_se', 0.3) - 0.15) / 0.15 * 100))}` and the print at 463
findings.claim: f_perc — an input to the ionic law's f_p³ term — is replaced by a hard-coded ramp on a third, undocumented percolation threshold (0.15), in a file that already carries two others; and the log line asserts a CV measurement that is not being made.
findings.evidence: Code: threshold 0.15 here, `PHI_C_V12 = 0.20          # percolation threshold (fixed)` at line 71, and `PHI_C = 0.185  # v2.0: optimized percolation threshold (was 0.18)` at line 594 — three thresholds for the same physical quantity in one module. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md §'σ_ionic form FINALIZED': '⚠ NEVER re-screen φc.  φc_P, φc_S, δ stay FROZEN at (0.200, 0.195, 0.040)' and 'φc_P = 0.200 (P-heavy threshold, FROZEN); φc_S = 0.195 (S-heavy threshold, FROZEN)'. The print statement `print(f"    {target:15s}: PHYSICS (GPR skipped, CV_R² was negative)")` fires unconditionally for f_perc regardless of the current corpus, and `scores[target] = -1; cv_scores[target] = -1` then propagate a sentinel −1 into the response's cv_scores dict.
findings.proposed_action: Use the measured `percolation_pct` the loader already reads (predictor_engine.py:294) instead of synthesizing f_perc, or gate it on the frozen φc. Change the log line to report the value actually observed this run rather than a historical claim.

findings.locator: load_training_data(), lines 179-343 — quality filters at 246-257; no EXCL list anywhere in webapp/ (grep for _EXCLUDED returns zero hits in webapp/)
findings.claim: The GPR corpus applies none of the audit exclusions the σ_e and σ_thermal work depends on, and its porosity filter is one-sided so the documented negative-porosity broken sims pass straight through.
findings.evidence: Code: the only gates are `if not tau or tau <= 0 or tau > 8`, `if m.get('porosity', 0) > 30`, `if sigma_ion < 0.01`. A negative porosity satisfies `> 30 == False` and is kept. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md §σ_thermal T1: '⚠ DO NOT remove EXCL.  Including 23 σ_e EXCL cases drops LOOCV 0.90 → 0.58.  The same broken sims (plate_z bugs, marginal percolation, sibling-tail) that poison σ_e ALSO poison σ_thermal', and by the Round 5 list naming the exact cases: 'input_1mAh_100_6  err -41% (plate_z metadata bug → negative porosity); input_1mAh_100_8  err +1093% (WORST outlier, broken porosity); input_1mAh_100_11  err -68% (broken porosity)'. scripts/electronic_nested_cv.py:49 holds the canonical `_EXCLUDED_NAMES_EL` set; webapp/ never imports it.
findings.proposed_action: Import _EXCLUDED_NAMES_EL and _EXCLUDED_NAMES from the scripts and apply them in load_training_data, and change the porosity gate to a two-sided sanity band (e.g. 0 < porosity ≤ 30) so negative-porosity rows are rejected rather than silently trained on.

findings.claim: The sklearn-missing guidance the train route was written to return never reaches the user — the route puts it under `error` and the JS reads `message` — so the documented permanent-deploy state shows a bare 'Training failed'. This is the 'Not Trained' issue only half-fixed.
findings.evidence: Template: `} else { showToast(data.message || 'Training failed'); }`. The route (webapp/app.py:10571-10578) returns `jsonify({'success': False, 'error': f'학습 라이브러리 미설치 ({e}) — WSL/로컬서 pip install scikit-learn joblib 후 학습'})` for ImportError and `{'success': False, 'error': f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'}` for everything else; the only path that sets `message` is predictor_engine.train_models line 372 ('Not enough training data'). The route's own docstring states the intent: 'sklearn 부재(클라우드) 시 raw 500 대신 JSON 안내'. structure_predictor.py's module docstring records why this matters: '배포 호스트엔 없어서 예측기 페이지가 영구 "Not Trained" 였다.'
findings.proposed_action: Read `data.error || data.message || 'Training failed'`. Consider also short-circuiting the button when the server already knows sklearn is absent, so the user sees the WSL instruction without a round trip.

findings.locator: lines 134-135 and 191-192 ('스케일링법칙(LOOCV .975/.953/.90) 소관'), surfaced at predictor.html:77
findings.claim: The σ-triad LOOCV numbers are printed as a bare authority directly beneath the structure model's nested-CV table, which is the cross-scale certification reading the ledger explicitly rejects — the mirror image of the GPR-CV caveat that IS present elsewhere on this page.
findings.evidence: Code: `'note': ('σ 삼중항은 이 모델의 타깃이 아니다 — 스케일링법칙(LOOCV .975/.953/.90) 소관.  ML 은 그 법칙의 **입력**(구조)만 예측한다.')`, rendered two lines under the table whose caption reads '판정은 **nested** 기준'. Contradicted by docs/reviews/claims.json, CDX-11 (status `rejected`): 'REJECT the 0.9752 value as unbiased external evidence. The separately reported nested score is a different estimand; family-blocked nested selection is required.'; CDX-09: 'REJECT as external-validation evidence. Require recipe/family-blocked outer nested CV…'; CDX-10 likewise for 0.9028. CLAUDE.md further notes for the .90: 'Production reports the FINALIZED metric (n=82, 0.90)' while the current corpus gives 0.84-0.85, and the CL-12 banner adds that T1's causal narrative is not citable.

The same footnote should note that this page's own nested column is also case-level.

findings.locator: model bundle features list includes `d_am`; corpus docs/data/design_performance_corpus.csv; free knob used by shap_importance() and pareto()
findings.claim: 40 of the 291 training rows (13.7 %) carry d_am = 0 µm — a nonphysical particle diameter — in rows whose own phi_am is 0.29-0.38, and the two features derived from it fall back to sentinels; d_am is one of the six free knobs the exact-Shapley importance and the Pareto search are computed over.
findings.evidence: Measured on the corpus: 40 rows have `d_am == 0`, of which 36 have ps_frac = 0.0 (mono AM_S, so the builder took d_AM_P = 0 as d_AM). Those rows carry `d_ratio = 0.1` and `size_ratio_inv = 0.0` — the literal fallbacks. Example: `input_particulate_7` has d_am = 0 and phi_am = 0.3794366848010121 in the same row. Contradicted within the same webapp by predictor_engine.py:281 `d_am = max(d_am_p, d_am_s)`, which can never return 0 for a bed with AM, and by scripts/lhs_design_dataset.py:13 declaring '`d_am/d_se` = **직경** (ML 설계층, docs/data/design_performance_corpus.csv)'. The UI slider range is 3-12 µm, so no user query can reproduce the sentinel, but the leverage/extrapolation gate uses a hull that includes 0.
findings.proposed_action: Rebuild the corpus with d_am = max(d_AM_P, d_AM_S) as predictor_engine already does, then retrain. Until then, treat any d_am coefficient, its Shapley share and any d_am axis on the response surface as contaminated by a zero-vs-nonzero indicator.

findings.locator: line 1321-1323 `_structDesign()` comment 'predictor_engine.derive_features 와 같음 — 대립을 쓴다' with `d_am:_sv('d_am_p',5.0)`, vs line 703 `d_am: Math.max(d_am_p, d_am_s)` in getParams()
findings.claim: The two prediction panels on the same page feed different d_AM into their models whenever the small-AM slider exceeds the large-AM slider, and the comment asserting they agree is false.
findings.evidence: `getParams()` (line 700-705) sends `d_am: Math.max(d_am_p, d_am_s)`; `_structDesign()` (line 1322-1324) sends `d_am:_sv('d_am_p',5.0)` under the comment '// d_am 은 단일 피처 규약 (predictor_engine.derive_features 와 같음) — 대립을 쓴다'. The slider ranges overlap: d_am_p is `min="3" max="12"` (line 148) and d_am_s is `min="1" max="8"` (line 158), so d_AM_S > d_AM_P is reachable. predictor_engine.load_training_data:281 confirms the training convention is `max(d_am_p, d_am_s)`, which is what getParams matches and _structDesign does not.
findings.proposed_action: Make _structDesign use Math.max(d_am_p, d_am_s) so both panels query the same design point, and correct the comment. Note the existing d_AM_S tooltip (line 154) already warns the single-feature convention makes the small slider inert unless it exceeds the large one — that warning is precisely the case where the two panels now diverge.

findings.locator: generate_heatmap():1027-1032, sensitivity_analysis():1075-1080 and 1091-1096, compute_pareto():1125-1127, generate_phase_diagram():1281-1286, sweep_optimal():1387-1389 — every predict() call omits temperature/additive/ptfe
findings.claim: Five of the six analysis tools silently discard the Conductive Additive and PTFE selections (and the temperature), while the on-page disclosure names only temperature and only for Find Optimal Design — so the very 'silent no-op' the C-3 audit set out to eliminate survives on the additive axis.
findings.evidence: All five call sites pass only the six geometry knobs, e.g. sweep_optimal: `pred = predict(params['d_se'], d_am, params['am_pct'], params['ps_frac'], params['loading'], params['rve'])` — so `additive='none', ptfe=False, temperature=298` apply. The routes drop them too: app.py:10641-10643 and 10664-10666 whitelist only `['d_se','d_am','am_pct','ps_frac','loading','rve']`. The disclosure at predictor.html:216-219 says only '**Find Optimal Design** 스윕은 온도를 전혀 반영하지 않고 항상 298 K 로 계산한다', and renderOptimal (line 925-931) repeats the temperature-only warning. The page's own stated principle, at line 891-894, is '"돌아가는 척하고 같은 답을 주는" 것보다 **명시적으로 막는** 편이 정직하다'. Concretely, the Sensitivity panel prints 'Base sigma_ionic: X' (predictor.html:1010) that will disagree with the Predict card whenever an additive or PTFE is selected.
findings.proposed_action: Thread additive/ptfe/temperature through the five backends (they are three keyword arguments), or extend the existing disclosure block to name all three ignored axes and all five tools — and block rather than silently compute, as the temperature axis already does.

findings.locator: LABELS entries at lines 43-44 for 'mpm_plastic_gain_AM_P_tabor_pp' and 'mpm_dg_mean'; served through predict_structure() and rendered at predictor.html:1391-1400
findings.claim: Two MPM-derived quantities are offered as predictions with a nested-R² badge and no provenance caveat, while the runs they were measured from are the subject of an open, canonical platen defect that makes those very quantities functions of the stop frame.
findings.evidence: Code: `'mpm_plastic_gain_AM_P_tabor_pp': ('MPM 소성 피복 증분 (AM_P, Tabor)', '%p'), 'mpm_dg_mean': ('MPM 평균 소성변형', '')` — both emitted with verdict WEAK (nested 0.587 / 0.611, n=169) and no caveat field, unlike porosity_derived which does carry one. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md's ★★정정 2026-08-12 on the scaffold runs (canon docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md, ledger CL-04 still open): '속도 사다리(--sub 40/80/160, 변형 이력 동일)에서 porosity 14.38 → 12.76 → 11.08 % 로 계속 내려가고 수렴하지 않는다' and '진짜 반증 가능한 MPM 산출물은 응력-정지 두께 하나다'. Accumulated plastic strain and plastic coverage increment are read at the same stop frame those numbers walk with.
findings.proposed_action: Add a caveat string to both rows (structure_predictor already has the mechanism — see the porosity_derived caveat) pointing at docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md and CL-04, or suppress them until the platen track closes. A scientific call on whether stop-frame-dependent targets are predictable at all belongs upstream.

findings.locator: line 94-96, `chk('[C-1] predictor_engine 도 se_material 경유 유지', 're.SIGMA_GRAIN = se_material' or 'SIGMA_GRAIN = se_material.SIGMA_GRAIN_MS_CM_25C' in pe)`
findings.claim: The regression guard on predictor_engine's σ_grain single-source routing can never fail — the expression short-circuits on a non-empty string literal, so it reports PASS regardless of the file's contents.
findings.evidence: Python evaluates `'re.SIGMA_GRAIN = se_material' or (... in pe)` as the first operand, which is a truthy non-empty string; the membership test is never reached. The stray `re.` prefix shows the intended expression was `'SIGMA_GRAIN = se_material...' in pe`. This is the false-green class CLAUDE.md rule ⑤ names — '"후보를 고르는 코드" 가 곧 사각지대다' — and the file's own header claims the opposite: '검증이 찾은 3건을 각각 못 되갈게 못박는다'.
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite as `chk(..., 'SIGMA_GRAIN = se_material.SIGMA_GRAIN_MS_CM_25C' in pe)` and add a mutation check (temporarily substitute a bare 3.0 and confirm the check goes red), per the repo's own selftest-vs-repo-run distinction in scripts/check_all.sh.

findings.locator: lines 683-689 (the CV_R² caveat) with base.html:61 `showToast(msg, duration=4000)`; number produced at predictor_engine.py:560
findings.claim: The GPR CV_R² caveat the brief asked about is present and substantively correct, but it is delivered in a four-second toast and nowhere persistent, and it understates the defect: the number shown is the maximum over six kernels AND the random forest, while the label names only kernel selection.
findings.evidence: Template: `cvMsg += '\nCV_R² (커널선택 미중첩·스케일러 누수 → 낙관): ' + cvParts.join(', ')` with a JS comment correctly explaining max-of-6 and the pre-split scaler fit. Engine: `cv_scores[target] = round(max(best_cv_r2, rf_cv_r2), 3)  # best of GPR/RF` (line 560), where `best_cv_r2` is itself already the max over the six `kernel_candidates` (lines 485-506) — so the reported figure is a max over seven candidates. The scaler leak is real as described: `scaler_X.fit_transform(X)` at line 390 and `scaler_y.fit_transform(...)` at line 476 both precede `kf.split(X_scaled)`. CLAUDE.md's own wording is 'max-of-6 낙관'. Delivery channel: base.html:61 `function showToast(msg, duration=4000)`.
findings.proposed_action: Move the caveat out of the toast into a persistent line under the status bar (where 'Not Trained' already lives), and amend the wording to 'max over 6 kernels + RF, non-nested selection, standardization leak → optimistic'. Cross-reference it with the structure card's nested column so the two scales are explicitly declared non-comparable in both directions.

findings.locator: lines 794-800, the σ_thermal card rendering `${cond.sigma_thermal.toFixed(4)}` with `mS/cm`
findings.claim: σ_thermal is displayed in mS/cm next to two genuine conductivities with no note that it is a Kirchhoff-normalized surrogate scale, not a thermal conductivity in W/(m·K).
findings.evidence: Template renders σ_thermal in the same card family and the same unit as σ_ionic and σ_electronic. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md §σ_thermal Stage T1 FORM-STRUCTURE SCREEN B: 'Bruggeman 2-phase EMT (κ_EMT × residual):  baseline R² NEGATIVE (-0.15 to -1.53) — literature W/m·K κ_AM=4/κ_SE=0.7 don't map to the Kirchhoff-normalized solver mScm-equiv scale'. A reader comparing the page's σ_thermal to any literature κ would be comparing incommensurable quantities.
findings.proposed_action: Label the unit 'mS/cm-equiv (Kirchhoff-normalized; not W/m·K)' and add a one-line note pointing at the T1 section. This is cheap and independent of whether the underlying formula is fixed (see the P0 finding on the same card).

findings.locator: suggest_batch() at lines 252-269, exposed at app.py:10555-10565 as /predictor/structure/suggest — no caller anywhere in predictor.html
findings.claim: The sequential D-optimal batch suggester — the caveated, selftest-covered, sklearn-free one — has no button on the page; the only 'Next DEM Suggestion' the user can press is the GPR UCB path that requires the untrained model.
findings.evidence: grep of predictor.html for 'structure/suggest' returns nothing; the only suggestion fetch is line 1078 `fetch('/predictor/suggest')`, which routes to predictor_engine.suggest_next and returns `{'error': 'Models not trained.'}` on any host without sklearn. Meanwhile structure_predictor's selftest asserts the D-optimal path works end to end: '✓ 다음 DEM 배치 제안이 돈다 (순차 D-최적)' and '✓ ★배치 제안이 자유노브 6 개만 낸다 (그대로 시뮬 입력)' (19/19 PASS, run 2026-09-08).

findings.locator: suggest_next() docstring at line 1162 and the comment block at 1226-1228; route docstring at app.py:10706
findings.claim: The acquisition function is documented as Expected Improvement / Bayesian optimization but implemented as a fixed-κ upper confidence bound, and the best-known value it computes for EI is never used.
findings.evidence: Docstring: 'Suggest next DEM conditions using GPR uncertainty + predicted value (Expected Improvement)'; route docstring: 'Suggest next DEM conditions using Bayesian optimization'; implementation: `# Expected Improvement: EI = (pred - best) * Phi(z) + std * phi(z) / # Simplified: score = pred + 1.5 * std (upper confidence bound)` then `score = float(pred) + 1.5 * float(abs(std_raw))`. `best_sigma` is computed at lines 1207-1211 and appears only in the returned payload, never in the score. The template gets this right — predictor.html:1089 says 'Top 3 suggestions (UCB acquisition)' — so only the Python-side labels are wrong.
findings.proposed_action: Correct the two docstrings to say UCB with κ = 1.5, or implement EI using the best_sigma already computed.

findings.locator: load_bundle() lines 94-104 (caches on the JSON's mtime) vs surface():240-249 and suggest_batch():261-268 (read the CSV live)
findings.claim: The served model is cached against the coefficient JSON's mtime while two of the same module's functions read the training corpus live, so a corpus regeneration would silently produce a stale surface with fresh scatter points overlaid and no staleness signal anywhere.
findings.evidence: `load_bundle` compares only `os.path.getmtime(p)` for the JSON; `surface()` and `suggest_batch()` both do `csv_path or os.path.join(_ROOT, 'docs', 'data', 'design_performance_corpus.csv')` and read it at call time. The surface legend then presents both together as one thing: '면 = 모형 예측 (nested R² …) · 점 = 실측 코퍼스 …건(모형 아님)'. Currently benign — the only corpus commit since the model was built (2026-08-03 → 2026-09-06) is 'chore: renormalize CSV line endings to LF (content unchanged)' — so this is a latent trap rather than an active error.
findings.proposed_action: Record the corpus file hash (or row count) in structure_model.json at training time and have status() compare it against the CSV on disk, surfacing a 'model older than corpus' warning in the badge.

surface_worthy.why: This is the predictor that actually works on the deploy host and it is the best-disciplined ML code in the repo, but the page header still announces the other one. Its docstring states the division of labour that nothing user-facing says.
surface_worthy.one_line: The sklearn-free ridge path is the live predictor: verdict-gated (REJECT targets are never emitted), 90 % PI, extrapolation flags, derived porosity, 19/19 selftest green as of 2026-09-08.

surface_worthy.why: A reusable convention buried in a helper: the band is clipped to physical bounds, the clip is announced, the raw endpoints are preserved, and the point estimate is never clipped — with a mutation test proving the clip actually fires. This pattern belongs in the repo's method discipline, not just in one webapp module.
surface_worthy.one_line: _apply_bounds (lines 49-84): never silently clip a PI — a clip is itself the information that the fit is loose there, and a point estimate crossing a physical bound must stay visible.

surface_worthy.why: The right answer to 'why is my R² low' is recorded here as a measured quantity, not a hand-wave, and the gated column is blacklisted by name — but it is only reachable by reading source or hovering a caveat string.
surface_worthy.one_line: porosity is derived from ε = C − φ_SE − φ_AM with a band from the measured out-of-fold residual sd (2.98 %p) and a 17× small-difference amplification factor; use_porosity_pct is FORBIDDEN because its gate mixes two models.

surface_worthy.why: The temperature-scope block (lines 206-232) is the model of an honest 'what this knob does and does not do' disclosure — scaled / not scaled / ignored / band-not-single-value — and it is exactly the template the additive and PTFE axes still need. It is currently the only such block on the page.
surface_worthy.one_line: The temperature disclosure pattern: list what is scaled, what is not, what is silently ignored downstream, and refuse to run a sweep that would be a no-op.

surface_worthy.why: This is the caveat the brief asked about. It is correct and hard-won, but it lives in a JS comment plus a four-second toast, so in practice nobody reads it — and the reverse comparison (σ-triad LOOCV beside the nested table) has no caveat at all.
surface_worthy.one_line: The GPR CV_R² and the structure model's nested R² are not the same scale — non-nested max-over-kernels selection plus a standardization leak make the former optimistic; never put the two numbers side by side.

surface_worthy.why: The free-knob-products decision is one of the repo's cleanest measured methodology wins (nested 0.466→0.587, bias 0.178→0.032 on mpm_plastic_gain; use_porosity_pct bias 18× down), it is carried by a single JSON flag, and CLAUDE.md marks it DO-NOT-REVERT — yet the flag is invisible from the page.
surface_worthy.one_line: free_products: true — interaction terms are formed only among the six free knobs, because products of derived features are polynomial re-expression, not physics.

surface_worthy.why: A working, caveated, sklearn-free next-experiment planner that no button on the page can reach, while the button that exists calls the path that cannot run on the deploy host.
surface_worthy.one_line: suggest_batch(): sequential D-optimal DEM batch proposal that emits exactly the six free knobs, ready to paste into a simulation input — exposed at /predictor/structure/suggest with no UI.

surviving_p0p1.corrected: Substance stands; three details need correcting. (b) "~12 % of rows" understates the leak. With 10 ungrouped folds, ~90 % of the 68 twin rows (~61 rows, ~21 % of 291) have their exact twin in the training fold; 12 % corresponds to counting one row per pair (34/291). refuted_p0p1.claim: The page's σ_thermal number comes from a compact analytic power law that the repository measured, rejected, and left a standing DO-NOT against; the coefficient 286 exists nowhere else in the repo and has no recorded fit.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
All three load-bearing pillars of the claim are false on inspection.

(1) "The coefficient 286 exists nowhere else in the repo and has no recorded fit" is decisively false. The auditor's grep (`286 *`) only matches the multiplication form. The repo contains a DEDICATED derivation document, docs/thermal_conductivity_derivation.md, whose §5 is literally titled "The Prefactor C = 286: Physical Origin", stating the fit was regressed on 41 DEM cases against the Kirchhoff network solver as ground truth (R²=0.90, mean error 9.4%, 90% of cases within 20%). GB_correction_fitting_report.md §23.4 ("C = 286") and §24 give the full validation: Train R² 0.90 with 1 free param, LOOCV R² 0.86, mean |err| 9.4% (LOOCV 9.2%), 37/41 within 20%, an exponent-sensitivity table (free fit 0.758/1.987/-1.171 vs fixed 3/4, 2, -1) and a σ_ion ablation. It also appears in scripts/hybrid_predictor.py:184 as `def scaling_law_thermal(sigma_ion, phi_am, cn_se, C=286)`, in generate_comparison_plots.py:3130/3166/3984/4094 (plot registry carrying "R²=0.90 (1 free param), LOOCV R²=0.86"), webapp/app.py:8631, and two scaling-law reports. Decisively, `git blame` shows the code line and the derivation doc were added in the SAME commit 660600a44 (2026-04-24) — the coefficient shipped with its fitting record, the opposite of an orphan.

(2) "left a standing DO-NOT against" is false as of 2026-08-12. CLAUDE.md lines 1980-1981 explicitly suspend the exact line quoted: '⚠ DO-NOT 세 줄("Hertz 로 되돌리지 마라 / EXCL 빼지 마라 / compact form 시도하지 마라") 중 셋째는 보류한다'. The T1 section carries a "⚠⚠ 정정 배너 2026-08-12" (CL-12, commit 27258c77) at its head recording that run_decomposition never passed `mode=` to build_network, so it defaulted to 'ionic' and every edge got k_weight=1.0 — meaning all compact-form screens ran on an unweighted target. This is the listed failure mode: the auditor quoted banner-ed text and presented the banner-suspended DO-NOT as standing canon.

(3) "a power law the repository measured and rejected" is the wrong formula family. scripts/thermal_powerlaw_redesign.py:112 shows screen A is `feats_16 = [f[0] for f in gcp._THERMAL_T1_FEATURES]` — the same 14/16 structural features (porosity, se_se_cn, tortuosity_std, gb_density_mean, asr_ionic, am_vulnerable_pct, se_se_cn_std, electronic_active_fraction, R_brug_over_full_physics, bruggeman_fallback_fired_any, area_SE_SE_total_physics, area_AM전체_SE_total_physics, tortuosity_median, e_se_eff_gpa), merely re-expressed all-log. σ_ion is NOT among them. The 286 law is σ_ion-anchored, and the derivation doc's own ablation shows that substituting an analytic structural surrogate for σ_ion collapses R² from 0.90 to 0.17. Different inputs, different target (thermal_sigma_full_mScm_stage_e_physics at n=82 vs network solver at n=41). The 0.59 ceiling never tested this law.

Additionally the proposed remedy rests on a false premise: predictor_engine.py is a pre-simulation design→property predictor whose inputs (phi_am, cn, sigma_ionic_298) are all GPR-predicted from design knobs (webapp/predictor_engine.py:700-760). There is no full_metrics.json at that point — the T1 Ridge's 14 features are exactly the post-solver metrics the page exists to avoid needing, so "its features are all in full_metrics.json" does not apply to this page.

The code line and render site do exist as described, but every inference drawn from them is wrong.

summary: This scope is the webapp's electrochemical-characterisation surface: /eis (physics-derived Randles EIS + Tikhonov DRT + ICA + cycle-N trajectory + an experimental-EIS upload/CNLS-fit manager) and /step5 (an interactive R_int(N) fade decomposition), plus an orphaned PyBaMM DFN wrapper. The engineering is careful — both templates carry explicit §F1 honesty boxes, ASSUMED-FORM labels, retraction notes, and a dense record of prior UI defects and their fixes — but the scope has a systemic freshness problem: every one of its numeric anchors is frozen at a 2026-07/2026-08-03 state while its upstream sources moved. Three separate anchor withdrawals never propagated here. (1) eis.html's SBE/DBE/SC presets still hard-code the vox-0.4 SDCP campaign pair σ_e 1.98 → 3.00 S/cm and σ_ion 2.03e-4 → 2.15e-4 S/cm — i.e. the retracted +52 %/+5.6 % headline, whose ionic direction has since been sign-reversed (CL-24, CL-38); the page's own banner names the retraction while the presets that produce it are unlabelled, and the same numbers are fail-closed gated on /api/seminar/slides thirty lines earlier in the same file. (2) The experimental archive README withdrew the Brug C_dl anchor on 2026-08-07 ("no C_dl number") and forbade the pooled full-cell R_int mean, but the "🔬 실험앵커" toggle still fixes the model's C_dl and R_w to exactly those withdrawn quantities and the anchor box still prints the pooled mean. (3) CL-81's binding CONTACT_FREE citation rule (2026-09-08) is not honoured anywhere on the page that puts STEP3-derived σ_ion next to measured Nyquist data. step5.html is in much better shape — its numbers reconcile with docs/data/rint_eis_anchors.csv and its arithmetic checks out — with one stale button label reproducing the exact bug the comment two lines below documents as fixed. pybamm_predictor.py is a dead module untouched since 2026-04-24 that predates the repo's §F1 discipline; it contradicts the repo's own PyBaMM anchor on four counts (Bruggeman exponent, electrode area, parameter set, transference number) and silently ignores its temperature argument. Overall health: the prose is honest, the anchors are stale, and the pages have no regression test to keep them honest — unlike /seminar, which has one.
