findings.evidence: eis.html:259 `R_w=${a.r_w_ohm_cm2} Ω·cm² (Wo1_R median)`; scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:641 `'r_w_ohm_cm2': (round(st.median(rw), 1) if rw else None)`; webapp/app.py:4256-4257 `if exp_anchor.get('r_w_ohm_cm2') is not None: kw['r_w_ohm_cm2'] = exp_anchor['r_w_ohm_cm2']`, which overrides the value scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:123 labels `'ASSUMED-FORM (dU/dx·r/(F·c_max·D·a); O(1) 인자 미정 → 실험 Wo1_R 로 교체 권장)'`. Contradicted by 이종기술/eis/README.md group-A row `| **A** `260719_*_only_full` | 4 | pure small SC | ... | R_w 0.0–135.8 | rmse 2.6–**13.0** |` and the text "A reaches rmse 13 % and leaves **R_w unidentified (0.0 ↔ 135.8)**, i.e. the arc/tail split is at a local minimum, so A's R1 spread is partly a fit artifact."
findings.proposed_action: Restrict the R_w anchor to the group-B cells the README calls best-fit (rmse 1.4-3.3 %, R1 reproduced to 1.2 %), or drop it and keep the ASSUMED-FORM label; either way surface the per-cell R_w spread next to the median so an unidentified fit cannot masquerade as a measurement.

findings.locator: whole page — the R0/element card (lines 113-117, 332-355) and the Nyquist overlay (119-142, 373-421)
findings.claim: The page is the repo's main surface for putting a STEP3-derived σ_ion next to measured EIS, and it carries no CONTACT_FREE caveat anywhere, in violation of the citation rule CL-81 made binding on 2026-09-08.
findings.evidence: `grep -n "CONTACT_FREE|협착|constriction|Holm" webapp/templates/eis.html` returns nothing. The page nevertheless computes R0 from σ_ion (scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:66,84-85, surfaced at eis.html:335 `HF절편 σ_e ${...} + 이온TL ${...}`) and frames the result as a direct comparison: eis.html:10-11 "실험 EIS ... 와 **같은 회로** → **frame[4] 대조**(모델↔실측 Nyquist 겹침)", :123 "Nyquist (Z′ vs −Z″) — frame[4]", :327 "🔬 실험 ${nc}개 겹침 (Ω·cm² ASR) — physics-EIS 선과 대조". Contradicted by docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md §6 (2026-09-08, canon for CL-81): "⛔ STEP3 σ_ion **절대값**을 실험과 나란히 적을 때는 *\"접촉/GB 협착 미포함 = `CONTACT_FREE` 상한\"* 을 **함께** 적는다." and "⛔ σ_ion **상대비교**에 *\"공통모드로 상쇄된다\"* 를 **근거 없이 쓰지 않는다** — §3 의 6배 산포."
findings.proposed_action: Add the CONTACT_FREE upper-bound caveat to the element card wherever R_ion/R0 is shown and to the experimental-overlay hint, with a pointer to docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md; state the corpus multiplier range (R_brug_over_full median 4.04x Hertz / 6.69x Physics, range 2.3-13.6x) so the reader knows the gap is not common-mode.

findings.locator: DRT hover tooltip — eis.html:662-694 (drtHover) rendering the `bands` payload from /api/eis (webapp/app.py:4277); band text authored at scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:203-206
findings.claim: The DRT band map tells the user that the high-frequency grain-boundary / particle-contact band corresponds to our STEP3 CN and coverage, but the voxel STEP3 solver has no constriction or grain-boundary term at all, and CN/coverage are DEM contact-network outputs rather than STEP3 outputs.
findings.evidence: Band text served to the tooltip: "SE 입계 + 입자접촉 (고주파) … SE 입계(grain boundary) 저항 + SE–SE·AM–SE 입자 접촉 저항. 냉간압축 복합양극서 두드러짐 (접촉 품질·성형압력 의존; 우리 STEP3 CN·coverage 와 대응)." Contradicted by docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md:19,36,68 — "코드 주석이 **`CONTACT_FREE — upper bound, ideal contact limit`** 이라 부른다", "CONTACT_FREE: R_constriction = 0 → σ_cf", "⇒ **STEP3 = `CONTACT_FREE` 가지.**" — and by CLAUDE.md §5 frame[5] table, which assigns the contact network, CN and coverage to the DEM/network_conductivity side and the voxel finite-volume solve to STEP3.
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite that band's detail string to say the opposite of what it says now: that STEP3's voxel solve does not represent this band (no Holm/GB term, harmonic-mean faces), so any experimental DRT weight here is by construction absent from the model. Cite docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md.

findings.claim: The preset labelled "Kang&Shin B-NCA" reproduces neither the source's growth factor nor its absolute R_int: it encodes 50 → 125 Ω·cm² (2.5x) where the cited table reports 113.5 → 501.8 Ω·cm² (4.4x).
findings.evidence: eis.html:181 `<button class="btn btn-sm btn-secondary" data-cyc="kang">Kang&Shin B-NCA (50→125)</button>`; eis.html:746 `cyclePresets:{ kang:{r0:50,rc:125,ntot:1000}, mild:{r0:50,rc:80,ntot:1000} }`. Contradicted by docs/a10_cycle_chemomech_design.md:45 (verbatim from the paper): "| ★ B-NCA(3+10µm)/LPSCl 0.5C 100cyc | R_int 113.5→275.6→332.2→335.7→**501.8 (4.4×)**, R_w 70.7→353.4 (5×); retention 47.7% | Kang&Shin 2025 Table S2 (pdf_local, verbatim) |" and :46 "| U-NCA(3µm 단일) | R_int 56.0→84.5 (**1.5×**) |". CLAUDE.md repeats the same figures ("Kang&Shin U-NCA 1.5×/B-NCA 4.4×"). The preset's N_total (1000) also disagrees with the source's 100 cycles. The same wrong preset is propagated into docs/eis_drt_ica_cv.md:106 ("프리셋(Kang&Shin B-NCA 50→125·완만 50→80)").
findings.proposed_action: Either set the preset to the source values (r0=113.5, rc=501.8, ntot=100) or rename it so it no longer claims the source — e.g. "급성장 (50→125, 2.5×, ASSUMED)" — and add a second preset carrying the real Kang&Shin B-NCA and U-NCA anchors. Fix docs/eis_drt_ica_cv.md:106 in the same commit.

findings.locator: line 49 (DBE preset button label) vs lines 138-144 (the dbe preset object and its own correction comment)

findings.evidence: step5.html:49 `<button class="btn btn-sm btn-secondary" data-preset="dbe">DBE (R_int 18→3.8×@1000)</button>`; step5.html:138-142 `// ★ 정정 (2026-08-03): rint0 이 18(=SBE 의 pristine)로 박혀 있었다. DBE 의 pristine 은 docs/data/rint_eis_anchors.csv \`lab_dbe_pristine\` = **12** Ω·cm² 다. 성장 **배수**는 맞았지만(46/12=3.83) 절대 궤적 끝점이 18×3.8=68.4 로 나와 실측 46 대비 **+48.7 %** 틀렸다` followed by `dbe: { rint0:12, expx:3.83, ... }`. findings.locator: lines 4030-4036, the `_RETR` string in api_seminar_slides (adjacent to, not inside, the eis/step5 route block)
findings.claim: The retraction banner itself quotes the CL-33 / CL-41 sphere-stamp ratios in rounded form, which the ledger permits only inside CL-41, and the rounding is what lets it past the ban sweep.
findings.evidence: webapp/app.py:4035-4036: "현재 말할 수 있는 것은 구-스탬프 규약의 측정 서술뿐입니다 (vox 0.15/0.125/0.115 에서 비 **1.123/1.144/1.155**, 격자 수렴 미확인)." These are the rounded forms of the registered patterns 1.123191, 1.143817, 1.155448 (docs/reviews/claims.json quotation_ban entries 14, 19, 20), which are `allowed_in` only `docs/data/prereg_v2/raw_sigma.json`. CLAUDE.md SR-01 CL-41 paragraph: "⛔⛔ **세 격자(vox 0.15 · 0.125 · 0.115)의 R·이득 값은 인용 금지** — 전부 p1 plate rule 산물이다. 숫자는 원장 CL-41 (status `hold`) 에만 있다 (R5-CX-06)." `python3 scripts/check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` reports "철회값 누수 없음 ✓" because the truncated strings do not match the literal patterns and because retraction words sit within ±2 lines, so the sweep cannot see this.
findings.proposed_action: Delete the three ratios from the banner and point at claims.json CL-41 instead — the banner's job is to refuse, not to restate. Separately, consider adding rounded forms of hold-status ratios to the quotation_ban registry so truncation stops being an escape hatch.

findings.claim: The Bruggeman coefficient is set to the tortuosity, which is a category error (b is the exponent in eps^b, not tau) and double-counts the tortuosity correction because the sigma_ionic fed in is already an effective value.
findings.evidence: pybamm_predictor.py:72 `param["Positive electrode Bruggeman coefficient (electrolyte)"] = tau`, with :25 documenting the input as `sigma_ionic: effective ionic conductivity (mS/cm) from DEM/scaling law` and :76 `param["Electrolyte conductivity [S.m-1]"] = kappa_SI`. The repo's own maintained PyBaMM path does the opposite for exactly this reason — scripts/step4_pybamm_anchor.py:122-124 sets `'Positive electrode Bruggeman coefficient (electrode)': 0.0, 'Positive electrode Bruggeman coefficient (electrolyte)': 0.0, 'Separator Bruggeman coefficient (electrolyte)': 0.0` alongside `'Electrolyte conductivity [S.m-1]': a.sigma_ion_s_cm * 100.0`. The repo also defines a Bruggeman coefficient as an exponent elsewhere (scripts/generate_fitting_report.py:605-608, "φ_AM⁴ — Bruggeman / percolation power law … Bruggeman EMT의 standard 3D 분산상 exponent"). With the module's own test cases (porosity 16-18 %, tau 1.20-1.87) the extra eps^b factor suppresses the electrolyte conductivity by roughly an order of magnitude.
findings.proposed_action: Set all Bruggeman coefficients to 0.0, matching scripts/step4_pybamm_anchor.py, and add a comment saying why (sigma_ionic is already effective). If a bulk sigma is ever passed instead, take tortuosity as a separate explicit argument rather than reusing the exponent slot.

findings.claim: The comment 'PyBaMM uses 1m² electrode area by default' is false, so the theoretical-capacity denominator — and therefore every reported utilization from the DFN path — is wrong by the ratio of the real default area to 1 m².
findings.evidence: pybamm_predictor.py:106-109 `# PyBaMM uses 1m² electrode area by default` / `A_electrode = 1e4  # cm² (1 m²)` / `Q_theo_Ah = 200e-3 * 4.8 * phi_am * T_m * 100 * A_electrode / 1000`, then :114 `util = Q[-1] / Q_theo_Ah` and :121 `round(float(min(1.0, max(0.0, util))), 3)` which clamps the error out of sight. Contradicted by scripts/step4_pybamm_anchor.py:152-153, which must set the area explicitly precisely because it is not 1 m²: `pv.update({'Electrode width [m]': np.sqrt(a.area_cm2) * 1e-2, 'Electrode height [m]': np.sqrt(a.area_cm2) * 1e-2}, check_already_exists=False)`. The DFN default parameter set (pybamm_predictor.py:65 `param = model.default_parameter_values`) is a fraction of a square metre, so Q_theo is over-stated by roughly an order of magnitude and utilization is under-reported by the same factor.
findings.proposed_action: Set 'Electrode width [m]' and 'Electrode height [m]' explicitly (as the anchor script does) and derive A_electrode from them, or read the area back out of the parameter set instead of asserting 1 m². Remove the [0,1] clamp on utilization, or at least log when it fires — it currently hides exactly this class of error.

findings.locator: lines 20, 33, 44, 51 (temperature threaded but unused) and 172 (T_K hardcoded)
findings.claim: The temperature argument is accepted, documented and passed down two call levels but never used — no PyBaMM temperature parameter is set and the Newman fallback hardcodes 298 K — while a capability document cites this file's signature as part of the temperature-capable code path.
findings.evidence: pybamm_predictor.py:20 `tau=1.5, porosity=15, c_rates=None, temperature=298)`, :33 `temperature: K`, :44 passes it into `_run_pybamm_dfn(..., temperature)`, :51 accepts it in the signature — and `grep -n "temperature|T_K|298" webapp/pybamm_predictor.py` returns only those lines plus :172 `F = 96485; R = 8.314; T_K = 298`. No `param["Ambient temperature [K]"]` or equivalent is ever assigned. docs/temp_pressure_capability.md:164 lists `webapp/pybamm_predictor.py:20` among the code paths for the STEP6 predictor temperature row ("PARTIAL — 규약 통일됨"), i.e. the doc treats line 20 as evidence of wiring that does not exist. This is the SELF-15 danger class (an axis silently ignored while the run looks correct).
findings.proposed_action: Either set the temperature into the parameter set (and into the Newman fallback's T_K) or delete the argument and correct the docs/temp_pressure_capability.md citation. Do not leave an accepted-but-ignored axis.

findings.locator: step5.html:67-75 (coating select), 159-165 (params), 183-188 (coating_info render); route at webapp/app.py:3915-3921
findings.claim: Selecting a coating while leaving the chemical-growth field blank silently does nothing — the server applies the coating only when chem_x is explicitly given, and the UI shows no notice that the user's selection was dropped.
findings.evidence: webapp/app.py:3917 `if coating.lower() != 'none' and chem_x is not None:` — with chem_x parsed at :3898-3906 as None whenever the field is empty/`bare`/`auto`. The response therefore carries no `coating_info`, and step5.html:183 `if(d.coating_info){ ... }` renders nothing, so the dropdown still displays e.g. LNO while the trajectory is the uncoated one. Compounding this, step5.html:150-158 `applyPreset` never resets `s5-coat`, so a coating selected earlier persists across preset clicks; the SBE/DBE/Yun presets all set `chemx:''`, meaning the coating is dropped for every one of them. This is the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule ⑤ / ledger SELF-15 names: "unread axis env vars silently ignored produced a run that gave *correct* numbers while testing nothing".
findings.proposed_action: Return an explicit `coating_ignored` reason from /api/step5/fade when a non-none coating is requested without chem_x, and render it as a warning; reset the coating select in applyPreset (or have the coated preset set it to LNO).

findings.claim: The template still computes the thickness warning from the heuristic a server-side fix was written to replace, so the false positive that fix was meant to kill is still shown; the replacement flag the server emits is consumed nowhere.
findings.evidence: eis.html:565-566 `+ (r.filename_thickness_um!=null&&r.L_composite_um!=null&&Math.abs(r.filename_thickness_um-r.L_composite_um)<0.51 ?\`⚠\`:'')`. The server added a dedicated flag with an explicit rationale — webapp/app.py:4699-4702: `# L 이 사용자 지정인지(override JSON 에 키 존재) — ⚠경고는 '지정했을 때만' 띄워야 한다. # 기본 45 와 파일명 45um 이 우연히 같아도 경고가 뜨던 오탐 차단 (감사 L1).` / `'L_is_user_set': fn in _ovr,`. `grep -n "L_is_user_set" webapp/templates/*.html` returns nothing — the flag has no consumer anywhere in the repo.
findings.proposed_action: Gate the ⚠ on `r.L_is_user_set && Math.abs(...) < 0.51`, i.e. warn only when the user actually set L, which is what the server-side comment specifies.

findings.claim: The experimental-overlay route hard-codes the lab archive path and ignores WEBAPP_EIS_FOLDER — the override that was added on 2026-08-03 specifically because this class of hard-coding let a test destroy real measurement data.
findings.evidence: webapp/app.py:4579 `exdir = os.path.join(root, '이종기술', 'eis', 'extracted')` where `root` is the repo root. Every other EIS path goes through `_eis_archive_paths()` (app.py:4653-4661), whose docstring says: "★ WEBAPP_EIS_FOLDER 로 override 가능 (2026-08-03). 이 경로는 다른 폴더들과 달리 env 를 안 봐서 **리포 안 실제 측정 아카이브로 고정**돼 있었다 — 그 결과 이 라우트를 부르는 테스트가 WEBAPP_* 를 tmp 로 다 돌려놔도 **진짜 fits CSV·두께 override 를 덮었다** (실제로 발생: eis_fit_results.csv 12행 → 테스트 1행으로 소실)." scripts/eis_fit.py:29-33 applies the same override. api_eis_exp is read-only so it cannot corrupt data, but it will read a different archive than the rest of the page whenever the override is set.
findings.proposed_action: Replace line 4579 with `_eis_archive_paths()['extracted']`. Also reconcile the hard-coded areas at line 4589 (`area = 0.7854 if ('sym' in name) else 1.3273`) with the `area_cm2` column `_eis_exp_table()` already reads from the catalog, so there is one source of area.

findings.locator: lines 524-529 and 571 (filename interpolated into onclick/title); upload sanitation at webapp/app.py:4828, rename validation at webapp/app.py:4995
findings.claim: Uploaded filenames are interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript handlers, while the rename route enforces a strict character whitelist for the same strings — so a filename containing an apostrophe breaks that row's rename/delete buttons and permits script injection, and the two write paths disagree about what a legal name is.
findings.evidence: eis.html:524-529 `<td ... title="${r.filename}"> ... <button onclick="EIS.renameExp('${r.filename}')" ...>` and :571 `<button onclick="EIS.deleteExp('${r.filename}')" ...>`; no escaping anywhere in renderExpTable. Upload sanitation is only `webapp/app.py:4828 base = os.path.basename(raw_name).replace('\\', '_').replace('/', '_')` — path separators only. The rename route by contrast enforces `webapp/app.py:4995 if not new_stem or not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9가-힣 ._+#()\-]{1,120}', new_stem):` with the comment `# 파일명 안전성: 경로구분자·상위참조 거부 (표시용 이름이 곧 파일명이라 여기서 막는다)` — the repo already knows display names become filenames and blocks it on one path but not the other.
findings.proposed_action: Apply the same `[A-Za-z0-9가-힣 ._+#()\-]` whitelist to uploaded stems in api_eis_exp_upload (rejecting or sanitising, with a note), and escape `r.filename` in renderExpTable (use data-attributes plus a delegated listener rather than inline onclick).

findings.locator: lines 319-330 (refreshExpOverlay hint) and the /api/eis_exp note at webapp/app.py:4630-4632
findings.claim: The model-vs-experiment overlay does not tell the user that the model presets and the measured cells are different electrode compositions, which is the specific reason the archive README gives for why the σ_e gap is not yet a discrepancy.
findings.evidence: eis.html:327-328 states only `🔬 실험 ${nc}개 겹침 (Ω·cm² ASR) — physics-EIS 선과 대조 (셀 배치차 → 자릿수 대조)` and webapp/app.py:4631-4632 only `(반쪽셀 모델 vs primer-SUS 풀셀 = 배치 다름, 자릿수-대조)`. Contradicted by 이종기술/eis/README.md: "### σ_e: the STEP3 comparison set was mismatched (carbon), not a model gap — These cells are **AM:SE:VGCF:PTFE = 80:18:1:1**; the STEP3 numbers they were compared against (SBE 1.979 / DBE 3.002 mS/cm) come from the SDCP campaign beds at **70:27:3:1** — **3× the VGCF**. Carbon is a percolating additive, so 1 % vs 3 % can move σ_e by an order of magnitude on its own. The measured 0.092–0.292 mS/cm (n=9, median 0.140) is therefore **not yet a discrepancy**." The presets the page defaults to are precisely those 70:27:3:1 beds.
findings.proposed_action: Add the composition of the overlaid cells (80:18:1:1) and of the active model preset to the overlay hint, and state the README's conclusion that the two are not like-for-like. Surface the README's proposed valid test (run STEP3 at 80:18:1:1 with SC AM) as the path to a real absolute σ_e validation.

findings.claim: All three EIS API routes default to the retracted vox-0.4 SBE bed, so any caller that omits parameters — a script, a bookmarked URL, a figure download — silently gets the retracted numbers with no marker in the response.
findings.evidence: webapp/app.py:4205-4212 (and identically at 4440 and 4518): `kw = dict(sigma_e_S_cm=_f('sigma_e', 2.0, 1e-6, 1e3), sigma_ion_S_cm=_f('sigma_ion', 2e-4, 1e-9, 1e2), thickness_um=_f('thickness_um', 72.0, 1.0, 1000.0), ... porosity=_f('porosity', 8.0, 0.1, 60.0))`. These reproduce docs/sdcp_318_base_sbe_dbe_comparison.md §2-3 (SBE σ_e 1.975 S/cm, σ_ion 2.034e-4 S/cm, thickness 72.48 µm, porosity 7.87 %), under that file's DO-NOT-CITE banner and claims.json CL-24. The same defaults appear in the CLI (scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:660-663) and in the documented example docs/eis_drt_ica_cv.md:38 `python3 scripts/eis_drt_ica.py --eis --sigma-e 1.98 --sigma-ion 2.03e-4 --thickness-um 72.48 --r-int 50`. The `/api/eis_fig` route writes these into a downloadable presentation figure with no provenance stamp.
findings.proposed_action: Make sigma_e/sigma_ion required (error out rather than defaulting), or stamp every response and every rendered figure with the provenance of the σ actually used, including a retraction marker when the values match a banned bed.

findings.claim: The stated key ASSB modification 'Interface kinetics: lower j0 than liquid LIB' is never implemented in the DFN branch, and the only j0 in the file is an unanchored magic constant in the fallback.
findings.evidence: pybamm_predictor.py:6-11 lists `- Interface kinetics: lower j₀ than liquid LIB` among 'Key ASSB modifications', but `_run_pybamm_dfn` (lines 50-132) sets thickness, radius, porosity, active fraction, Bruggeman, electrolyte conductivity/diffusivity, transference number, thermodynamic factor, anode/separator thickness and current — and no exchange-current density. The Newman fallback has `:180 j0 = 0.01e-3  # A/cm², ASSB interface` and `:179 a_s = a_s_geo * 0.20  # coverage ~20%` and `:192 ohmic_factor = min(1.0, 0.3 / delta_V)` — three bare constants with no provenance. Contradicted by scripts/step4_pybamm_anchor.py:132, which does set it explicitly (`'Positive electrode exchange-current density [A.m-2]': j0`, with j0 built from the run's measured i0_ref at :110-113), and by the repo's §F1 rule that unanchored magnitudes must be labelled ASSUMED and sourced.
findings.proposed_action: Either implement the exchange-current override in the DFN branch (following the anchor script) or delete the claim from the docstring. Label j0, the 0.20 coverage factor and the 0.3 V ohmic cap as ASSUMED with a source or a sweep-only marker.

findings.locator: line 65 (model.default_parameter_values), lines 79 and 83 (electrolyte diffusivity, transference number)
findings.claim: The module builds an ASSB NCM811 cathode on PyBaMM's default parameter set — an LCO cell — where the repo's own PyBaMM path deliberately loads Chen2020 (NMC811), and it differs from that path on two parameters the anchor set for specific numerical reasons.
findings.evidence: pybamm_predictor.py:64-65 `model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()` / `param = model.default_parameter_values`, with no OCP, c_max or voltage cut-off override anywhere in the function. Contradicted by scripts/step4_pybamm_anchor.py:7 `pybamm 내장 Chen2020(NMC811) 파라미터에서 §F1-깨끗한 앵커 파일 생성` and :106 `pv = pybamm.ParameterValues('Chen2020')`, which then sets `Maximum concentration in positive electrode`, `Initial concentration`, and `Lower/Upper voltage cut-off [V]` from the run. On the two shared parameters the anchor uses `:127 'Electrolyte diffusivity [m2.s-1]': 1e-8,  # 농도분극 무력화 (t⁺=1 SSB)` and `:128 'Cation transference number': 0.9999`, whereas pybamm_predictor.py:79 uses `1e-9` while its comment claims `# High diffusivity → no concentration polarization in solid SE` (1e-9 m²/s is a typical liquid-electrolyte value, not a high one) and :83 uses `1.0` exactly.
findings.proposed_action: Load Chen2020 and set c_max, initial concentration and voltage cut-offs explicitly, matching scripts/step4_pybamm_anchor.py; align the electrolyte diffusivity and transference number with that script and reuse its comments so the reasons travel with the values.

findings.claim: The theoretical capacity uses 200 mAh/g for NCM811, but the repo standardised on 175 mAh/g in an audit specifically to remove this bias.
findings.evidence: pybamm_predictor.py:109 `Q_theo_Ah = 200e-3 * 4.8 * phi_am * T_m * 100 * A_electrode / 1000` and :189 `Q_vol = 200 * 4.8 * phi_am * 1e-3`. Contradicted by scripts/grade_engine.py:973 `return (wt_pct / 100.0) * 175   # NMC811 C_am=175 mAh/g — STEP4 x-window(|Δx|·275≈177) 정합`, :983 `rho_am, rho_se, C_am = 4.8, 2.0, 175   # 정본 밀도(additives.DENS) + STEP4 x-window 정합 C_am (감사 F4)` and :1209 `C_am   = 175    # mAh/g, NMC811 STEP4 x-window 정합 (Q_volumetric과 통일)`, and by CLAUDE.md's 2026-07-23 additive-audit entry `물리 3(**grade 밀도 조화평균 +13%편향 제거·4.8/2.0·C_am175 통일** …)`. 200 vs 175 is a 14 % over-statement of the utilization denominator.
findings.proposed_action: Use 175 mAh/g and cite scripts/grade_engine.py as the source, or import the constant rather than re-typing it. (webapp/predictor_engine.py:890-891 carries the same stale 200 and should be checked in the same pass — outside this scope.)

surface_worthy.why: This is the single most consequential live document in the scope and it lives outside docs/ where no index points at it. Written 2026-08-07, it withdraws two anchors the webapp still uses, resolves the symmetric-cell blocking question, and identifies a lab result that points against a locked scaling-law direction. Three of this audit's P0/P1 findings are contradictions against this one file.
surface_worthy.one_line: The lab EIS archive canon: withdraws the Brug C_dl anchor as out of domain (541x spread at CPE alpha ~0.3), forbids the pooled full-cell R_int mean (report A ~50 n=4 fit-limited and B ~202 n=2 separately), explains the sigma_e gap as a 3x-VGCF composition mismatch rather than a model failure, and flags one Poly cell (0.2924 vs 0.1278 mS/cm) that contradicts the locked sigma_S > sigma_P ordering.

surface_worthy.why: CL-81 canon, written the day of this audit (2026-09-08), carrying a §6 citation rule that is binding on every surface in the repo that quotes a STEP3 sigma_ion absolute — and the busiest such surface, /eis, does not know it exists. It also names the highest-value unrun experiment (voxel vs contact-network, no GPU needed).
surface_worthy.one_line: The voxel STEP3 solver sits on the branch the code itself calls CONTACT_FREE — the Holm term R = 1/(2*sigma*a) is exactly zero — the gap is already measured at 4.04x/6.69x median over n=157 (kim2025 GB-only 3.75x agrees within 8 %), it scatters 6x across the corpus so relative comparisons are not automatically common-mode safe, and it does not close as h to 0.

surface_worthy.why: Lines 4013-4050 plus webapp/test_seminar_page.py are the repo's only working answer to 'how do you stop a webapp from serving a retracted number', and they sit thirty lines from an EIS route that serves the same retracted numbers with no gate. surface_worthy.why: A rare and reusable pattern worth copying: a NOT-WIRED banner that a selftest actively defends, so the banner cannot rot into a lie. Given how much of this scope's decay is 'a fix was made in one place and the derived surface never learned about it', this is the mechanism that would have caught several of the findings above.
surface_worthy.one_line: A dead-field banner enforced by code: only get_preset and coated_chem_x are live (only cei_suppress is ever consumed), and the selftest walks the whole repo AST-free to fail if coated_rint0 / coating_effect / preset_summary ever gain a caller — so wiring a placeholder forces the banner to be updated.

surface_worthy.why: It holds the verbatim, pdf-local R_int(N) anchors that the /eis cycle-trajectory presets claim to use and do not — the fix for one of this audit's P1 findings is literally three numbers from lines 45-47 of this file, which nothing in the webapp links to.
surface_worthy.one_line: Kang&Shin 2025 verbatim cycle anchors: B-NCA R_int 113.5 -> 501.8 Ohm.cm2 (4.4x) at 100 cycles, U-NCA 56.0 -> 84.5 (1.5x), LZO-coated B-NCA 36.8 -> 102.5 — the U/B split being the branch-discrimination target for the contact-ledger model.

surface_worthy.why: Contains a real, current physics correction (2026-07-24) that exists nowhere else and is invisible from the page it governs: moving R_int from a series offset to a mid-frequency arc changed the model's HF intercept from 62 to 12 Ohm.cm2 against a measured ~10, i.e. an actual model-vs-experiment win buried in a doc while the page shows only the result.
surface_worthy.one_line: The R_int arc-vs-series correction: the experimental R_int is a mid-frequency R1||CPE1 arc, not an HF series intercept, so placing it in series produced the wrong Nyquist shape (large offset + small arc vs the measured small offset ~10 + large arc ~50); arc mode is now default and the HF intercept dropped 62 -> 12 to match.

surface_worthy.why: The one provenance-tagged anchor table behind both pages in this scope, with precision grades (pdf_verified / panel_e_approx / projected_literature) and explicit unresolved caveats per row. surviving_p0p1.corrected: Claim confirmed as stated; two details added for precision. (a) The pooled R_int is DISPLAY-ONLY — load_experimental_anchors' r_int_ohm_cm2 is never written into kw for physics_eis (only c_dl_areal_uF_cm2 and r_w_ohm_cm2 are applied, at app.py:4251-4253 and eis_drt_ica.py:699-701). So the defect is a mislabelled 'frame[4] 대표앵커' shown to the user, not a silently corrupted solve; it stays P1 because R_int is a live STEP4 input (--step4-r-int, &s4rint=) and the box explicitly invites transfer ('→ 🔬실험앵커 토글로 physics-EIS 에 적용'). (b) The n shown next to the value is wrong for R_int: eis_drt_ica.py:644 sets 'n_full': len(cdl) — the count of C_dl values, not of the R1 values averaged into r_int_ohm_cm2 — so a row with C_dl<=0 but valid R1 enters the mean without incrementing the displayed count. The fix should therefore split by electrode group (filename prefix 'only' vs '55_70um', using the filename column eis_fit.py:203 already writes), report both anchors with their own per-quantity n and the A-side fit-quality caveat, and never render a single pooled R_int.

surviving_p0p1.corrected: The R_w experimental anchor (scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:641) medians Wo1_R over ALL full cells with R_w>0, applying no group A/B filter, so it pools the group-A fits the archive README calls fit-limited ("leaves R_w unidentified (0.0 ↔ 135.8)", rmse to 13 %) with the two best-fit group-B cells. Corroborating scope: the same anchor call also sets r_int_ohm_cm2 = 100.5, precisely the pooled n=6 mean the README forbids ("report two anchors ... never the pooled mean"), so the code ignores that entire README section rather than R_w alone. Severity caveat: fits/eis_fit_results.csv is absent and untracked in this checkout, so the anchor returns None here with an explicit UI fallback; the defect activates on the user's machine once eis_fit.py regenerates fits/.

surviving_p0p1.corrected: The comment at webapp/pybamm_predictor.py:107 ("PyBaMM uses 1m² electrode area by default") IS false — DFN's default_parameter_values is Marquis2019 (base_lithium_ion_model.py:70-78), whose Electrode height 0.137 m × width 0.207 m = 0.02836 m² = 283.59 cm², so A_electrode = 1e4 cm² overstates it by 35.26×. But the auditor has the net direction and magnitude backwards: line 109 carries a SECOND, independent 1000× unit error — `200e-3` is Ah/g while the trailing `/1000` is the mAh→Ah conversion the adjacent comment's own formula ("specific_capacity(mAh/g) × ρ × φ × T(cm) × A(cm²)") calls for. refuted_p0p1.claim: The DBE preset asserts a +5.9 % ionic conductivity gain over SBE, but the sign of that ratio has been reversed by every later measurement, and the absolute value is ~2.8x low — and unlike σ_e, σ_ion feeds R0 materially (R_ion/3 ≈ 12 of ~62 Ω·cm²), so the Nyquist the page draws and overlays on measured data is wrong in shape, not just in label.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The load-bearing assertion — "the sign of that ratio has been reversed by every later measurement" — is false, and the contradicting source the auditor cites (CL-24) is itself the outdated one on that axis.

(1) SIGN NOT REVERSED. CL-59 (docs/reviews/claims.json, status `live`, 2026-08-31) is the newest σ_ion measurement and the only one run under an identifiability pre-registration. At the `PROD` arm — confirmed at docs/reviews/ion_r_sensitivity_prereg_20260831.md:79 as "현 생산 규약의 비(`0.001/0.003`)" — it measures R = σ_ion(DBE)/σ_ion(SBE) = **1.008257**, i.e. DBE ABOVE SBE, the same direction as the preset. The four-point span is 0.977497 / 0.980238 / 0.997162 / 1.008257, monotone in r and crossing 1. CL-59's verdict is h0 and states explicitly: ⛔ 쓸 수 없는 것: "σ_ion 이 증가/감소한다"(부호 미식별). The proposed action ("remove the DBE>SBE ionic ordering — it is the one quantity CL-24 shows flips sign") would encode a direction the live ledger forbids asserting.

(2) CL-24's IONIC READING IS THE STALE ONE. CL-24's own verdict carries a 2026-08-13 Codex downgrade: "이온 비 −0.92 % 를 수렴으로 부르지 않는다 … origin 앙상블(half-cell shift ×4) 없이는 판정 불가." Its vox 0.3/0.25 runs also predate the ionic defect CL-59 records as fixed ("옛 이온 결함이 해소된 상태의 측정이다" — SBE's PTFE 1 wt% was absent from the grid until PTFE_STAMP=centerline, making the two beds asymmetric on exactly this axis).

(3) THE "~2.8x LOW" DIRECTION IS ALSO UNESTABLISHED. 5.686e-4 / 2.03e-4 = 2.80 is arithmetically right, but CL-81 (status `live`, dated today 2026-09-08) places every voxel STEP3 σ_ion on the `CONTACT_FREE` branch, 4.04–6.69x above the constriction-included value (n=157, R_brug_over_full). 5.686e-4 / 4.04 = 1.41e-4 — BELOW the preset's 2.03e-4. The sign of the absolute error is not determined.

(4) "WRONG IN SHAPE" DOES NOT HOLD AS ARGUED. I ran scripts/eis_drt_ica.py physics_eis with both presets: SBE R0 = 11.9051 (R_ion_tl_dc 11.9015, R_e 0.0037, R_dc_total 70.33 Ω·cm²), DBE R0 = 11.2396 (total 69.66). So the σ_ion→R0 coupling is real and material (the auditor's "R_ion/3 ≈ 12" is right; the "~62" total is actually 70.33 for the current presets — 62.67 is the total after substituting CL-38's σ_ion). But the SBE↔DBE difference the presets draw is 0.67 Ω·cm² on a ~70 Ω·cm² arc ≈ 1 %, i.e. the two Nyquists are visually near-identical — which is exactly what the page's own banner asserts should happen ("SBE≈DBE EIS 는 정상(버그 아님)").

refuted_p0p1.claim: The retraction banner itself quotes the CL-33 / CL-41 sphere-stamp ratios in rounded form, which the ledger permits only inside CL-41, and the rounding is what lets it past the ban sweep.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The line exists as quoted (webapp/app.py:4035), but every load-bearing part of the finding fails.

1) The stated escape mechanism is factually wrong — the sweep never reads this file. `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS` (scripts/check_review_findings.py:104-124) covers CLAUDE.md, docs/**/*.md|json|docx|pptx|js, wiki, webapp/templates/*.html, webapp/static/js/*.js, scripts/seminar_deck/*.js, scripts/*.sh — no `*.py` at all. Measured: `_ban_files('.')` returns 844 files, zero of them `.py`, and `webapp/app.py` is not among them. Rounding has nothing to do with the green result.

2) Rounding is not what protects the banner even when the file IS force-scanned. I forced `ban_sweep(files=['webapp/app.py'])` → 0 problems. I then re-ran on a copy of the same six `_RETR` lines with only the retraction vocabulary scrubbed (철회/인용 금지/CL-/⛔/claims.json/CLAUDE.md) → **7 hits fire**: `+52.0 %`, `+5.6 %`, `+42.15`, `+52 %`, `+52%`, `+5.6%`, `+52.0%`. Those are all `allowed_in: []` CL-24 patterns sitting on the *same lines* as the triple the auditor flags, and they are unflagged in production for exactly the reason the auditor calls a blind spot: the documented allowance ⓒ ("그 줄 ±2 줄에 철회 표지가 있음 = 철회를 밝히고 인용", ban_sweep docstring lines 326-329) plus the file-head banner rule ⓑ. The flagged triple produces zero hits even with all exemptions stripped — it is simply not a registered pattern. So the banner passes by design, not by truncation.

3) The ledger does not confine the rounded triple to CL-41. claims.json:1395 (the CL-41 verdict) states the *prescribed citable wording*: «현재 규약에서 인용 가능한 형태는 "구 스탬프 규약에서 σ_e 비는 vox 0.15/0.125/0.115 에서 각각 1.123/1.144/1.155 이고, 격자 수렴은 확인되지 않았다" 뿐이다». CLAUDE.md:77 likewise permits «"구 스탬프 규약에서 비 = 1.123" 이라는 측정 서술로만 쓸 것». The banner reproduces that sentence near-verbatim, qualifier included ("격자 수렴 미확인"). The registry's granularity matches this deliberately: full precision (1.123191 / 1.143817 / 1.155448) and the gain-% forms (+12.3 %, +14.38, +15.54) are registered; the 3-decimal ratios are not.

4) This exact string was already adjudicated by the maintainers *after* R5-CX-06. docs/reviews/codex_review_request_r6_20260825.md (2026-08-25) sweeps every generator in the repo and tabulates: «`webapp/app.py` | 안 덮음 (`.py` 정책) | 있으나 **철회 배너 문자열 자체** (`_RETR`, fail-closed 주입기)» → «지금 실제 누수는 0 이다», with the residual `.py`-policy hole explicitly put to the reviewer. Registered as findings.json SELF-08 (P1, claimed_fixed); the banner itself is the fix for CDXIJ-9.

5) This is the "auditor read a correction banner as the error it corrects" case, in its strongest form: `_RETR` is the fail-closed refusal payload — without `?historical=1` the deck data is withheld and only this text is returned. The proposed action (delete the three ratios) would strip the very sentence the ledger designates as the sole permitted phrasing, and the proposed registry change is built on a diagnosis ("truncation is the escape hatch") that the measurement above disproves.

summary: This scope is five view templates plus two service modules, and it splits cleanly in two. The *seminar* surface is in better shape than its reputation: both checked-in .pptx decks now carry a "⛔ HISTORICAL — 인용 금지" banner as slide 1, `check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` returns zero leaks across all 844 scanned files, the .pptx download and the slides API are both fail-closed behind `?historical=1` with a machine-readable refusal that names `docs/reviews/claims.json` CL-24, and `bash scripts/check_all.sh` is fully green. But the *retraction notice itself* — the one string a /seminar visitor actually reads — was written 2026-08-20, five days before R5-CX-06 put CL-33/CL-41 on hold, and it still tells the reader that the three-grid sphere-stamp ratios are "현재 말할 수 있는 것" (what we can currently say). Worse, the slide console that would render the deck is unreachable dead code (the template never sends `?historical=1`), and inside that dead code three correction badges are keyed to slide ordinals that shifted by +1 when the banner slide was inserted on 2026-09-01 — so a green "✓ 방어 가능한 결과" badge asserting the vox-0.4 SDCP result is defensible (refuted by CL-24/CL-33 on 2026-08-13/16) would now land on the wrong slide, while the slide carrying the retracted numbers table would carry none. The *mpm_lab* surface is the more consequential half. Its 2026-09-07 convention-lifting fix is the right idea implemented with the exact anti-pattern CLAUDE.md rule ⑤ names by name: `build_meta` picks 14 manifest keys by hardcoded name, so 14 of the 26 canonical `run_contract.PROTOCOL_FIELDS` never reach the UI — including `se_source` (the SE_PROXY gate), `dilate_z` and `temp_c` (rule ⑤'s own worked examples), `sdcp_bridge_um` (CL-87's live axis) and the whole σ_ion/σ_AM table. Of the keys it *does* lift, `plate_rule` — the p1↔p2 axis under which CL-33/41/58 are quotation-banned — is never rendered at all, and the vox badge is suppressed exactly at 0.4 µm, making the retracted grid look like the unremarkable default. The ⚖ compare modal exports manuscript-grade colourbars and PNGs from two payloads with no convention-parity guard. Separately, `compute_trust` (including its "planned but no result = silent failure" detector) is computed, persisted, and never rendered anywhere; `stage_e_le_baseline_sigma_ion` is written into every full_metrics.json and read by nothing in the repo; and mpm_lab's clipboard summary — explicitly labelled "AI에 먹이기용" — emits STEP3 σ_ion as a bare absolute one day after CL-81 made the `CONTACT_FREE` upper-bound label mandatory. Finally, `webapp/*.py` is outside `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS` even though the sweep's own criterion is "사용자에게 노출되는 산출물", and `app.py` currently holds a registry-pattern string; and `storage_sync` never syncs `mpm_lab/` although `scripts/restore_webapp_data.py` restores that prefix and `.gitignore` excludes the folder — mpm_lab payloads have no backup on either path. Every finding below is invisible to the current discipline apparatus, which is green.

findings.proposed_action: Remove the `!= 0.4` exclusion and always render the vox badge; render `🔲 vox (기록 없음)` in a warning colour when `vox_um` is absent, since absence and 0.4 are currently conflated. Give vox 0.4 a distinct warning style with a tooltip naming CL-24/CL-25.

findings.locator: lines 4031-4036, `_RETR = (...)` — rendered into the page by webapp/templates/seminar.html `renderDeck()` via `esc(deckData.error)`
findings.claim: The retraction notice that the /seminar page actually shows tells the reader that the three-grid sphere-stamp ratios are what we can currently say — quoting values that were placed under a standing quotation ban five days after the notice was written.
findings.evidence: webapp/app.py:4031-4036 (git blame: commit 1da6cbdaff, 2026-08-20) — `_RETR = ('⛔ 이 덱은 2026-08-06 발표 기록이고, ... 격자를 조이면 σ_e 이득은 +42.15 → +8.49 % 로 내려가며 σ_ion 이득은 부호가 뒤집힙니다.  현재 말할 수 있는 것은 구-스탬프 규약의 측정 서술뿐입니다 (vox 0.15/0.125/0.115 에서 비 1.123/1.144/1.155, 격자 수렴 미확인). ...')`. The same sentence exists in two other files served by the same page: docs/seminar/seminar_deck.json `_RETRACTED` — "현재 말할 수 있는 것은 구-스탬프 규약의 측정 서술뿐이다 (vox 0.15 R=1.1232 · 0.125 R=1.1438, 미수렴)" — and docs/seminar_20260806_script.md:8. CONTRADICTED BY: claims.json CL-33/CL-41 `hold_reason` (2026-08-25, R5-CX-06) — "⇒ 재측정(새 p2 GPU 8팔) 전까지 **인용 금지**" — and by the quotation_ban registry itself, whose patterns `1.1232`, `1.143817`, `1.155448`, `+12.3 %` carry `allowed_in: ['docs/data/prereg_v2/raw_sigma.json']` only. The sweep does not catch these three files because each contains the word '철회' within ±2 lines (a legitimate near-line exemption for the *retracted* values `+52.0 %`/`+5.6 %`/`+42.15`) — the exemption then silently covers the *held* values in the same sentence.
findings.proposed_action: Replace the clause in all three files with a statement that carries no numbers: "현재 인용 가능한 값은 없다 — 구 스탬프 세 격자의 비는 전부 p1 plate rule 산물이라 p2 재측정 전까지 인용 금지 (CL-33 · CL-41, R5-CX-06). 값은 원장 안에만 있다." Since these are inside the same sentence as legitimately-marked retracted values, consider splitting retracted-and-quotable-with-a-marker from held-and-not-quotable onto separate lines so the near-line exemption cannot straddle both.

findings.claim: The ban sweep does not scan `webapp/*.py`, even though the sweep's own stated inclusion criterion is 'everything exposed to the user' and app.py is the module that composes and serves the seminar page's visible text; there is a live registry-pattern occurrence in it right now.
findings.evidence: `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS = ('CLAUDE.md', 'docs/**/*.md', 'wiki/**/*.md', 'webapp/templates/*.html', 'webapp/static/js/*.js', 'scripts/seminar_deck/*.js', 'docs/**/*.json', 'webapp/**/*.json', 'scripts/*.sh', 'docs/**/*.pptx', 'docs/**/*.docx', 'docs/**/*.js')`. Its own comment states the criterion: "⇒ **사용자에게 노출되는 산출물**을 전부 넣는다 (JSON 덱·러너 셸·덱 생성기). scripts/*.py 는 넣지 않는다 — 그쪽 등장은 대부분 철회를 설명하는 주석이고". Measured by executing the module's own file enumerator: `check_review_findings._ban_files('.')` returns 844 files, 17 of them under webapp/, and `any(f.endswith('webapp/app.py'))` is False — as are mpm_lab_register.py and storage_sync.py. webapp/app.py:4033 currently contains the registry pattern `+42.15` (exempted only because it is unscanned; it would also pass on the near-line rule, but that is a different question from being scanned at all). This is the same media hole the sweep already fixed twice for JSON decks (CDXIJ-4) and Office zips (CDXIJ-9): the serving layer was outside the glob.
findings.proposed_action: Add `'webapp/*.py'` to `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS`. The stated rationale for excluding `scripts/*.py` (mostly explanatory comments) does not apply: webapp/*.py contains user-facing strings, and the line-proximity marker rule already handles the genuine explanatory comments there.

findings.locator: line 268, inside `labBuildSummary()` — the '요약' button's clipboard export
findings.claim: The clipboard summary — whose button tooltip is explicitly '물성 요약을 클립보드에 복사 (AI에 먹이기용)' — emits STEP3 σ_ion as a bare absolute value with no CONTACT_FREE upper-bound label, one day after that label became a standing citation requirement.
findings.evidence: mpm_lab.html:268 — `L.push(\`STEP3 σ_e (벌크): ${s3s.sigma_e_eff_S_cm} S/cm\` + (s3s.sigma_ion_eff_S_cm != null ? \`   ·   σ_ion: ${s3s.sigma_ion_eff_S_cm} S/cm\` : ''));` (file last changed 2026-09-07). CONTRADICTED BY: CLAUDE.md CL-81 block dated 2026-09-08 — "⛔ **인용 규약**: STEP3 σ_ion **절대값**을 실험 옆에 적을 때 *\"협착 미포함 = CONTACT_FREE 상한\"* 을 함께 적는다. σ_ion 상대비교에 *\"공통모드 상쇄\"* 를 근거 없이 쓰지 않는다." and claims.json CL-81 measured — "복셀 FV (STEP3) — 없다 ... SE 셀 ↔ SE 셀 = 2·(3.0·3.0)/(3.0+3.0) = 3.0 mS/cm ⇒ 계면 항 **정확히 0**", with the magnitude already stored: `R_brug_over_full` Hertz median 4.04×, Physics median 6.69×, range 2.26–13.61 over n=157 — i.e. the multiplier scatters 6× across the corpus, so "⚠⚠ **상대비교도 자동으로 안전하지 않다**". Because this text is built for pasting into an LLM, the caveat is exactly the part that must travel with the number.
findings.proposed_action: Append the mandated label to the σ_ion line, e.g. `σ_ion: <v> S/cm  ⚠ 협착·계면 저항 미포함 = CONTACT_FREE 상한 (CL-81; 코퍼스 배수 중앙값 4.04×/6.69×, 범위 2.3–13.6×)`. Apply the same to `σ_apparent` if it is derived from the ionic channel, and add the note that relative σ_ion comparisons are not automatically common-mode safe.

findings.claim: The convergence/silent-failure badge set is computed on every registration and persisted into meta.json, and no template renders it — so `⚠UNCONVERGED` arms, channels that were planned but produced no result, and the porosity sentinel never reach the screen the user actually compares payloads on.
findings.evidence: The module docstring states the intent: "등록 시 `trust`(수렴/미수렴 배지)도 payload 가 이미 기록한 실제 잔차/UNCONVERGED 마커에서 계산해 임베드 → '각 값의 수렴을 db 에서 읽어 자동 배지'(파이프라인 ④)의 데이터-측을 등록 훅이 함께 채움." `build_meta` returns it, and webapp/app.py:7219 `return render_template('mpm_lab.html', items=_mpm_lab_list())` passes each meta.json wholesale into the template. `grep -n 'trust' webapp/templates/mpm_lab.html` returns zero hits; a repo-wide grep of templates/JS finds `trust` only in audit.html and single.html, both of which refer to the unrelated Stage-E `_build_trust_card`. So the three checks the module was written to surface are all invisible: the 1e-6 residual threshold added as "★F1(리뷰) ... false-green 방어", the `component_plan` branch that emits `'detail': '계획됐는데 결과가 없다 (조용한 실패 의심)'`, and the `por <= 0 or por >= 60` sentinel. Non-converged arms demonstrably occur: CLAUDE.md prereg v3 STEP 3 records "**STEP 3 = HOLD** — DBE 팔 **미수렴**(cg_info=30000, resid 2.2e-08)", and findings.json SR-03 is open on the solver.
findings.proposed_action: Add a trust column to the mpm_lab table rendering `it.trust.overall` as a chip (ok/warn/na) with the per-badge `label`/`detail` in the tooltip, and mirror it into the JS `labAddRow` path so freshly uploaded rows show it too. Block or red-flag ⚖ compare when either side is `warn`.

findings.locator: module docstring line 3 and `restore_all(upload_dir, results_dir, archive_dir)` lines 356-391
findings.claim: The mpm_lab folder is never synced to Supabase and is gitignored, so registered MPM payloads have no backup on either path — while the documented recovery script already expects an `mpm_lab` remote prefix that nothing ever writes.
findings.evidence: storage_sync.py:3 — "Keeps uploads/, results/, archive/ synced with Supabase Storage so data persists across Render redeploys"; `restore_all` takes exactly three directories. `grep -n 'storage_sync' webapp/app.py` shows sync calls only for `uploads/{case_id}`, `results/{case_id}` and `archive/{rel}` (lines 5208, 5334-5335, 9343, 9366-9367, 9476, 9479, 9553); `MPM_LAB_FOLDER` (app.py:318) never appears in any storage_sync call. CONTRADICTED BY: scripts/restore_webapp_data.py:35 — `FOLDERS = ('results', 'uploads', 'archive', 'mpm_lab')` with the comment "#: 웹앱이 쓰는 네 폴더 — 원격 prefix 는 `storage_sync` 가 업로드할 때 쓰는 것과 같아야 한다", i.e. the restore side asserts a symmetry that does not exist. There is no git copy either: `.gitignore:8` `webapp/mpm_lab/`, and `git ls-files webapp/mpm_lab` returns nothing. Meanwhile mpm_lab_register.py:17-18 advertises exactly the ephemeral-disk topology this breaks: "--url URL 실행중 webapp 의 /mpm-lab/upload 로 HTTP push (Render 등 원격 호스트)".
findings.proposed_action: Call `storage_sync.sync_dir_to_remote(d, f'mpm_lab/{pid}')` from `mpm_lab_upload` (and from `register_local` when a remote is configured), add `delete_prefix(f'mpm_lab/{pid}')` to the delete route, and add the mpm_lab directory to `restore_all`'s signature and body. Until then, the recovery script's mpm_lab row should be documented as aspirational so a future restore does not silently return zero payloads and read as 'nothing was ever there'.

findings.claim: `sync_dir_to_remote` prints an attempt count as a success count — every upload can fail and the module still reports 'Synced N files' — while other functions in the same file do check and log status codes, so the file is internally inconsistent about whether failures are visible.
findings.evidence: Lines 293-300: `upload_file(remote_path, local_path)` then `count += 1` unconditionally, then `print(f"[Storage] Synced {count} files to {remote_prefix}")`. `upload_file` (112-152) ends with `except Exception as e: print(f"  Upload error {remote_path}: {e}")` and returns None in every path; `_upload_raw` (104-109) does `return False` on non-2xx but its return value is discarded at both call sites (138, 146). Contrast within the same file: `delete_path` (208-218) does `if r.status_code not in (200, 201): logger.warning(...)`, and `list_files` (252-262) does `logger.warning(f"List failed {prefix}: ...")`. Also `delete_prefix` (221-233) assigns `r = requests.delete(...)` and never inspects it — a third variant of the same inconsistency in one module.
findings.proposed_action: Have `upload_file` return a bool, count only successes, and print `Synced {ok}/{attempted}` with a non-zero-exit or explicit warning when `ok < attempted`. Check the `delete_prefix` response the way `delete_path` does.

findings.claim: Startup restore is gated on the `uploads` prefix alone, so results/ and archive/ are never restored when remote uploads is empty, and any single local file under uploads/ disables restore of all three folders.
findings.evidence: Lines 365-366: `has_local = os.path.isdir(upload_dir) and len(os.listdir(upload_dir)) > 0` and `has_remote = _remote_has_data('uploads')`; the restore branch at 379-385 is `elif not has_local and has_remote:` and only then pulls `results` and `archive`. There is no per-folder decision. This is the same class of gap that produced scripts/restore_webapp_data.py, whose header says "`webapp/storage_sync.py` 에 `sync_remote_to_dir` 이 이미 있었는데 **부르는 자리가 없었다** (업로드 방향만 웹앱이 자동으로 쓴다)" — and that script deliberately restores per folder with `--only` and a `--force` overwrite guard, i.e. its design contradicts the all-or-nothing gate here.
findings.proposed_action: Decide per folder: for each of uploads/results/archive (and mpm_lab, per the previous finding) compare local emptiness against that folder's own remote prefix, and log the decision per folder so a skipped restore is visible rather than silent.

findings.locator: lines 12-17 (header prose) and the gate table header row, lines 68-76
findings.claim: The Trust Audit's 'σ ≤ baseline' column is the electronic channel only. The ionic and thermal baseline invariants are computed and written into every full_metrics.json and are read by nothing in the repo, so a case that violates the ionic invariant still displays '✓ Trust'.
findings.evidence: audit.html:14-17 — "Four core gates (ASR, Frac, Solver, σ ≤ baseline) determine the per-case verdict; a fifth indicator reports whether the Bruggeman fallback fired." webapp/app.py:10220-10231 `_AUDIT_GATE_TIPS` contains `'stage_e_le_baseline_sigma_e': 'Stage-E σ_e ≤ baseline (factor-≤-1 invariant; Bruggeman bound)'` and nothing for the ionic channel. scripts/run_network_full_corrections.py:599-602 computes both — `flags['stage_e_le_baseline_sigma_ion'] = _le(sigma_ionic_e, fm.get('sigma_full_mScm'))` and `flags['stage_e_le_baseline_kappa'] = _le(sigma_th_e, fm.get('thermal_sigma_full_mScm'))` — but the verdict set at 615-620 (`gate_results = {...}`) includes only the four, and `flags['trustworthy_overall']` is computed from those four. A repo-wide grep for `stage_e_le_baseline_sigma_ion` returns exactly one hit: its own assignment. `stage_e_le_baseline_kappa` appears only in three thermal scripts, and there only as an *excluded* leak feature (thermal_push_higher.py:25, thermal_final_decision.py:95, thermal_powerlaw_redesign.py:51). scripts/audit_validation_flags.py:32-36 `GATES` mirrors the same four, so this is a shared truncation, not a webapp-only one. This asymmetry now points the wrong way: CL-81 (2026-09-08) identifies the ionic channel as the one with the newly-quantified structural deficit.
findings.proposed_action: Either add a fifth substantive gate column for the ionic invariant (and a sixth for κ), or change the header to say explicitly that the σ ≤ baseline gate is electronic-only and that the ionic/κ invariants are recorded but not gated. Do not leave a computed, persisted boolean with zero readers.

findings.locator: line 78 (and the identical JS at line 230) — `title="스탬프·σ 표·origin 위상 — 이게 다르면 같은 침대라도 비교 불가"`
findings.claim: The convention chip's tooltip promises the σ table, but the chip shows only three of the ten σ-table protocol axes — omitting, among others, the AM conductivities that enter the σ_e solve directly.
findings.evidence: The tooltip claims '스탬프·σ 표·origin 위상'. The label is built at mpm_lab_register.py:182-185 from exactly three keys: `for _k, _lab in (('sigma_vgcf_S_cm', 'σ_VGCF'), ('sigma_sdcp_S_cm', 'σ_SDCP'), ('sigma_ptfe_S_cm', 'σ_PTFE'))`. `run_contract.PROTOCOL_FIELDS` classifies ten σ-table axes as protocol: sigma_vgcf_S_cm, sigma_sdcp_S_cm, sigma_ptfe_S_cm, sigma_superp_S_cm, sigma_swcnt_S_cm, sigma_ion_se_S_cm, sigma_ion_sdcp_S_cm, sigma_am_s_S_cm, sigma_am_p_S_cm, plus `cam` and `temp_c`. scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py's own manifest comment says why the omission matters: "ⓑ `sigma_table_S_cm`(:1084)·`cam_preset`(:1092) 도 매니페스트 **밖** = 미게이트인데 σ_AM 은 σ_e 솔브에 **직접** 들어간다." A second omission in the same builder: line 178 emits a chip only when `ptfe_stamp != 'off'` and line 180 only when `sdcp_stamp == 'sphere'`, so the retracted point-stamp convention renders as no chip at all.
findings.proposed_action: Render every σ axis present in the manifest (falling back to `(기본)` when absent), and render `SDCP 점 스탬프` explicitly rather than as silence. If the chip must stay short, change the tooltip to name exactly the three σ values it shows.

findings.locator: line 159 (build_meta comment) and line 379 (the same sentence repeated in `_selftest`)
findings.claim: A code comment quantitatively cites a σ_e ratio pair whose baseline is a p1 plate-rule value under a standing quotation ban, and which the cited claim itself says cannot be quantitatively cited.
findings.evidence: mpm_lab_register.py:159 — `#    나란히 보였다.  같은 침대라도 PTFE 규약 하나로 σ_e 비가 1.12↔1.31 로 갈린다(CL-49)`, repeated verbatim at :379-380 (both written 2026-09-07). CONTRADICTED BY: claims.json CL-49 measured value `R 1.126267 → **1.309170**` together with its own citation limits — "⚠⚠ **인용 한계**: ① **arm 0 한 팔**이라 표준오차가 없다 (8팔 아님) — 비를 정량 인용하려면 8팔이 필요하다" — and by CL-33's `hold_reason`, since 1.126267 is the sphere-stamp p1 baseline: "이 값들은 전부 **p1 plate rule** ... ⇒ 재측정(새 p2 GPU 8팔) 전까지 **인용 금지**". Nothing would catch this today because webapp/*.py is outside `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS` (see the sweep-coverage finding), and `1.12`/`1.31` are three-significant-figure roundings that the registry's literal patterns do not match.
findings.proposed_action: Drop the numbers: "같은 침대라도 PTFE 규약 하나로 σ_e 비가 크게 갈린다 (CL-49 — arm 0 한 팔이라 값은 정량 인용 불가; 기준선은 p1 plate rule 이라 CL-33 인용 금지 대상)". The comment's argument (convention differences make same-bed runs incomparable) does not need a magnitude to land.

findings.locator: lines 318-320 in `labBuildSummary()` — `L.push('— 전체 mpm_metrics (raw JSON · 새 물성이 추가되면 자동 포함) —'); L.push(JSON.stringify(m, null, 2));`
findings.claim: The clipboard export raw-dumps the full mpm_metrics blob, which includes the voxel-adjacency coverage keys that canon says must never be reported and that a sibling pipeline actively blocks with a selftest.
findings.evidence: mpm_lab.html:318-320 dumps `m` in full, and the button tooltip (line 100 / 250) is '물성 요약을 클립보드에 복사 (AI에 먹이기용)'. scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py:2847-2848 writes those keys into mpm_metrics: `'coverage_AM_P_mpm_pct': round(pick(a.cov_p, 'coverage_AM_P_pct', cov['AM_P']), 1), 'coverage_AM_S_mpm_pct': ...`. CONTRADICTED BY: CLAUDE.md — "⚠ NEVER report the voxel-adjacency `coverage_AM_*_mpm_pct` (~26 %) — density/n_vox-bound, does NOT converge; it is a preview artifact" — and by scripts/design_performance_dataset.py:58 `MPM_FORBIDDEN = ('coverage_AM_P_mpm_pct', 'coverage_AM_S_mpm_pct')` with a selftest at :342 asserting "★금지 키(coverage_AM_*_mpm_pct, 복셀-인접 preview 아티팩트)가 차단된다". One pipeline enforces the ban; this export, which is built to travel into an LLM, does not. Note the curated part of the same summary is correct — line 285-290 reports Hertz/Tabor coverage properly.
findings.proposed_action: Filter `MPM_FORBIDDEN` keys out of the raw dump (or rename them in-place to `coverage_AM_P_mpm_pct__FORBIDDEN_preview_artifact`), and reuse the same constant so the block cannot drift from design_performance_dataset.py.

findings.locator: `show()` at line ~395 (`fetch('/api/seminar/slides')`) and the mode button at line 152 (`<button data-m="deck" class="on">🗂️ 슬라이드 (덱 + 대본)</button>`)
findings.claim: The entire slide console is unreachable in the served app: the template never sends `?historical=1`, and the API is fail-closed without it, so the default tab always renders a refusal box and the deck renderer, nav, tables, charts, badges, keyboard navigation and deck search are dead code.
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'historical' webapp/templates/seminar.html` returns nothing (verified). webapp/app.py:4037 — `if (request.args.get('historical') or '') != '1': return jsonify({'ok': False, 'retracted': True, 'error': _RETR, ...})`. Therefore `renderDeck()` always takes the `if (!deckData.ok)` branch at line 289, and `slideHtml`, `navHtml`, `tableHtml`, `chartHtml`, `FLAGS`, the ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handler and the deck-mode branch of `doFind()` never execute. Meanwhile the page header still promises '덱·대본·출처를 한 화면에서 — 파일이 정본이고 이 화면은 뷰어다' and the deck tab is the default (`show('deck')` on load). webapp/test_seminar_page.py check 13 only asserts the literal strings `sm-flag` and `ArrowRight` appear in the HTML, so the dead code reads as wired.
findings.proposed_action: Pick one and make it true. Either add an explicit '⛔ 이력으로 열기' toggle that appends `?historical=1` (the banner slide is now slide 1, so the retraction is the first thing shown) and fix the FLAGS keying first; or delete the dead renderer, relabel the tab, and keep only the refusal + evidence pointer. Leaving ~150 lines of unreachable rendering next to a green test that checks for its class names is how the badge drift went unnoticed.

findings.locator: the '📄 대본 원문' / '📖 용어 · 기호' / '🧭 파이프라인 가이드' mode buttons (lines 153-155) → `/api/seminar/doc/<key>` (app.py:3992)
findings.claim: The document tabs are fail-open while the deck and .pptx tabs are fail-closed; nothing but the presence of a hand-written banner inside each specific markdown file protects the doc path, so adding a document to `_SEMINAR_DOCS` serves it ungated by default.
findings.evidence: app.py:4013 (slides) and 4076 (deck) both begin `if (request.args.get('historical') or '') != '1':` and refuse. app.py:3992 `api_seminar_doc` has no such gate — it opens `_SEMINAR_DOCS[key]` and returns the text. Today the risk is mitigated by content, not by code: docs/seminar_20260806_script.md:3-11 carries a head banner ("⛔⛔ **HISTORICAL — 2026-08-06 발표 대본** ... ⇒ **이 대본을 그대로 재발표하지 말 것.**") that the client's `md()` renders first as a blockquote, and docs/pipeline_step1_to_step5_guide.md:320-325 marks its two retracted rows inline. summary: webapp/app.py (10,757 lines, 139 routes, last touched 2026-09-06) is the Flask surface over the whole DEM→MPM→STEP3→STEP4 pipeline. Structurally it is in good shape: path traversal is centralised in three audited helpers (_contained_join / _archive_join / _safe_path), the auth gate is fail-closed when enabled, subprocess-running GET routes are all in security.py's protected set, and several routes (seminar fail-closed retraction gate, _kit_apply_temperature, the mech-reaction CSV headers, /step5) are model examples of honest labelling. The health problem is not the plumbing, it is that the routes carry a frozen 2026-04→07 layer of physics prose that the ledger has since overturned, and the discipline checkers cannot see it: webapp/app.py is not in BAN_SCAN_GLOBS, so every retracted value, stale formula and mis-attribution written in Python (rather than in a template) sits outside the sweep — that is where the single hardcoded model ID and the three quotation-banned p1 ratios both live. Concretely: /results/<id>/report still prints v12-clean v3 / FORM-X-era scaling laws with n=57 R² 0.981 as "the production model" while group.html four files away prints the correct T1 form and labels those exact formulas "legacy/deprecated"; the MPM-kit route can only emit vox ≥ 0.2 point-stamp kits (the retracted CL-24/CL-25 configuration) and calls 0.4 "σ 검증값"; the CL-81 headline quantity R_brug_over_full = σ_contact-free/σ_full is displayed everywhere under a "Bruggeman overestimation" label with a wrong formula; /porosity-corpus.csv exports the one column structure_predictor.py declares it will "never export"; and one hard correctness bug — the archive 3D-data twin drops x/y/z from atoms_by_id, so every archived case is told its SE network has zero percolating particles, and that zero is then cached into viewer_aux.json where the grade routes read it.

findings.claim: The archive 3D-data route builds atoms_by_id without x/y/z, so compute_se_network_diagnostics sees z=0 for every particle and reports 0 percolating SE / 0 articulation points / 0 bottleneck edges for EVERY archived case — then caches that zero into viewer_aux.json, which /case/archive:<...>/grade reads.
findings.evidence: Archive route: `atoms_by_id = {int(r['id']): {'type': int(r['type']), 'radius': float(r['radius']),} for _, r in df.iterrows()}` (app.py:9922-9925). Live twin at app.py:7623-7629 includes `'x': float(r['x']) ... 'y': ... 'z': float(r['z']) if 'z' in df.columns else 0.0`. Consumer scripts/viewer3d_data.py:566-570 does `z = float(a.get('z', 0)); if z <= r * boundary_factor: bottom_se.add(pid); if z >= plate_z - r * boundary_factor: top_se.add(pid)` — with all z=0 every SE lands in bottom_se, top_se stays empty, fallback L1 (z_top = plate_z*0.85) also yields empty, and fallback L2 is skipped because `span = z_max_obs - z_min_obs` is 0. Result: no bottom↔top component ⇒ n_percolating = 0. The route then writes exactly those keys to cache (app.py:9995-10008) and app.py:3746-3762 / 3676-3684 feed them to build_overall_grade as se_aux, where scripts/grade_engine.py:806-823 drops __cut_fraction / __bn_below_frac / __bn_median_norm (weights 1.2/1.2/0.7) whenever n_percolating is 0.
findings.proposed_action: Add 'x'/'y'/'z' to the archive route's atoms_by_id (one-line parity with L7625-7628), then invalidate every viewer_aux.json written by this route (bump the `_schema` sentinel from 11 to 12 so stale caches are recomputed rather than trusted). Add a regression that runs both twins on the same fixture and asserts se_n_percolating is equal.

findings.claim: The downloadable per-case report prints three superseded scaling laws as the production models, with inflated fit statistics, including a σ_thermal power law that the repo has separately proven cannot exceed LOOCV 0.59.
findings.evidence: app.py:8629-8635 emits `| σ_ion (v12-clean v3, final) | σ_grain × √(φ−0.2) × CN^(3/2) × cov^(2/5) × f_p³ × C_blend(τ) | 0.981 |`, `| σ_el | 0.015 × σ_AM × φ_AM^(3/2) × CN_AM² × exp(π/(T/d)) | 0.89 |`, `| σ_th | 286 × σ_ion^(3/4) × φ_AM² / CN_SE | 0.90 |` and the note `σ_ion is the v12-clean v3 production model (n=57, LOOCV=0.979)`. Contradicted three ways: (a) CLAUDE.md 'σ_ionic form FINALIZED — T1 production' gives `σ = σ_grain · Cronau(r_SE) · (φ_eff)^½ · CN² · cov_Hertz^½ · f_p³ · exp[a + b·ln τ + c·(ln τ)² + β_P2·P2 + β_F·log f_intact]`, LOOCV ≈ 0.975 at n=88, and states of the older line 'Performance: R²≈0.975, LOOCV≈0.968 on n=92 (was 0.9813 / 0.9791 on n=57)'; (b) CLAUDE.md σ_e Stage 22.5 locks φ_AM⁴ and reports LOOCV 0.9531 — 'data picks EXACTLY 4 from {2,2.5,3,3.5,4,4.5,5,6,8}', so φ_AM^(3/2) is refuted; (c) CLAUDE.md σ_thermal Stage T1 A/B/C screen: 'A. Pure power-law (κ = ∏ feature^c ...): LOOCV ceiling 0.59' — the exact form printed here at 0.90. Same-scope contradiction: webapp/templates/group.html:1289 prints the T1 form with 'R² ≈ 0.975, LOOCV ≈ 0.97' and group.html:1330-1331 explicitly labels 'v12-clean v3' and 'FORM X v4++' as legacy/deprecated. Blame: this block dates to commit 11ef6c98 / 3008448c, 2026-05-27 — one day before the T1 adoption, six days before Stage 22.5, eight before Stage T1.
findings.proposed_action: Replace the three rows with the current forms and statistics, or better, render the block from the same source group.html:1284-1331 already uses so the two cannot drift again; keep the superseded rows only under an explicit 'legacy (deprecated)' heading as group.html does.

findings.claim: Every MPM kit the webapp hands out is a point-stamp SDCP run at vox ≥ 0.2 — the configuration whose results were retracted — the default is vox 0.4, the production sphere-stamp convention is unreachable from the UI, and the in-code comment understates the grid effect as 'slightly'.
findings.evidence: app.py:6937-6940: `_vox = request.args.get('vox', '0.4')` / `if _vox not in ('0.4', '0.25', '0.2'): _vox = '0.4'`, preceded by the comment `σ_e/σ_ion/R_geom can shift slightly (finite-volume grid dependence)`. The generated run_mpm.sh (scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py:1076) passes `--step3-vox {a.step3_vox:g}` and never `--step3-sdcp-sphere-d`, whose default in scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py:864 is 0.0 = point stamp. Contradicted by claims.json CL-24 (live): σ_e ratio `1.4215 → 1.1621 → 1.0849` and σ_ion ratio `1.0742 → 0.9926 → 0.9908` across vox 0.4 → 0.3 → 0.25, i.e. a 34 % move and a sign flip, not 'slightly'. Contradicted by CL-25 / CLAUDE.md: 'SDCP 표현부피/참부피 = 4.311(vox 0.4) · 1.866(0.3) · 1.090(0.25) · 0.238(0.15)'. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md's gate note: 'd/vox ≥ 2 라 Ø0.30 SDCP 는 vox ≤ 0.15 에서만 구 스탬프가 허용된다 ... {0.25, 0.2} 는 원리적으로 불가' — so no offered value can produce a legal sphere stamp. The generator's own help still calls 0.4 'σ 검증값' (scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py:119) and webapp/templates/single.html:265 tells the user 'σ 절대값은 vox에 약간 의존하니 비교표는 0.4로' (written 2026-07-09, before CL-24 on 2026-08-13).
findings.proposed_action: Add 0.15 to the whitelist, expose --step3-sdcp-sphere-d 0.30 (gated to vox ≤ 0.15) as the production convention, change the default away from 0.4, and rewrite the two 'slightly / σ 검증값 / 비교표는 0.4로' strings to state the measured CL-24 grid dependence. If offering vox 0.15 is not affordable on the target hardware, at minimum stamp a warning into the generated run_mpm.sh and the zip name saying the kit is the CL-24-retracted convention.

findings.claim: An unauthenticated GET serves any file under the repository root, including webapp/.env (which holds the Supabase service-role key), with no extension or prefix whitelist — and the route is dead, referenced from nowhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: app.py:10210-10213: `doc_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__)); return send_from_directory(doc_dir, filename, as_attachment=True)` with `<path:filename>` — safe_join blocks `..` but not `webapp/.env` or `docs/reviews/claims.json`. app.py:52-58 loads secrets from `webapp/.env`; webapp/security.py header states the server 'Supabase **service-role key** 를 쥐고 있다'. security.py:_is_protected returns False for any GET not in _PROTECTED_GET_ENDPOINTS (:57-64), and download_doc is not listed, so the route stays open even with WEBAPP_REQUIRE_AUTH=1. Contradicted inside the same file: the sibling reader /api/seminar/file (app.py:3965-3966) carries `_SEMINAR_SRC_PREFIX = ('docs/', 'scripts/', 'webapp/')`, `_SEMINAR_SRC_EXT = ('.md', '.py', '.csv', '.json', '.html', '.sh', '.txt')` with the comment '임의 파일 열람 창구가 되면 안 된다'. `grep -rn 'download-doc'` across every .html/.js/.py/.md in the repo returns only the route definition itself.
findings.proposed_action: Delete the route (it has no caller), or give it the same prefix+extension whitelist as /api/seminar/file and add download_doc to _PROTECTED_GET_ENDPOINTS.

findings.locator: L2072 glossary, L1812-1816 row emit, L5960 group column, L8750 plain-language help
findings.claim: The dashboard, group table, MD report and grade guide all display `R_brug_over_full` as 'Bruggeman overestimation, R_brug = σ_Bruggeman / σ_ionic', but the solver writes that key as σ_contact-free / σ_full — the Holm/Maxwell constriction gap that CL-81 has just made the live cross-check quantity.
findings.evidence: scripts/network_conductivity.py:1095-1096: `if sigma_cf and sigma_full: results['R_brug_over_full'] = round(sigma_cf / sigma_full, 4)  # contact-free / full`, with the true EMT ratio stored separately at :1097-1098 as `R_bruggeman_over_full`. app.py:2072 maps the displayed label to `'Bruggeman overestimation, R_brug = σ_Bruggeman / σ_ionic'`; app.py:1813 fills that row from `metrics.get('R_brug_over_full')`; app.py:8750 explains it to users as '간단한 이론식이 실제보다 이온 전도도를 몇 배나 부풀려 예측하는지'; webapp/templates/single.html:1922-1923 repeats the wrong formula verbatim (`σ_Bruggeman = σ_grain × φ_SE × f_perc / τ²`). app.py contradicts itself at :2085, where the same key is correctly captioned `'σ_contact-free / σ_full — constriction overestimation'`. claims.json CL-81 (live, 2026-09-08): 'R_brug_over_full(= σ_cf/σ_full, 이온 채널) n=157 중앙값 4.04×(Hertz) · 6.69×(소성면적), 범위 2.3~13.6×' and 'kim2025 EIS 의 GB-only 3.75× 가 우리 4.04 와 8 % 안에서 만난다'. single.html:1925's own 'ensemble 통상 3~10×' matches the contact-free distribution, not a Bruggeman EMT ratio.
findings.proposed_action: Rename the displayed row and its plain-language help to 'Contact-free / Full (constriction gap)', fix the formula string to σ_cf/σ_full, and add the CL-81 pointer plus the 6× corpus scatter warning so readers do not treat it as a common-mode-safe constant.

findings.claim: The corpus CSV export ships `use_porosity_pct` and `use_source`, the exact column CLAUDE.md marks '학습·노출 금지' and that webapp/structure_predictor.py declares it will never export.
findings.evidence: app.py:7979 `'use_source': use_source, 'use_porosity_pct': use_por,` and :7989 lists both in the CSV fieldnames. webapp/structure_predictor.py:47: `# 이 열은 절대 내보내지 않는다 — 게이트가 φ 와 다른 모델을 섞어 한 물리상태가 아니다` / `FORBIDDEN = ('use_porosity_pct',)`, enforced by its own selftest at :329 `chk('★판정표에 use_porosity_pct 가 없다 (게이트 혼합열은 노출 금지)', ...)`. CLAUDE.md (2026-08-03, ml_design_structure section): '★ use_porosity_pct 는 학습·노출 금지 열 — 게이트가 porosity 만 MPM 으로 바꾸고 φ 는 DEM 것을 남겨, 닫힘 잔차 sd 가 ε 자체 sd 의 78 % (한 물리상태가 아님). porosity 는 회귀 말고 ε = C − φ_SE − φ_AM 로 계산' and the verdict line 'REJECT 1 = use_porosity_pct .397'. The route block predates that ruling (blame: commit 4fdb58cc, 2026-07-20).
findings.proposed_action: Drop `use_porosity_pct` from the CSV (keep `dem_porosity_pct`, `mpm_porosity_pct`, `gap_dem_minus_mpm`, `regime` — those are raw and honest), or gate it behind an explicit `?include_gated=1` with a header comment quoting the 78 % closure-residual reason.

findings.claim: The DEM↔MPM regime gate subtracts two porosities computed under different conventions and then calls |gap| ≤ 4 %p 'cross-validated — two independent models agree', a certificate reading the canon has withdrawn as circular.
findings.evidence: app.py:7940-7957 computes `_graw = float(dem) - float(mpm)` where `dem` is `porosity_spheresum` (ε_sphere) and `mpm` is `porosity_mpm_pct` (union bookkeeping), then comments `cross-validated : two independent models agree → use MPM.  ±2.4`; app.py:543 sets the same label for the case-list badge. Convention mismatch: docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md:754-758 measures `MPM관례(16.877) − ε_sphere(15.626) = 1.251 %p` and states 'DEM 은 ε_sphere(구 부피 합), MPM 은 union 부기', and CLAUDE.md adds '모든 porosity 는 ε_sphere 로 통일해 보고할 것'; the offset is ~31 % of the ±4 threshold. Worse, docs/reviews/fam_platen_prereg_20260812.md:309-325 shows it is not even constant: '오프셋 = (겹침 부피 946.66 µm³) / (A · h) ⇒ 1/h 로 스케일한다 ... 정정: ε_sphere = ε_MPM − 946.66/(A·h)·100', giving 1.4654 %p at h=25.84 µm. Certificate wording: CLAUDE.md 2026-08-12 — '★★ 정정 — 일치 = validity 증명서 는 hold 시대에 성립하지 않는다 ... 씨앗이 정답을 인코딩한다 ... ⇒ 일치를 증명서로 쓰면 순환이다.' The repo already applied this fix in one place only: webapp/templates/index.html:130 badges carry '⚠ 정본 유보: MPM porosity 는 정지 프레임의 함수이고 수렴하지 않는다 (CL-04 ...). DEM↔MPM 일치를 validity 증명서로 읽지 말 것 — 씨앗이 정답을 인코딩해 순환이다', while webapp/templates/single.html:684 and this CSV route carry no such caveat.
findings.proposed_action: Convert one side to the other convention with the §10-2 formula before differencing (or emit both raw values plus the computed offset as extra columns), re-derive the ±4 threshold on the converted gap, and propagate index.html:130's caveat text to single.html:684 and to the CSV header.

Does NOT change form σ_S/σ_P anchors (those stay locked / # at Trevisanello 10/5 literature defaults per Stage 22 design).` docs/a1_sigma_e_direction_closeout.md:7-10: 'The values σ_S = 10, σ_P = 5 mS/cm were cited as "Trevisanello 2021". findings.claim: The EIS routes put an absolute STEP3 voxel σ_ion next to measured EIS and present overlap as frame[4] cross-validation, with no statement anywhere that the voxel σ_ion carries no constriction/interfacial term and is a CONTACT_FREE upper bound.
findings.evidence: app.py:4223-4232 loads the case's σ via `_eis._load_step3_params(_mp)`, which in scripts/eis_drt_ica.py:584 returns `'sigma_ion_S_cm': s3.get('sigma_ion_eff_S_cm')` — the voxel STEP3 value. app.py:4246-4252 then overlays `_eis.load_experimental_anchors()` (the eis_fit CPE→C_dl and Wo1_R from the lab cells), and /api/eis_exp closes with the note `'방울=실측 Nyquist, physics-EIS 선과 겹치면 frame[4]'` (app.py:4637-4639). claims.json CL-81 (live, 2026-09-08): '복셀 FV 는 면을 harmonic mean 으로만 잇는다 ⇒ SE 셀↔SE 셀 = 3.0 mS/cm, 계면 저항 항이 정확히 0' and its citation rule '⛔ 인용 규약: STEP3 σ_ion 절대값을 실험 옆에 적을 때 "협착 미포함 = CONTACT_FREE 상한" 을 함께 적는다. σ_ion 상대비교에 "공통모드 상쇄" 를 근거 없이 쓰지 않는다', plus the size (median 4.04×/6.69×, range 2.3–13.6×). `grep -n 'CONTACT_FREE\|협착\|constriction'` over scripts/eis_drt_ica.py, the four route bodies and webapp/templates/eis.html returns nothing.
findings.proposed_action: Add a `sigma_ion_provenance` field to the /api/eis and /api/eis_cycle responses whenever `case_loaded` is set, carrying 'STEP3 voxel FV — constriction/GB term absent (CONTACT_FREE upper bound, CL-81; corpus σ_cf/σ_full median 4.04×, range 2.3–13.6×)', and render it in eis.html next to the overlay legend.
