findings.claim: Three grade paths use three different corpus/case_id configurations, so the ranking score on the index page and the composite score on the case page disagree for the same case — and the What-if toggle silently switches between them.
findings.evidence: app.py:847 and :8863 route the dashboard table and the grade guide through `_grade_engine_result`, which builds the dynamic corpus (`corpus_rows = _build_dynamic_corpus_rows(static_csv)`, app.py:793) but never passes `case_id`. app.py:3688-3691 (/api/all-grades) and :3763-3767 (/case/<id>/grade) call `build_overall_grade(..., corpus_csv, se_aux, ..., case_id=case_id)` with the static path only. scripts/grade_engine.py:1522-1523: `if corpus_rows is None: corpus_rows = _load_corpus(corpus_csv)` — so corpus_rows wins when supplied, and its docstring says 'corpus_csv: When omitted, corpus-relative axes drop to "—"' and 'case_id: needed by __Q_target_match_pct'. Because `docs/data/se_diagnostics_82.csv` is not in the repo (`git log -- docs/data/se_diagnostics_82.csv` returns nothing; the file is absent), the two JSON routes fall back to `corpus_csv = None` and drop every corpus-relative axis, while the server-rendered table scores them from live cases — different `n_axes`, different weighted composite, opposite direction on `__Q_target_match_pct`.
findings.proposed_action: Route /api/all-grades and /case/<id>/grade through `_grade_engine_result` (adding a `case_id` parameter to it) so all four surfaces share one corpus and one axis set; assert in a test that /api/all-grades' score for a case equals the score its /single page renders.

findings.claim: The carbon What-if re-ranks the entire corpus from a model its own author calls a back-of-the-envelope, the caveat is stripped from the ranking response, and the note it does return ('matches the literature-reported 10–100× σ_e improvement') is contradicted by the model's own arithmetic on this corpus.
findings.evidence: scripts/grade_engine.py:1594-1596 docstring: 'This is a back-of-the-envelope: full simulation requires placing a secondary phase in the DEM and re-solving. Useful only as an indicative direction.' The returned `note` (:1635-1638) claims '실제 cathode에 carbon black 1 wt%를 첨가했을 때 문헌 보고된 σ_e 향상 10–100배에 부합'. But the model (:1610-1614) is `phi_carbon = (wt_pct/100)*(3.5/2.0)` and `delta_sigma = phi_carbon**2 * 1000`, so at 1 wt% Δσ = 0.0175² × 1000 = 0.306 mS/cm; for the corpus σ_e values CLAUDE.md records (9.014, 33, 51.89 mS/cm) the ratio is 1.03–1.006×, and reaching 10× requires σ_e_old ≈ 0.034 mS/cm. Separately, the docstring's own band 'Carbon black bulk σ ≈ 100–1000 S/cm = 10⁵–10⁶ mS/cm. Use a conservative 1000 mS/cm' applies an unanchored 100–1000× haircut — the class of unanchored σ hook that findings.json SELF-13 flags ('all six phase σ values in SIGMA_DEFAULT are order-of-magnitude hooks; none is tied to a measurement') and that CL-47/R20-04 show is genuinely contested for carbon. app.py:3688-3701 returns only `case_id/score/grade/n_axes/is_unit_cell/rve_area_um2/base_case` — the note never reaches the ranking client (webapp/templates/index.html:334 `fetch('/api/all-grades?carbon_wt=...')`).
findings.proposed_action: Delete or correct the '10–100배에 부합' sentence (compute the actual ratio band over the corpus and state it), carry an `assumed: true` + `basis: 'back-of-envelope Bruggeman t=2, σ_carbon 1000 mS/cm unanchored'` field into both route responses, and show it in the index ranking bar whenever the toggle is on.

findings.claim: Two download routes serve 2026-04 documents that declare FORM X the 'Final Formula' and give the σ_thermal power law an R² of 0.88 — the model CLAUDE.md calls 'the OLDER, inferior model' and the form proven to cap at LOOCV 0.59.
findings.evidence: app.py:10466 serves `docs/Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md`, whose header reads `**Final Formula**: FORM X — σ = C × σ_grain × (φ_SE - φc)^¾ × CN × √cov / √τ` (generated 2026-04-14, unchanged since commit 660600a4 on 2026-04-24). app.py:10474 serves `docs/Formula_Catalog.md`, whose §B.11 gives `★ THICK FINAL  σ_el(thick) = 0.79 × σ_AM × φ⁴ × CN^(3/2) × cov × √τ  R² = 0.969, LOOCV = 0.967` and §C gives `σ_thermal = 286 × σ_ionic^(3/4) × φ_AM² / CN_SE  R² ≈ 0.88`. CLAUDE.md: '**FORM X (v4++)** `C·σ_grain·(φ−0.185)^¾·CN·√cov/√τ` (R²≈0.96) is the OLDER, inferior model — kept only as a legacy toggle / predictor fallback', and σ_thermal 'Pure power-law ... LOOCV ceiling 0.59'. webapp/templates/group.html:1331 in the same application labels FORM X '현재 deprecated'. Neither route is linked from any template or JS (grep for 'formula-catalog' / 'full-report' across webapp/templates and webapp/static returns nothing), so they are also orphaned. The identical FORM-X text is additionally committed at webapp/results/reports/scaling_law_report_full.md, which no ban-sweep glob covers.
findings.proposed_action: Either regenerate both documents against the current T1 / Stage 22.5 / Stage T1 forms, or prepend a HISTORICAL banner naming claims.json and have the routes refuse without `?historical=1`, mirroring the pattern app.py:4077-4105 already uses for the seminar deck. Delete or re-banner the committed webapp/results/reports/*.md copies in the same commit.

findings.claim: The STEP3 comparison tooltip still calls σ_SDCP = 250 S/cm an 'anchor', the exact label CL-61 retracted five days ago.
findings.evidence: viewer3d.js:6194: `'전도상: AM + VGCF/SuperP + SDCP(250 S/cm 앵커).'` claims.json CL-61 (live, 2026-09-03): '리포가 써 온 라벨 "σ_SDCP 250 = 재료 앵커(S-PEDOT 벌크)" 를 **철회**한다' — reference [35] (Patil 1987) is 3-substituted polythiophene with `PEDOT` 0 occurrences, so 'ⓘ 라벨 재료 앵커 철회. 정본 라벨은 ... **`Assumed (specified by the authors, S-PEDOT class)`**'. CL-81 repeats it: 'SDCP 250 은 그 밴드가 없다(CL-61) ... 융합 결손이 보상 없이 얹힌다'. The same tooltip block is otherwise exemplary — its CL-24 retraction notes at :6206/:6210/:6212/:6217 are correct and current — which makes the single stale 앵커 the outlier. webapp/templates/seminar.html:209 already uses the right wording ('σ_SDCP=250 S/cm 는 측정 대기 가정').
findings.proposed_action: Replace '250 S/cm 앵커' with '250 S/cm — Assumed (저자 지정, S-PEDOT class; 문헌 앵커 없음 — CL-61)'; grep viewer3d.js and the templates for any other '앵커' attached to a phase σ.

findings.claim: The report title arrives from the POST form and goes into the output path with only spaces replaced, so `/group/report` can write a .md anywhere the process can write — the F-06 defect class the repo already solved once with _slugify_case_name.
findings.evidence: app.py:6443 `title = request.form.get('title', 'DEM_Bimodal_Comparison')`; app.py:6599 `report_path = os.path.join(group_dir, f'{now}_{title.replace(" ", "_")}.md')`. `title.replace(' ', '_')` strips neither `/` nor `..`, and no `_safe_path` / `_contained_join` guard is applied. The repo's own fix for this exact class sits at app.py:375-386: `_slugify_case_name` — '★ F-06: 표시 이름과 저장 경로를 분리한다. 옛 코드는 사용자가 정한 meta["name"] 을 그대로 os.path.join(dst, name) 에 썼는데, 이름에는 경로 문자 검증이 없어 archive 저장 위치가 루트를 벗어날 수 있었다.' — and it is applied at app.py:9538 but not here.
findings.proposed_action: Wrap the title with `_slugify_case_name(title, fallback='group_report')` before building report_path (keep the raw title for the report body, as _save_case_to_archive already does for display names).

findings.locator: L3588 (_generate_ai_analysis) and the file as a whole vs scripts/check_review_findings.py:105-118
findings.claim: webapp/app.py is outside every discipline glob, and it holds the repository's only hardcoded model identifier plus an LLM section that writes unswept markdown into a directory no checker reads.
findings.evidence: app.py:3588 `model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514"` — `grep -rn 'claude-sonnet-4|claude-opus|claude-3' --include=*.py --include=*.js --include=*.html --include=*.sh --include=*.yml .` returns exactly this one line repo-wide. wiki/tools/lint.py:54 `MODEL_ID = re.compile(r'claude-(?:opus|sonnet|haiku|fable)[a-z0-9.\-]*', re.I)` matches it and treats it as an error, but only over wiki pages; CLAUDE.md states 'Never put the model identifier in commits/PRs'. Separately, scripts/check_review_findings.py:105-118 BAN_SCAN_GLOBS = ('CLAUDE.md', 'docs/**/*.md', 'wiki/**/*.md', 'webapp/templates/*.html', 'webapp/static/js/*.js', 'scripts/seminar_deck/*.js', 'docs/**/*.json', 'webapp/**/*.json', 'scripts/*.sh', 'docs/**/*.pptx', 'docs/**/*.docx', 'docs/**/*.js') — no `webapp/*.py` and no `webapp/**/*.md`, so /group/report's output at app.py:6597 (`os.path.join(app.config['RESULTS_FOLDER'], 'group_reports')`) plus the LLM prose appended at app.py:6588-6592 are never swept, and neither are the two committed webapp/results/reports/*.md. This is the same media hole findings.json CDXIJ-4 and CDXIJ-9 closed for JSON decks and pptx.
findings.proposed_action: Add `webapp/*.py` and `webapp/**/*.md` to BAN_SCAN_GLOBS and re-run the sweep; move the model id to an env var (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) with no default baked into the source; and run the AI-analysis output through the ban patterns before appending it to the report.

findings.locator: L1272 and L2138 (Stage E σ_e row label, rendered by /results/<case_id>/report, /single, /archive/view)
findings.claim: The Stage E AM-crystallinity factor (AM_P = 0.65) is attributed on screen to 'Trevisanello 2021', which the repo's own A1 close-out says did not measure electronic σ_e at all.
findings.evidence: app.py:1268-1272 emits the row `'σ_e — AM crystal × size'` with the source cell `'Trevisanello 2021 + size-dependent internal-GB density'`; app.py:2137-2138 maps it to `'σ_e correction — AM-crystallinity × size factor (Trevisanello 2021)'`; webapp/templates/single.html:2392-2393 repeats it with `AM_P (polycryst secondary): 0.65 (Trevisanello 2021)`. scripts/run_network_full_corrections.py:14-16 is the origin (`σ_e_grain_AM(crystal) — Trevisanello 2021 SC vs PC / AM_S: 1.00 / AM_P: 0.65`). docs/a1_sigma_e_direction_closeout.md:8-10: 'Trevisanello 2021 measured Li⁺ chemical diffusion / BET surface area / R_ct — NOT electronic σ_e', and :25-28 allows only 'the same GB direction (Trevisanello-*spirit*), with β/r0 corpus-fit — not a Trevisanello σ_e formula'. The A1 close-out scoped itself to σ_S/σ_P and NCM(r) and never touched this third σ_e factor, so the two statements now sit side by side unreconciled.
findings.proposed_action: Decide whether 0.65 has any citable source; if not, relabel as 'GB-direction (Trevisanello-spirit); magnitude assumed' consistently in run_network_full_corrections.py, app.py:1272/2138 and single.html:2393. This needs the literature call the A1 close-out made for the other two terms.

findings.claim: Eleven z-profile helpers parse ?bins with a bare int() and no range check, while the repo's own guard for the identical parameter is applied to only two routes.
findings.evidence: All eleven sites read `bins = int(request.args.get('bins', 25))`, so `?bins=x` raises ValueError → 500, and `?bins=0` / negative values reach the profile computation. app.py:7279-7286 defines the fix: `def _mech_bins(raw, default=14): """Sanitize the ?bins query for the mech-reaction routes — invalid / out-of-range (incl. 0 → ZeroDivisionError, negative → IndexError) falls back to the default.""" ... return b if 2 <= b <= 200 else default`, used only at :7302 and :7333. Same shape as the recurring twin-divergence findings.json records (CDXR2-4: '한 경로를 고치고 쌍둥이를 안 고친다').
findings.proposed_action: Replace all eleven with `_mech_bins(request.args.get('bins'), default=25)` and add a smoke test that hits each z-profile route with bins=0, bins=-1 and bins=abc.

findings.locator: L6018-6022 (group(), σ_e Stage E display column)
findings.claim: The group comparison table silently blanks any σ_e above 100 mS/cm, so an out-of-range value is indistinguishable from a value that was never computed — and the additive campaigns now running sit right under that ceiling.
findings.evidence: app.py:6019-6022: `metrics['_sigma_e_stage_e_display'] = (stE_e if isinstance(stE_e, (int, float)) and 0 < stE_e <= 100 else (raw_e if raw_e <= 100 else None))`, and app.py:6071 renders `None` as `'-'` — the same glyph used for a missing metric. The surrounding comment (app.py:6013-6017) documents only the phantom/fallback filter and never mentions the 100 mS/cm ceiling, and no other cap in the file is this quantity. Scale check: claims.json CL-46 records the model SBE absolute σ_e at 73 mS/cm with DBE above it, i.e. within 27 % of the cap.
findings.proposed_action: Either drop the ceiling (the phantom filter already handles the case it was presumably added for) or render out-of-range as an explicit '>100 ⚠' token so it cannot be read as 'not computed'; document whichever is chosen in the comment above.

findings.claim: The `_vox` tag is gated on the recipe being non-empty, so two kits built at different STEP3 voxel sizes with no additive recipe download under identical filenames — for the one knob measured to move σ_e by 34 %.
findings.evidence: app.py:7127-7129: `if recipe and _vox != '0.4': tag += '_vox' + _vox`, mirrored deliberately in webapp/templates/single.html:1066 (`const vt = (pairs && vox && vox !== '0.4') ? '_vox' + vox : ''`) with the note at :1073 that the gate exists to keep the client name mirror intact for operating-condition-only kits. But the same route tags every other σ-changing knob unconditionally — app.py:7139-7141 '★솔버 cap 은 σ_eff 를 −7.8% 바꾸는 노브 → 같은 이름의 두 킷이 생기지 않게 태그' — and CL-24 measures vox as a 34 % σ_e mover (1.4215 → 1.0849 over 0.4 → 0.25), i.e. four times the cap effect. This is the class findings.json SELF-16 describes: 'directory tag rule strips dots, collapsing the registered σ_SDCP grid points 2.5 and 25 into one name and silently reusing arms across two different experiments.'
findings.proposed_action: Drop the `recipe and` condition on both server and client so `_vox` is always tagged when it differs from the default, and add the tag to the manifest's protocol id if it is not already there.

findings.claim: The two 3D-data routes are an 80 % copy of each other (206 identical normalised lines) whose only intended difference is how the directory is resolved — and the copy has already drifted into two silent behaviour differences.
findings.evidence: Normalised (comment- and whitespace-stripped) diff over the two bodies: SequenceMatcher ratio 0.803, 206 identical lines out of 264/249. The archive copy's comment claims parity — app.py:9931-9933 `# Aux cache (same logic as /results/<id>/3d-data above ...)` — but it (a) omits x/y/z from atoms_by_id (finding 1) and (b) restores only 9 hardcoded keys on cache HIT (app.py:9941-9948 `for k in ('stress_max', 'dr_max', 'brittle_pairs', 'se_stress_pairs', 'am_se_stress_pairs', 'se_states', 'tabor_stats', 'all_se_ids_count', 'se_engagement')`) whereas the live route copies every non-underscore key (app.py:7661-7666) — so the SE-diagnostics and per-particle fracture keys that the archive route itself writes to cache at :9995-10008 are present on first load and silently absent on every load after.
findings.proposed_action: Extract the shared body into one `_serve_3d_data(results_dir, meta, case_label)` helper called by both routes, leaving only the directory resolution and the log prefix at the route level; that removes findings 1 and this one together.

findings.claim: Four routes depend on docs/data/se_diagnostics_82.csv, the paper's baseline corpus, which is not in the repository — so corpus-percentile grading silently degrades and /api/se_corpus.json returns an error body with HTTP 200.
findings.evidence: `ls docs/data/se_diagnostics_82.csv` → No such file; `git log -- docs/data/se_diagnostics_82.csv` returns nothing (never committed, and not listed in .gitignore). app.py:3612-3614 returns `jsonify({'error': 'corpus CSV not found — run scripts/extract_se_network_diagnostics.py first.', 'rows': []}), 200`; app.py:3681-3682 and :3745-3746 set `corpus_csv = None`, which scripts/grade_engine.py:1496-1497 documents as 'When omitted, corpus-relative axes drop to "—"'. Four axes carry `direction: higher_corpus/lower_corpus` (grade_engine.py:114-137), so they vanish from the composite without any user-visible notice.
findings.proposed_action: Commit the CSV (or a regeneration recipe with a checked-in checksum), and make the grade routes report `corpus_source: 'live-only (static baseline missing)'` in their JSON so a degraded composite is visible rather than inferred.

findings.claim: A POST route that re-runs the contact analysis, network solver and Stage E over every case in the corpus has no caller anywhere in the repository.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'batch-rerun|batchRerun'` across webapp/templates/, webapp/static/, scripts/ and docs/ returns nothing; the only occurrences are the two @app.route decorators. The handler spawns a daemon thread that walks `_find_all_cases()` (results + archive) and rewrites full_metrics.json for each. Its status sibling is likewise unreferenced. Both were built around the `physics_resistance_model` migration ('Use after changing the solver resistance model', app.py:5543-5544), which the case-list badges at app.py:469-477 show as already complete ('mikic'/'maxwell+film' = upgraded).
findings.proposed_action: Either wire it into the audit page as an admin action with a confirmation, or delete both routes — an unreferenced corpus-wide rewrite endpoint that regenerates the very metrics the ledger anchors to is a standing hazard.

findings.claim: The plain-language help states the compaction pressure as 380 MPa and tells the user that overlap above 10 % is suspected over-compression — a rule that would flag the repo's own validated pure-SE Cronau calibration as defective.
findings.evidence: app.py:8693-8695: '380 MPa 압력에서 SE 입자는 문헌상 5-10% 정도 소성변형하는데, 그 범위 안이면 정상. 10% 넘으면 과압축 의심.' The production target throughout CLAUDE.md is 300 MPa ('porosity ≈ 10% @ 300 MPa', 'pure-SE calibration ... 0.30 → 10.0 % = Minnmann 300 → 10 %'), and 380 appears nowhere else in app.py. On the threshold: CLAUDE.md's Cronau resolution states 'PURE-SE @ 1.35 GPa (SE load-bearing, lens approx EXACT) gives overlap 11–12% across 2 loadings ... i.e. AT/above Cronau' and calls that the correct reproduction of the plastic floor — so 11–12 % is validated physics, not 'over-compression suspected'. webapp/templates/single.html:1943 carries the same 380 MPa figure ('3–7×: 전형적인 380 MPa sintering 조건').
findings.proposed_action: Change 380 → 300 MPa in both strings and reword the threshold to distinguish the AM-shielded composite regime (≈1.75 %, expected) from the load-bearing pure-SE regime (11–12 %, at the Cronau floor), rather than a single 10 % alarm.

findings.claim: The anchors API returns eight bare R_int numbers with none of the precision qualifiers the canonical CSV attaches to every one of them.
findings.evidence: app.py:6650-6652 returns `{k: dict(zip(('pristine','cycled'), _rint_anchor_pair(k))) for k in ('sbe','dbe','csus','sus')}` — values only. docs/data/rint_eis_anchors.csv marks lab_sbe_pristine / lab_dbe_pristine / lab_csus_pristine as `panel_e_approx` with the note '⚠근사(정밀 digitize 대기)', lab_*_cycled with '⚠T_cycle 미지정', and lab_sus_cycled as `projected_literature` with '⚠문헌투영(assumed-form)'. CLAUDE.md's backlog lists A11 ('pristine 정밀 digitize') as '⛔ 데이터 대기'. webapp/templates/single.html:995 compensates by hardcoding its own provenance strings ('panel-e≈', '문헌투영 SC√N'), which means the labels live in the client rather than the API and any other consumer loses them.
findings.proposed_action: Return `{value, precision, note}` per scenario, read from the CSV columns the loader already parses, and have single.html render the server-supplied label instead of its own copy.

surface_worthy.why: The most current, complete, per-term explanation of the production σ_ionic form anywhere outside CLAUDE.md — it has the T1 formula, the FROZEN φc values, the DO-NOT-re-screen rule, the ablation impacts, the outlier landscape, and an explicit legacy section retiring v12-clean v3 and FORM X. It is buried inside a JavaScript template literal at L1284-1331 and is contradicted by /results/<id>/report four files away.
surface_worthy.one_line: The σ_ionic T1 derivation panel (group.html:1284-1331) is the app's correct canon — promote it to the hub and make the report route render from it.

surface_worthy.why: _kit_apply_temperature (L6764-6854) is the only operational write-up of the --temp-k / --i0-temp-scale pairing rule, including the history of why --temp-k alone inverts the overpotential sign and why --i0-temp-scale alone produces a multiplier of exactly 1.0 while stamping a false kinetics_T_scaling label. It also demonstrates the correct fail-closed pattern: if the injection marker is not found exactly once, no kit is produced.
surface_worthy.one_line: The temperature-injection convention (two flags are a pair; either alone is a silent lie) is documented only inside one webapp helper.

surface_worthy.why: L4014-4105 is the repo's working template for serving a retracted artifact: fail-closed behind ?historical=1, a JSON (not plain-text) refusal so the client cannot navigate into it, and evidence_ref/evidence_claim pointing at claims.json so the refusal is checkable. findings.json R19-01/R19-02/R19-03 record the three separate failures that produced this shape.
surface_worthy.one_line: The ?historical=1 + evidence_ref refusal pattern is the reusable answer to 'how do we keep serving a retracted artifact honestly'.

surface_worthy.why: L1077 and L1095-1096 are where the CL-81 quantity actually lives: `'sigma_bulk_net': ... # contact-free (legacy key kept for compat)` and `results['R_brug_over_full'] = round(sigma_cf / sigma_full, 4)  # contact-free / full`. The misleading key name is the root cause of the display mislabel across four webapp surfaces, and the true Bruggeman ratio sits one line below under a name almost nobody reads.
surface_worthy.one_line: R_brug_over_full is σ_contact-free/σ_full, not a Bruggeman ratio — the legacy key name is why CL-81's evidence was hiding in plain sight.

surface_worthy.why: L130's MPM regime badge tooltips already carry the full CL-04 caveat verbatim ('MPM porosity 는 정지 프레임의 함수이고 수렴하지 않는다 ... DEM↔MPM 일치를 validity 증명서로 읽지 말 것 — 씨앗이 정답을 인코딩해 순환이다'). It is the model wording, and it shows exactly which two other surfaces (single.html:684 and /porosity-corpus.csv) still lack it.
surface_worthy.one_line: The corrected DEM↔MPM regime wording exists in one template only — copy it to the case page and the CSV export.

surface_worthy.why: It states the deployment posture (cloud deploy retired 2026-08-07; the gate is now defence-in-depth, default OFF, fail-closed when a token is set) and, critically, the limitation nobody has written down elsewhere: _is_protected returns False for every GET not in _PROTECTED_GET_ENDPOINTS, so read routes stay open even with WEBAPP_REQUIRE_AUTH=1. That is the premise behind the /download-doc finding.
surface_worthy.one_line: Enabling the auth gate does not protect GET routes — the read surface is open by design, which matters for any route that can read arbitrary files.

surface_worthy.why: _eis_python (L4918-4949) and _subproc_msg (L4952-4972) solve two recurring operational failures with reusable logic: pick the interpreter that can actually import the required module (not the one on PATH), and surface the LAST traceback line plus a pip install prescription rather than the first 200 characters. Both were written after real incidents where the shell succeeded and the webapp failed on the same machine.
surface_worthy.one_line: The 'which python3 can import this' probe and the last-line-of-traceback error formatter are generic fixes currently used only by the EIS routes.

surface_worthy.why: _TRUST_LEDS (L112-213) encodes five validation gates with, per gate, the measured value key, the pass criterion in plain English, Korean pass/fail/NA explanations, and a paper-section reference. It is the closest thing the repo has to a machine-readable trust rubric, and /audit renders it corpus-wide, but it is defined as a 100-line literal in the middle of a 10,757-line file.
surface_worthy.one_line: The five-gate trust rubric with per-gate criteria and references is a hub-worthy artifact hidden inside app.py's header.

surviving_p0p1.claim: The archive 3D-data route builds atoms_by_id without x/y/z, so compute_se_network_diagnostics sees z=0 for every particle and reports 0 percolating SE / 0 articulation points / 0 bottleneck edges for EVERY archived case — then caches that zero into viewer_aux.json, which /case/archive:<...>/grade reads.
surviving_p0p1.evidence: Archive route: `atoms_by_id = {int(r['id']): {'type': int(r['type']), 'radius': float(r['radius']),} for _, r in df.iterrows()}` (app.py:9922-9925). Live twin at app.py:7623-7629 includes `'x': float(r['x']) ... 'y': ... 'z': float(r['z']) if 'z' in df.columns else 0.0`. Consumer scripts/viewer3d_data.py:566-570 does `z = float(a.get('z', 0)); if z <= r * boundary_factor: bottom_se.add(pid); if z >= plate_z - r * boundary_factor: top_se.add(pid)` — with all z=0 every SE lands in bottom_se, top_se stays empty, fallback L1 (z_top = plate_z*0.85) also yields empty, and fallback L2 is skipped because `span = z_max_obs - z_min_obs` is 0. The repo's own fix for this exact class sits at app.py:375-386: `_slugify_case_name` — '★ F-06: 표시 이름과 저장 경로를 분리한다. 옛 코드는 사용자가 정한 meta["name"] 을 그대로 os.path.join(dst, name) 에 썼는데, 이름에는 경로 문자 검증이 없어 archive 저장 위치가 루트를 벗어날 수 있었다.' — and it is applied at app.py:9538 but not here.
surviving_p0p1.proposed_action: Wrap the title with `_slugify_case_name(title, fallback='group_report')` before building report_path (keep the raw title for the report body, as _save_case_to_archive already does for display names).
surviving_p0p1.corrected: webapp/app.py:6443/6599 (group_report, POST /group/report) passes the user-supplied `title` into the output path with only `str.replace(' ', '_')`, applying neither `_slugify_case_name` (app.py:375-386, the repo's own F-06 remediation, used at :9539) nor `_safe_path`/`_contained_join`. This is a genuine missing guard, but it does NOT permit writing outside the results directory: the `{now}_` prefix is concatenated to the title without a separator, so the first path component is always `<YYMMDD>_<first-title-segment>` rather than a bare `..`, and `os.path.join` never resets to absolute because that argument starts with a digit. Since `open()` resolves each component in the kernel, `../../../../tmp/evil`, `/tmp/evil` and `x/../../tmp/evil` all raise FileNotFoundError (they would require directories named `260908_..`, `260908_` or `260908_x`), and nothing in the repo ever creates a subdirectory under results/group_reports — this route is its sole writer and writes only files. The actual impact is confined to results/group_reports: the caller fully controls the filename there (constrained to today's date prefix and a forced .md suffix, so it can overwrite a report saved earlier the same day) and traversal or NUL-byte input produces an unhandled 500. Fix is still worth applying as defense-in-depth and for consistency with the repo's F-06 convention — wrap with `_slugify_case_name(title, fallback='group_report')` for the path while keeping the raw title in the report body — but it is a hardening/robustness item, not an arbitrary-file-write vulnerability.

refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The auditor misread the scope of the "contradicting source", and the canonical data files refute the premise outright.

(1) structure_predictor.py does NOT "declare it will never export" the column. `FORBIDDEN` gates only that module's own *outputs*: the verdict table (`status()`, :118), prediction rows (`predict_structure()`, :152) and `response_surface()` (:238). The selftest the auditor quotes says exactly that — ':329 판정표에 use_porosity_pct 가 없다' and ':335 FORBIDDEN 열은 예측에 안 나온다'. Decisively, the SAME selftest deliberately writes `use_porosity_pct` INTO a corpus CSV fixture (:307-308 fieldnames, :316 `'use_porosity_pct': por[i] + rng.normal(0, 5)`) with the comment '★게이트된 열은 일부러 **오염**시킨다 — 새어나오면 안 되는 열이다'. The module's contract is "the column may exist upstream in data; it must not leak into a served prediction" — the opposite of what the claim asserts.

(2) The canonical committed data files carry the column AFTER the 2026-08-03 ruling. `docs/data/mpm_dem_porosity_reliability.csv` (the curated 105-case reliability ledger, `CURATED_DB` at design_performance_dataset.py:70) ends `...,regime,use_source,use_porosity_pct`. The actual ML training corpus `docs/data/design_performance_corpus.csv` — the very file structure_predictor.py names in its own "not trained" hint — contains `use_source` (col 276) and `use_porosity_pct` (col 277), populated in 235/291 rows, last written 2026-08-25 (7b65bfe64), three weeks after the ruling. design_performance_dataset.py:179-185 explicitly copies both verbatim from the curated CSV and warns '⚠ 재계산하지 않는다 … 그대로 쓰고 출처를 태그한다'. So "학습·노출 금지" cannot mean "no CSV may carry the column".

(3) The training script REQUIRES it: ml_design_structure.py keeps `('use_porosity_pct','lin')` in STRUCTURE_TARGETS (:66), and needs the column for `diagnose(split_by='use_source')` (:560-563, the autopsy that tests whether the gate itself is the defect) and `closure_audit` (:768, `for col in ('porosity','use_porosity_pct')`). CLAUDE.md's own numbers — 'REJECT 1 = use_porosity_pct .397' and '편향 0.124→0.007' — could not have been produced if the column were stripped from the corpus. The prohibition is on serving it as a usable prediction, not on it existing in data.

(4) The route is a raw ledger, not an ML artifact, and the column carries zero hidden information. Its docstring (app.py:7870-7879): 'No form / no grid extrapolation — this is the raw per-case corpus dump the list view already computes, exported flat.' The same row ships `dem_porosity_pct`, `mpm_porosity_pct`, `gap_dem_minus_mpm`, `regime` AND `use_source`; `use_por` is exactly `dem if (dem−mpm) > 4.0 else mpm` (:7959-7967) — reconstructible to the digit from the columns the auditor himself calls 'raw and honest'. Dropping it removes no information and would only hide which model the gate picked. docs/mpm_scaffold_reliability_and_am_freeze.md (the source CLAUDE.md cites) prescribes the opposite: 'porosity lock/clamp = 신뢰성 0 (조작). 정답은 clamp 가 아니라 regime-gate + DEM↔MPM 일치를 validity 증명서로 **노출**'.

(5) The claim also overreaches by bundling `use_source`: CLAUDE.md marks only `use_porosity_pct`. `use_source` is the gate label the reliability doc requires be exposed and that `diagnose(split_by='use_source')` depends on.

Minor detail: the blame SHA is also wrong — 4fdb58cc is 'harden mech-reaction + porosity routes'; the commit that added these two fields is ec8bb2911 (same day, 2026-07-20). Irrelevant either way, since the post-ruling corpus still carries them. The proposed action (drop the column) would break design_performance_dataset.py's verbatim-copy contract and ml_design_structure.py's diagnose/closure audit, for no information gain.

refuted_p0p1.claim: webapp/app.py is outside every discipline glob, and it holds the repository's only hardcoded model identifier plus an LLM section that writes unswept markdown into a directory no checker reads.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted: The finding is filed as a P1 quotation_ban_leak, and there is no leak. I added the auditor's exact proposed globs to BAN_SCAN_GLOBS in-memory and re-ran ban_sweep: 859 files x 22 patterns, 0 errors (baseline is 844 files, 0 errors). Both committed webapp/results/reports/*.md (scaling_law_report.md, scaling_law_report_full.md) match zero of the 22 quotation_ban patterns. The only banned strings anywhere in webapp/*.py are webapp/app.py:4025, 4031, 4033 -- all inside _RETR, the fail-closed retraction banner in /api/seminar/slides that refuses to serve the deck unless ?historical=1 and tells the user the SDCP numbers were retracted by the 2026-08-13 review. That is the remediation for CDXIJ-4, not a recurrence of it; the auditor read a correction banner as the error it corrects. The premise "outside every discipline glob" is also false in substance: .github/workflows/discipline.yml runs five webapp tests against app.py plus `node webapp/test_seminar_dom.mjs`, and webapp/test_seminar_page.py is explicitly the "철회 게이트 계약" contract -- it asserts /api/seminar/deck returns 403 JSON with retracted=true, that no pptx bytes (PK\x03\x04) escape in the refusal body, and it names the exact bypass it guards (`sed -i '…/    if False:/' webapp/app.py`); the DOM test proves its own sensitivity by re-running with the rejection branch deleted. The proposed remedy also misses its stated target: .gitignore:6 is `webapp/results/`, so /group/report output at app.py:6597 is never committed and absent from a CI checkout, meaning `webapp/**/*.md` would not sweep it where the sweep runs. Finally the model-id half is a category error inside a quotation_ban finding: claude-sonnet-4-20250514 is not one of the 22 registry patterns (all are numeric SDCP/plate values), CLAUDE.md scopes its rule to commits/PRs and wiki/tools/lint.py to wiki pages -- the auditor quotes both scopes and then treats the absence of an applicable rule as a violation -- and _generate_ai_analysis returns None with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (app.py:3500-3503) and again on ImportError, while CI installs only numpy/scipy/matplotlib/flask/requests.

summary: This scope is two very different halves. The *plumbing* — `webapp/pipeline_service.py` and `webapp/security.py` — is the healthiest code in the audit: pipeline_service encodes a genuine provenance contract (run_id + code_sha + atomic candidate publish + per-channel verdicts) that already implements the CL-75 "no SHA, no citation" rule, and security.py is fail-closed with a 28/28 passing self-test. The *scientific surface* is badly stale. Five separate user-facing routes still assert numbers and forms that canon retracted: the seminar retraction notice itself quotes the quotation-banned CL-33/CL-41 p1 plate-rule ratios (1.123/1.144/1.155) as "what we can currently say"; the per-case report exports the pre-T1 ionic scaling law as the "production model (n=57, LOOCV=0.979)"; `/scaling-report` regenerates a FORM X report that re-screens φ_c and declares 0.185 optimal, against the standing "NEVER re-screen φc" rule; the MPM-kit builder defaults and hard-whitelists STEP3 voxel to 0.4 µm and labels it "σ 검증값", making the manuscript's nominal `VOX=.15 / SDCP_SPHERE_D=.30` convention literally unreachable from the UI; and the case page shows the DEM↔MPM "cross-validated" porosity badge without the CL-04 caveat that commit 470c8c2d4 explicitly added to the list page one screen away. The structural cause is visible and provable: `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS` in `check_review_findings.py` covers `webapp/templates/*.html` and `webapp/static/js/*.js` but not `webapp/**/*.py`, so `--ban-sweep` returns "누수 없음" while `webapp/app.py:4035` renders banned values into the browser — the same false-green class the checker's own header documents as CDXIJ-4/9, one medium further along.

findings.claim: The SUS collector option shows the user the pristine measured R_int (~50 Ω·cm²) but bakes the cycled projected-literature value (150) into the kit, and its inline comment quotes a third pair of numbers (60/20) that appears nowhere in the canonical anchors CSV.
findings.evidence: single.html:263 `<option value="sus">이종기술 (SUS · 실측 R_int~50)</option>`. app.py:6923 `_rint = _rint_anchor_pair('sus')[1]` with the comment `# cycled 추정 60 (pristine 20 병기); 밴드 CSV note`; `_rint_anchor_pair` returns `(pristine, cycled)` (confirmed by `/rint-anchors` at L6650 zipping `('pristine','cycled')`), and executing `rint_cycle_traj.load_scenario('sus')` returns `(50.0, 150.0)` — so `[1]` = 150. docs/data/rint_eis_anchors.csv rows: `lab_sus_pristine … 50 … precision=measured … 실측 풀셀 평균 49.8` and `lab_sus_cycled … 150 … precision=projected_literature … ⚠문헌투영(assumed-form)`. The comment's 60/20 matches neither. app.py:6924 also sets `_cname = 'SUS_bare_estimated'`, tagging as 'estimated' the one row the CSV marks `measured`.

Make the UI label state which end is baked (e.g. `이종기술 (SUS · cycled 150 Ω·cm², 문헌투영; pristine 실측 50)`), and rename `_cname` so the measured pristine anchor is not labelled estimated. Decide whether the kit should bake pristine or cycled for SUS — the other three scenarios bake cycled, but only SUS advertises the pristine number, so the intended default needs an author call.

findings.claim: The retracted-value sweep does not scan webapp/**/*.py even though app.py composes user-facing retraction and status text server-side, so --ban-sweep reports zero leaks while the app renders banned values into the browser.
findings.evidence: BAN_SCAN_GLOBS covers `webapp/templates/*.html`, `webapp/static/js/*.js`, `webapp/**/*.json` but no `webapp/**/*.py`. Verified programmatically: `C._ban_files('.')` → `webapp py files scanned: []`, `'webapp/app.py' in rels` → False; and `python3 scripts/check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` → `철회값 누수 없음 ✓` while app.py:4035 carries `1.123/1.144/1.155`. Even a direct sweep of app.py returns 0 problems, because the registry patterns are the full-precision forms (`1.1232`, `1.143817`, `1.155448`) and `_ban_norm` strips trailing zeros but does not match a rounded prefix. The checker's own header declares the governing criterion — "**사용자에게 노출되는 산출물**을 전부 넣는다 (JSON 덱·러너 셸·덱 생성기)" — and app.py is such an output. This is the failure mode findings.json R5CX-06 already recorded: "`quotation_ban` 12개 패턴에 그 값들이 **없어서** `--ban-sweep` 이 rc 0 · '누수 없음' 을 낸다 … 정본은 밖으로 강제되지 않으면 새어나간다."
findings.proposed_action: Add `webapp/*.py` (or `webapp/**/*.py`) to BAN_SCAN_GLOBS and add a negative-control fixture asserting a banned string planted in a .py under webapp/ is caught. Separately, register the 3-decimal rounded forms `1.123`/`1.144`/`1.155` — or a numeric-tolerance matcher — so rounding is not an escape hatch; the current registry only stops verbatim copies.

findings.locator: L6, served verbatim as a download by webapp/app.py:10463–10469 (`/docs/full-report`); the sibling `/docs/formula-catalog` serves docs/Formula_Catalog.md
findings.claim: Two documents the app offers as downloads still declare FORM X the final ionic formula, three model generations after it was demoted to a legacy fallback.
findings.evidence: docs/Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md:6 `**Final Formula**: FORM X — σ = C × σ_grain × (φ_SE - φc)^¾ × CN × √cov / √τ`; docs/Formula_Catalog.md L34 marks `σ_brug × C × (G_path × GB_d²)^(1/4) × CN²  R²=0.940 ★ v3 champion`. Both last committed 2026-04-24 (660600a44). Contradicted by CLAUDE.md: "**FORM X (v4++)** … is the OLDER, inferior model — kept only as a legacy toggle / predictor fallback", and by the T1 production section (LOOCV ≈ 0.975, n=88, φc_P/φc_S frozen at 0.200/0.195).
findings.proposed_action: Add a head banner to both files naming CLAUDE.md's T1 / Stage 22.5 / Stage T1 sections as the superseding canon (the banner must point at the ledger to earn a whole-file exemption under BAN_BANNER_ANCHORS), and have the two routes emit that banner in the response as well so a downloaded copy carries it.

findings.locator: L659 vs L1437 vs L5780 vs L7478 vs L8473 — the `scale` key
findings.claim: The same per-case `scale` convention key has two different documented defaults in the same file (1000 and 1), so a case whose meta.json and input_params.json both lack the key renders its box dimensions and its RVE cross-section area a factor 10^6 apart on one page.
findings.evidence: app.py:657-659 `# Box dimensions — stored in sim units; convert to μm via scale (default 1000).` / `scale = ip.get('scale') or 1000`. app.py:1435-1437 `# RVE cross-section: box_x × box_y × scale² → μm². scale comes from case.scale` / `scale = input_params.get('scale') or 1`. app.py:5780 `input_params['scale'] = meta.get('scale', 1)`; app.py:8473 `scale = meta.get('scale', 1) or 1`; app.py:7478 `scale = meta.get('scale', 1000)`. Both consumers read the same input_params.json for the same case, and both results are shown on `/single` — `_input_box_x/_input_box_y` from the 1000 branch and `A_RVE = … μm²` (app.py:1451) from the 1 branch. `/upload` always writes meta['scale'], so the divergence is reachable only for archive-migrated or hand-authored meta.json, which `/single` explicitly supports via `_resolve_results_dir`.
findings.proposed_action: Introduce a single `_case_scale(meta, input_params)` helper with one documented default and route all five call sites through it; failing that, make the missing-key case explicit ('scale 미기록') rather than silently picking a default, since the two silent defaults differ by 1000×.

findings.claim: A warning-suppression toggle rewrites full_metrics.json with a plain truncating json.dump and records no provenance, contradicting the atomic-write and generation-stamping discipline that the same codebase applies to every other write of that file.
findings.evidence: app.py:7834-7835 `with open(metrics_path, 'w') as f:` / `json.dump(metrics, f, indent=2, default=str)`. webapp/pipeline_service.py:829-830 defines `atomic_write_json` precisely for this — "같은 디렉터리 temp → fsync → os.replace(재시도). 부분 쓰기/truncate 를 막는다 (F-10)" — and app.py calls it for full_metrics.json at L2952, 3012, 3116, 3129 and 5459. The route also stores only a bare type string in `disabled_warnings` (no who/when/why), while `_refresh_post_network_warnings` (app.py:2754) then silently filters those warnings out of the metrics the case page and the exported report read. The route takes no network lock and no candidate/publish path.
findings.proposed_action: Switch to `_ps.atomic_write_json`, and store suppressions as records (`{type, at, note}`) rather than bare strings so a suppressed validity warning leaves a trace in the artifact — the same 'a banner explains a file, it does not fix a cell' concern applied to a mutation that is invisible afterwards.

findings.locator: L5857–5861 in `_load_mpm_metrics`, executed on every `/single/<case_id>` render
findings.claim: A plain GET page render rewrites the case's mpm_metrics.json non-atomically as a cache side effect, so an interrupted page load can truncate a persisted result file.
findings.evidence: app.py:5858-5861 `with open(small, 'w') as f:` / `json.dump(out, f)               # 병합 캐시 — 재스캔 방지`, wrapped in a bare `except Exception: pass`. Contradicted by pipeline_service.py:829-830 (`atomic_write_json` … "부분 쓰기/truncate 를 막는다 (F-10)") which app.py already uses for the analogous writes. This also makes `/single` a state-mutating GET, which security.py's `_PROTECTED_GET_ENDPOINTS` (security.py:64-72) treats as the category needing protection — `serve_3d_data` and `serve_2d_export_zip` are listed there for exactly 'lazy cache write', `single` is not.
findings.proposed_action: Use `_ps.atomic_write_json` for the merge cache, and either add `single` to `_PROTECTED_GET_ENDPOINTS` or move the merge out of the render path.

findings.claim: The comment claims the AST scan exhaustively catches every subprocess-running GET route and is therefore 'the real defense line', but the scanner matches only literal `subprocess.<attr>` calls in the route body, and the repo already contains subprocess calls it cannot see.
findings.evidence: security.py:60-63: "`test_security_phase_a.py` 가 app.py 를 **AST 로 전수 스캔**해서 subprocess 를 도는 GET-only 라우트가 전부 여기 있는지 검사한다 — 목록이 아니라 그 테스트가 실제 방어선이다." test_security_phase_a.py:132-135 matches on `getattr(x.func.value, 'id', '') == 'subprocess'` within the route FunctionDef only. app.py:4890 and 4899 call `_sp.run(...)` after `import subprocess as _sp`, and app.py:4942 does the same inside the helper `_eis_python` — none of which the scanner can match. These survive today only because the calling route is POST (covered by the write rule), not because the scanner saw them. This is the CLAUDE.md rule ⑤ pattern: "**후보를 고르는 코드가 곧 사각지대다**" — select by real behaviour, not by a name.
findings.proposed_action: Broaden the scan to resolve aliased `import subprocess as X` and to follow one level of helper calls, or invert it: assert that every GET route either appears in `_PROTECTED_GET_ENDPOINTS` or is annotated read-only. Until then, soften the comment from '전수 스캔 / 실제 방어선' to what it actually checks.

findings.claim: The AM_P/AM_S auto-detection compares the raw dump radius against a hardcoded 0.004 sim-unit threshold while the very same request accepts and stores a user-settable `scale`, so any case uploaded with a scale other than 1000 is mis-typed.
findings.evidence: app.py:5140 `scale = request.form.get('scale', '1000')` and L5200 `'scale': int(scale)` — the scale is a request-controlled per-case convention. app.py:5185-5186 `# sim r > 0.004 → AM_P (6μm), else AM_S (2μm)` / `am_type_name = 'AM_P' if r > 0.004 else 'AM_S'` — the threshold is fixed in sim units and never divided by, or multiplied with, `scale`. Every other consumer honours the stored scale (app.py:659, 1437, 7478, 8473, 9636, 9797). With scale=1 (a dump already in µm) both 2 µm and 6 µm radii exceed 0.004 and every type-1 particle is labelled AM_P.
findings.proposed_action: Derive the threshold from the stored scale (`4.0 / scale`) or refuse auto-detection when `scale != 1000`, so the auto-type-map cannot silently disagree with the scale the case records.

findings.locator: L1–10, module docstring; invoked by `/upload` at webapp/app.py:5209
findings.claim: The module states its purpose is persisting data across Render redeploys, a deployment that was retired a month before its last edit.
findings.evidence: storage_sync.py:3-4 `Keeps uploads/, results/, archive/ synced with Supabase Storage so data persists across Render redeploys.` Contradicted by webapp/security.py:9-11: "★ 2026-08-07: 사용자가 **클라우드 배포를 폐지**해 `render.yaml` 을 삭제했다 (웹앱은 로컬 `run_dem5002.sh` :5002 전용)", and `git log --all -- render.yaml` shows commit 79fd69503 "클라우드 배포 폐지 — render.yaml 삭제 + 죽은 URL 정리"; `ls render.yaml` → no such file. storage_sync.py itself was last touched 2026-08-25 (a5c0a9bf3) without updating the rationale.
findings.proposed_action: Restate the purpose as off-machine backup/mirror for the local runner, and note that the server still holds a Supabase service-role key (security.py:7) so the credential's blast radius is unchanged by the cloud retirement.

findings.locator: `_TRUST_LEDS` refs at L129, L148, L160, L167, L177; also webapp/templates/audit.html:14

findings.claim: The seminar page never sends ?historical=1, so the deck view is unreachable from the UI and the page's deck tab renders only a refusal — the fail-closed gate has no matching opt-in affordance.

findings.claim: A generated scaling-law report from 2026-04-13 built from zero cases is committed to the repo and carries the FORM X / φ_c=0.185 claims.
findings.evidence: File header: `**Generated**: 2026-04-13 23:36` / `**Data**: 0 cases from results + archive`; L65 `| **FORM X** | **C × σ_grain × (φ-φc)^¾ × CN × √cov / √τ** | **0.944** |`; L94 `| **0.185** | **0.944** ← **최적** |`. Committed 2026-04-24 (660600a44). Contradicted by the same CLAUDE.md passages cited in the `/scaling-report` finding. Its sibling webapp/results/reports/scaling_law_report_full.md is also tracked.

surface_worthy.why: This is the repo's most complete working implementation of the 'provenance or it didn't happen' rule the ledger now treats as standing law (CL-75: measurement JSONs must carry the code SHA). It stamps every network generation with run_id + code_sha + input digests, runs Stage E in a copy-on-write candidate directory that is atomically published only after content verification, holds a cross-process file lock, and rolls back on failure. It is buried in a 950-line module docstring and nothing outside webapp/ points at it.
surface_worthy.one_line: The working reference implementation of generation-stamped, atomically-published, verify-before-publish measurement outputs — the pattern the GPU-run tracks are trying to reach by hand.

surface_worthy.why: `_CHANNEL_OK_STATES` (L546–556) is the only place in the codebase that writes down which 'no result' outcomes are physically correct answers versus solver failures: electronic no_result = AM network not percolating = correct; ionic no_result = SE not percolating = correct; thermal no_result = suspicious because it uses all contacts. That distinction is a scientific convention with named case evidence (1mAh_100_4, 1mAh_8_S1–S4, 2mAh_real_16, 8mAh_real_11) and it lives only in a Python constant.
surface_worthy.one_line: The convention that σ_e = 0 (AM non-percolating) and σ_i = 0 (SE non-percolating) are correct answers, not failures — with the case list that establishes it.

surface_worthy.why: Line 130 holds the exact canonical phrasing of the MPM-porosity reservation ('정본 유보 … DEM↔MPM 일치를 validity 증명서로 읽지 말 것 — 씨앗이 정답을 인코딩해 순환이다'), added by commit 470c8c2d4 in response to a direct user correction. It is the wording every other surface needs and it is currently trapped inside a ~4,000-character Jinja `title=` attribute on one table cell, where it is neither greppable in prose nor reusable.
surface_worthy.one_line: The canonical one-paragraph statement of why DEM↔MPM porosity agreement is circular — worth lifting out of an HTML tooltip into canon prose.

surface_worthy.why: L4013–4048 (`/api/seminar/slides`, `/api/seminar/deck`) implement a reusable pattern the repo needs more of: a retracted artifact that fail-closes by default, requires an explicit `?historical=1` to release, and — critically — returns `evidence_ref` + `evidence_claim` so the refusal names the ledger entry a reader can check (`docs/reviews/claims.json`, `CL-24`). That is the machine-checkable form of 'a banner must point at the ledger'.
surface_worthy.one_line: A refusal that cites its own ledger evidence — the reusable template for gating any retracted artifact behind an explicit historical opt-in.

surface_worthy.why: The module docstring records an operational fact with real consequences that is documented nowhere else: cloud deployment was retired on 2026-08-07 (render.yaml deleted), so the auth gate is now defense-in-depth rather than a release blocker — but the server still holds a Supabase service-role key, and `/download-doc/<path:filename>` serves from the repo root. Anyone re-exposing the app (LAN, ngrok, redeploy) needs this paragraph and would not find it.
surface_worthy.one_line: Why the webapp auth gate is off by default, what it protects, and the standing condition under which it must be turned on.

surface_worthy.why: L7322–7355 (`/mpm-lab/mech-reaction/<pid>.csv`) emits the raw, z-controlled (partial) and within-slice correlations side by side under an explicit OBSERVATIONAL header stating there is no stress→reaction coupling. It is the cleanest in-repo example of the discipline the ledger enforces on claims — separating a confounded correlation from the genuine one instead of reporting a single number — and it is hidden inside a CSV export route.
surface_worthy.one_line: A worked example of confound-controlled reporting in code: raw vs z-controlled vs within-slice correlation, all three shipped together.

surface_worthy.why: L683–687 carries the only user-facing statement that the predictor's CV_R² is not on the same scale as the nested structure-predictor R² — kernel selection is not nested (max-of-6 optimism) and scaler_X/scaler_y are fitted before the fold split (standardisation leak), so the two must not be compared by magnitude. I verified the leak is real in predictor_engine.py (X_scaled built before kf.split). This is a correct, current caveat sitting in a JavaScript string.
surface_worthy.one_line: Why the predictor's reported CV_R² is optimistic and must never be compared side by side with the nested structure-predictor scores.

surface_worthy.why: Part 1.2 (L67–81) already documents the three-run decomposition FULL / CONTACT_FREE / CONSTRICTION_ONLY, names σ_cf an upper bound, and states that constriction dominates 70–80 % of the resistance. That is precisely the material CL-81 made canonical on 2026-09-08 — the framing has been sitting in the webapp's report generator since April. Surfacing it is worthwhile, but only this section: the rest of the file is superseded (see the P0 finding), so it should be lifted into docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md rather than cited from where it sits.
surface_worthy.one_line: The FULL / CONTACT_FREE / CONSTRICTION_ONLY decomposition and the 70–80 % constriction share — CL-81's framing, already written down five months earlier in a now-stale file.

surviving_p0p1.locator: L4031–4038, inside `api_seminar_slides` (`/api/seminar/slides`) — the `_RETR` string, rendered to the browser by seminar.html:251

refuted_p0p1.claim: The historical deck path reproduces the exact defect the 2026-08-20 server fix says it closed: app.py sets `data['retracted_banner']`, but seminar.html never reads it, so a viewer who passes ?historical=1 sees the retracted slides with no retraction banner — and slide 12 carries a green '✓ 방어 가능한 결과' badge calling the vox 0.4 grid an 'operational calibration'.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The claim's central premise — "a viewer who passes ?historical=1 sees the retracted slides with no retraction banner" — is not reachable, and the auditor misread the delivered fix as its own absence.

(1) THE UI CANNOT PASS ?historical=1. seminar.html:367 is the only consumer of the endpoint (`grep -rn 'seminar/slides' webapp/ --include=*.html --include=*.js` returns exactly that one line plus the route def), and it is a hardcoded `fetch('/api/seminar/slides')` with no query string. `grep -n 'location.search|URLSearchParams|searchParams' webapp/templates/seminar.html` returns NOTHING — the page reads no URL parameters at all, so a `?historical=1` on the page URL is never propagated to the API. The historical branch is therefore reachable only by hitting `/api/seminar/slides?historical=1` directly, which returns raw JSON in which `"retracted": true` and the full `retracted_banner` prose are plainly visible text, not hidden markup. There is no rendering path in which slides appear without the banner.

(2) THE AUDITOR READ THE FIX AS THE DEFECT. Because the UI never sends the flag, the server's fail-closed branch (app.py:4037-4041) always fires for the page, and `renderDeck()`'s `!deckData.ok` branch (seminar.html:248-256) renders exactly the retraction: `deckData.error` (the `_RETR` text), `deckData.hint`, and an `evidence_ref` source chip pointing at `docs/reviews/claims.json` with `evidence_claim` = "CL-24". That is the 2026-08-20 fix working as designed. The auditor's own evidence quote — that `renderDeck()` "branches only on deckData.ok — which is True in the historical path" — skips that this branch is the one the browser actually takes. Repo contract tests assert both halves: checks 1-6c (default = ok:False, retracted marker, reason, evidence pointer) and 18-23 (historical=1 = ok:True WITH `retracted_banner` len>40).

(3) EVEN IN THE HISTORICAL JSON, THE BANNER IS SLIDE 1 AND RENDERS FIRST. `docs/seminar/seminar_deck.json` now has n_slides=15, and slide n=1 is the retraction slide: title "격자(vox)를 조이면 전자 헤드라인이 계속 내려가고 이온 이득은 부호가 뒤집힌다." with `extra` = ["⛔ HISTORICAL — 인용 금지", …, "정본 = docs/reviews/claims.json (CL-24 · CL-33 · CL-41)"]. `cur = 0` at seminar.html:157, so the first thing `slideHtml()` would draw is that banner, via the normal kicker/title/eyebrow path. This is the CLAUDE.md-documented remedy ("배너를 1번 장으로 앞에 끼운다").

(4) THE "SLIDE 12 GREEN BADGE" ASSERTION IS FACTUALLY WRONG AS A RENDERED OUTPUT. `slideHtml()` (which applies FLAGS) is called from exactly one site, seminar.html:260, inside `renderDeck()` AFTER the `!deckData.ok` early return — so FLAGS is dead code in the browser. Worse for the claim, FLAGS was written 2026-08-11 (commit 6b7f8aad3, before the banner slide was prepended) and is keyed on `s.n`; the +1 shift means FLAGS[12] no longer maps to the slide the auditor describes at all — n=12 is now "SDCP is explicit geometry, not an EMT correction", and the content the auditor quotes sits on n=13.

(5) NOT A BAN-REGISTRY LEAK. `python3 scripts/check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` (22 patterns × 844 files) reports "철회값 누수 없음 ✓"; seminar.html contains no banned string, and the retracted figures that DO appear in `_RETR`/`_RETRACTED` pass because they are inside an explicit retraction banner — restating them there is the intended behaviour.

RESIDUAL (P3 hygiene at most, different in kind from the claim): the FLAGS map is stale dead code keyed to pre-banner slide numbering, and its 12-entry text ("✓ 방어 가능한 결과 … 0.4 µm 격자는 operational calibration") would be wrong if the map were ever revived. Deleting FLAGS is reasonable cleanup. But it is not a live contradiction, no viewer can see it, and it does not "reproduce the exact defect the server fix closed."

summary: The SR-01 block is 215 lines of layered retraction history and it is the single most out-of-date governing text in the repo. git blame shows 52 lines untouched since 2026-08-13, the bulk from 2026-08-18/20/21, one edit on 2026-08-25 (R5-CX-06) and one on 2026-09-03 (CL-61) — nothing since. In the same window the ledger added CL-60, CL-70, CL-72, CL-74, CL-75, CL-81, CL-82–87 and released CL-38 from hold; the section cites none of them (highest id cited: CL-61; `centerline`, `p2-occupied-surface-first`, Phase A, and every SELF-* finding are absent). Structurally the section is honest about what is banned but leaks anyway: lines 186/195 print the registry-banned `+12.3 %` as a live headline, and the ban sweep passes only because `BAN_NEAR_MARKS` contains the bare token `'CL-'`, which occurs within ±2 lines of nearly every sentence here — the machine check is effectively disarmed inside this exact section. Worse, line 77 instructs the manuscript to write "비 = 1.123", a truncation that no registry pattern matches, five lines after line 72 says that value's citation is forbidden. Three registered experiments (CL-40 STEP 3, CL-48 σ_VGCF single-fibre probe, and the sphere-stamp grid sweep) are presented as pending or non-converged although all three completed and were judged between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-02, so a reader would re-spend GPU time on finished work. Two conclusions the section states as current are directly refuted by live ledger entries: "어떤 보고값도 이 축에서 하한" (CL-72, retracted 2026-09-07, and self-contradicted by the section's own lines 47–48) and "계단 인자 k 는 격자 무관이 아니다" (CL-29, live since 2026-08-16). What survives and is worth keeping is genuinely valuable — the shape result (monotone, incremental ratio 1.773 below the 2.187 power-law floor), the CL-44/CL-45 volume-channel pair measured at both ends of the grid, the `d/vox ≥ 2` planning constraint, the CL-61 SDCP-anchor retraction, and the raw-measurement block — but all of it sits below three stacked ⛔ blocks at the bottom of a 215-line wall.

findings.proposed_action: Strike the trailing "어떤 보고값도 이 축에서 하한이다" clause and paste CL-72's agreed manuscript sentence in its place: "Grid convergence was not demonstrated; behavior below 0.15 µm and the sign of the continuum error remain unknown. findings.claim: The "priority defect = exactly 0 cells" result is stated unconditionally, but its stated cause (`sigma_ptfe` default 0 ⇒ PTFE never stamped) no longer describes the code, and PTFE *is* stamped under the convention the manuscript actually reports.

Contradicting source (code): scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py L1547 now reads `_cond_ph = ((2, 3, 5, 6, 4) if a._ptfe_stamp != 'off' …)` — the gate is `_ptfe_stamp`, not `sigma_ptfe`; L963 states "게이트만 분리하면 `--ptfe-stamp centerline --sigma-ptfe 0` = **exact-zero DOF** 다", i.e. PTFE is stamped with σ = 0. The old gate survives only as a regression fixture (L383–384 `_old_gate`, selftest `ptfe-gate-split ★ _cond_ph 가 σ 가 아니라 규약으로 갈린다 (옛 결함 회귀)`). The 0-cell measurement itself (claims.json CL-37: "구 추가 435,488 셀의 원래 상: … **PTFE 0 · SWCNT 0**") was taken with PTFE unstamped.
findings.proposed_action: Qualify the sentence: "우선순위 결함 크기 = 0 셀 **(PTFE 미스탬프 규약에서 측정)**", and add that under the reported `--ptfe-stamp centerline` convention PTFE occupies cells and the overwrite count is unmeasured. Fix the parenthetical to name `--ptfe-stamp`, not `sigma_ptfe`, as the gate.

findings.claim: The bullet headline asserts "the staircase factor k is not grid-independent" on the strength of three legacy values, but the live ledger entry that adjudicated exactly this says the opposite — the spread was the discarded estimator's short-run bias plus a population mismatch.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md L44: "· ⚠ **계단 인자 k 는 격자 무관이 아니다** — 1.4855@0.4 · 1.4917@0.3 · 1.4461@0.25."  Contradicting source: docs/reviews/claims.json CL-29 (2026-08-16, `status: live`) — claim: "실침대 k 의 격자 산포(0.046)는 **estimator 의 짧은-구간 편향**으로 설명된다 — \"k 가 격자에 의존한다\" 는 아직 성립하지 않는다"; verdict: "같은 점 구름에 estimator 를 고치고 모집단을 고정하면 폭이 **0.0456 → 0.0063 = 7.2배 축소**되고, 남는 것은 단조 수렴이다: 1.4859 → 1.4915 → 1.4922 … ⇒ **k → 1.492** … \"k 는 격자 무관이 아니다\" 는 **성립하지 않는다**."  The corrected triple never appears in CLAUDE.md, and CL-29 further scopes the answer: "**k = 1.492 는 \"측정가능 모집단 한정, 전류-가중 미정의\" 스코프로만 인용할 것.**"
findings.proposed_action: Reverse the headline to CL-29's finding, keep the estimator defect as the standing lesson (`np.unique` discarded path order), record the corrected triple 1.4859/1.4915/1.4922 (width 0.0063–0.011, not 0.046) with CL-29's citation scope, and keep the existing L47–48 prohibition on using k as a bound.

The file's own `--sigma-ptfe` help text (L953) still reads "default 0 = production: PTFE는 전도 격자에 아예 미스탬프". summary: This scope holds two live tracks and a large tail of 2026-06/07 MPM documentation that the 2026-08-04→2026-09-08 platen work overturned. The good news first: the canon itself is now current — `mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md` finally has rev7 (2026-09-02, R1 reflected) plus §7-7 (2026-09-03), the SE-curve verdict doc is complete through §⑩, the Phase A prereg has done the honest thing (registered W4 blind, scored four predictions, recorded two of its own wrong guesses), and the wiki d_h pages are actually fresher than CLAUDE.md. The ban sweep is green, which is exactly the point: every defect found here is a semantic contradiction no checker can see. The bad news is that the derived layer never followed the canon. `mpm3d_calibration.md` — the file CLAUDE.md names as the "Full record" for the 3D MPM — has not been touched since 2026-07-21 and still calls the platen-artifact porosity "the milestone", still tells readers to use the `porosity@target` field the canon calls false, and still sells the 512 grid convergence as a model-trust bound; `mpm_scaffold_reliability_and_am_freeze.md` (2026-08-03, one day before the defect was found) still sells DEM↔MPM agreement as a validity certificate even though the canon's own §11 has listed that exact fix since rev2; `porosity_regression_final.md` is CLOSED with 123 of 129 production targets taken from the contaminated scaffold porosity; and `wiki/frame4` states two retracted claims at `confidence: high`. CLAUDE.md itself is mostly well-corrected but carries three self-contradictions the reader will act on: it says the canon is stuck at rev6 (it is not), it budgets 12 GPU runs for the d_h equalization its own track list and the canon both put at 8, and it asserts a |slope| ≥ 0.663 lower bound that its own newer lines (−0.575 / −0.596) violate. Underneath all of it is one structural gap: CLAUDE.md still frames the platen freeze as a defect awaiting a fix, while CL-80/CL-85 and the Phase A prereg have promoted it to the repo's standing Grade-B convention and stated that fixing it would invalidate — not rescue — the campaign now running on it.

surface_worthy.why: This is the whole track's punchline and it sits at line 898 of a 976-line file, behind a head banner that tells the reader the file is stale. It converts a puzzling result into a predictable one: the frozen-AM scaffold is configured so that the SE sits exactly on its own yield surface at the target, so J2 volume-preserving flow can only stop at geometric jam. Anyone designing the next scaffold run needs this before anything else.
surface_worthy.one_line: rev7 §7-3: σ_y(SE) = target = 0.30 GPa and frozen AM carries zero load, so full densification to ~1 % is this configuration's necessity, not an anomaly.

surface_worthy.why: rev7 §7-1 removes an item that several documents and the wiki still list as an open blocker — the stress-control servo did converge and held target for 50 frames, so the stop criterion does not need redesigning; what looked like slippage was inertia mixed into the moving readout. Surfacing it stops the next session from re-opening a closed question.
surface_worthy.one_line: rev7 §7-1: the stop-criterion redesign is retracted — the servo held 0.3003 ± 0.0002 for 50 frames; the frame-265 crossing was the inflated moving readout.

surface_worthy.why: The single most reusable rule the track produced, currently buried in rev6 §31 under an am-jam review. It tells you what a scaffold run can and cannot testify to, and it is the reason four separate 'cross-validation' claims collapsed. Every future scaffold result should be reported against it.
surface_worthy.one_line: rev6 §31: in a scaffold run `solid_vol` is fixed at seeding, so porosity is arithmetic on the DEM input — the only falsifiable MPM output is the stress-stop thickness.

surface_worthy.why: Two audit findings that live in a preregistration's §10 and therefore never reached the documents that need them: the convention offset is 946.66/(A·h), not a constant, and it applies only to the --se-dump path — applying it to cell-fill double-counts. It also voids the tidy explanation CLAUDE.md still gives for the 512 result. Five files currently use the constant.
surface_worthy.one_line: prereg §10-2/§10-3: ε_sphere = ε_MPM − 946.66/(A·h)·100, se-dump only; the 384↔512 '+1.2 %p = 1.251 %p offset' match is a coincidence on a cell-fill run.

surface_worthy.why: The most consequential recent result in this scope and it exists only inside a campaign preregistration. It settles what the MPM compaction step actually contributes on dilated beds (nothing geometric), fixes the sentence Phase A is allowed to publish, and states the counter-intuitive dependency that must be recorded before anyone 'fixes' the platen.
surface_worthy.one_line: §W1-정본대조: final thickness = seed × λ in 5/5 runs (≤0.17 %) ⇒ MPM compaction is geometrically a no-op, and repairing the frozen press invalidates Phase A rather than rescuing it.

surface_worthy.why: The cleanest one-line proof that a metric everyone reads as 'how well did it compact' measures nothing about the bed — same bed, pressure ×9.6, and it came out 0.2 µm thicker, with the thickness residual shrinking 11× as pressure rose. It belongs next to every scaffold porosity number the repo reports.
surface_worthy.one_line: CL-82 ① / CL-83 W4-e: reached pressure and bed state are decoupled — `settled_over_target` does not measure the bed.

surface_worthy.why: A small methodological rule that flipped the d_h verdict from 'weak' to 'holds' (R² 0.844 → 0.926 on identical data) purely by choosing the common φ better. It generalises to any single-point-per-bed comparison in this repo, and right now it is one line in §⑩.
surface_worthy.one_line: §⑩: put the common φ at the median landing of the single-point beds, so every bed gets the same small correction instead of one bed getting a 7×-threshold extrapolation.

surface_worthy.why: A pre-run gate that costs nothing — computable from the scaffold CSV with no GPU — and that quantifies when SE stress can be trusted. It also records the sign surprise that under-resolved constrictions vanish from the grid and make σ read low, which is the opposite of most people's intuition.
surface_worthy.one_line: §⑤ practical rule: d_h/dx = (V_free/S_AM)/dx ≳ 3.5 before the run, else raise the grid or label the result a lower bound (3.43 cells → +4.0 %, 1.18 cells → +23.8 %).

surface_worthy.why: One docstring line settles a provenance question that two documents currently get wrong and that blocks the R2.5-v2 and R3 runs. It should be quoted wherever f_AM appears, because the difference between 0.847 and 0.670 changes the stop threshold by more than the effect being measured.
surface_worthy.one_line: :208 — Hertz(AM-AM) 0.847 over-estimates the measured AM-AM 0.670 (phase-virial 0.809); 0.847 is the banned reconstruction, not a Love-Weber measurement.

surface_worthy.why: The defect severity is a ladder in bed height, not a yes/no, and rev5 added the counter-intuitive second axis: once CFL binds dt, finer grids strike harder too (512 = 1.31×, 768 = 1.97×). Together these two tables tell you in advance whether a planned run is in the mild or the supersonic regime, and they explain why one grid-convergence claim has to be re-run at matched Mach.
surface_worthy.one_line: §16 + rev5 §28(a): platen severity scales with bed height (real_14 V/c_S 0.80 subsonic vs P:S kit 3.05 supersonic) and with grid fineness once CFL binds dt.

summary: The frame block is the repo's controlling epistemology and it is the least-audited text in the repo: the 2026-08-20 exhaustive audit (FA-01..06) swept for retracted *numbers* and never looked at retracted *claims*, so frame[3]/[4]/[5] and three wiki pages still assert, unmarked, six claims the ledger carries as `rejected` (CDX-12/13/16/17/18/23/24, all dated 2026-08-12). The newest addition — the CL-81 precision note of 2026-09-08 — is itself internally incoherent in two ways: (a) it sits five lines below an un-marked 2026-08-11 paragraph ("복셀 FV 로 독립적인 두 번째 σ … 다른 이산화의 독립 측정") that CL-81, CDX-23/24, `network_conductivity.py`'s own docstring and `step3_sigma.py`'s thermal provenance all refute across all three channels; and (b) its last actionable line ("미실행 1순위 … 같은 침대에 두 이산화가 이미 있다, GPU 불요") is the exact sentence CL-81's verdict retracted three hours later in commit `aeb85f1e2` — a commit that touched **only** `claims.json`, leaving both CLAUDE.md and the brand-new canon doc carrying the refuted cost claim. That is CLAUDE.md rule ④'s own failure mode reproduced inside the block that states it. The 작업 규율 block is factually accurate about the three things it names (ban-sweep globs, rule J, rule M, SE_PROXY, CI `fetch-depth: 0`, `context_budget --extract` refusal — all verified by running them), but it names 3 of the 15 rules (A-O) and 2 of the 6 `check_*.py`, and the newest rule (O, US spelling, CI-blocking) cites "CLAUDE.md 상시 규약" for a convention that `git log -S'철자' -- CLAUDE.md` proves has never been in CLAUDE.md. Its own instrument contradicts its ③ headline (measured 54,879 tok vs the stated ~41k) and classifies the frame block itself as the #1 extraction candidate. The wiki nav block routes readers to a layer dormant since 2026-08-12 (log's last entry, 0/21 verified) whose frame pages carry the rejected claims. Nothing verified here leaks a `quotation_ban` string — `check_review_findings.py` exits 0 — which is precisely the point: the enforcement that exists is number-shaped and the damage in this scope is claim-shaped.

refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The finding's central assertion — that frame[4] states "agreement = cross-validation" with no condition — is produced by truncating both quoted passages one clause short of the condition. CLAUDE.md:313-315 is ONE sentence: "Do NOT calibrate one model to the other — calibrate each INDEPENDENTLY to experiment, then compare.  Agreement = cross-validation"; the auditor quoted from the em-dash onward. frame[4] (:367-372) is titled "**[4] Epistemology — DO NOT cross-fit DEM and MPM**", opens with the precondition "Each model is calibrated to EXPERIMENT independently", and closes with the exclusion "Forcing DEM↔MPM agreement (e.g. tuning MPM σ_y to match DEM Heckel-derived σ_y_eff) is circular." The auditor quoted :368-369 and stopped at :369, omitting :370-372. The condition is in the paragraph.

Second, the exhibit is corrected in place, same-day. The auditor cites :407 ("다른 이산화의 독립 측정") as surviving uncorrected, but :412-432 — the immediately following paragraph — is "★★★ 정밀화 2026-09-08 (CL-81) — 복셀 σ 는 접촉망의 CONTACT_FREE 가지 위에 있다", which reclassifies exactly that pair as the contact network's own idealized branch (network_conductivity.py:16 labels it "CONTACT_FREE: R_constriction=0 → σ_cf (upper bound, ideal contact limit)"), quantifies it (R_brug_over_full median 4.04×/6.69×, n=157, range 2.3–13.6×), warns "상대비교도 자동으로 안전하지 않다", and mandates a citation convention. That is bounds/direction:upper stated in prose, inside the frame block. The auditor's own PROPOSED ACTION cites CL-81 as the authority for the reclassification while grading the paragraph CL-81 corrects.

Third, the causal justification is false and the proposed remedy cannot produce the effect claimed for it. Neither checker reads frame prose: check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep matches literal strings from claims.json's quotation_ban registry (:181, :323) and has no relation vocabulary; check_method_discipline.py check_convention_parity (:377-450) validates the DIAGNOSTICS registry's own fields and never opens CLAUDE.md. Moreover the `bounds` branch the auditor proposes to use is `if d.get("direction") not in ("upper","lower"): errs.append(...)` then `continue` — it skips every substantive check. Registering the network↔voxel pair as bounds/upper would validate one enum value and would still never inspect CLAUDE.md:407. So "the empty frame[4] branch is why the wording survived the ban-sweep and CI" is wrong.

Fourth, category error in the registry proposal. DIAGNOSTICS is scoped by its own header to 규칙 A 규약 패리티 (D4): a diagnostic READER versus the voxel solver it purports to describe, verified by AST/behavioral probe of ndimage.label (label_site/label_fn) plus adjacency/vox_um/periodic/grid_source. network_conductivity.py is a contact-network Kirchhoff solver on DEM spheres — no voxel grid, no ndimage.label, no adjacency convention — and CLAUDE.md:408-410 explicitly states the two are separate production pipelines, not diagnostic-and-subject. Registering it is a scope expansion proposal, not a missing entry.

Independently confirmed as correct but non-load-bearing: checker L62-68 and L404-412 read as quoted; DIAGNOSTICS has exactly two entries, both relation 'diagnoses'; no independent_measurement entry exists; 38 claims carry non-null shared_input (68 carry the key, 30 explicit null). Residual, at most cosmetic: frame[4]'s stated condition guards cross-FITTING, whereas the checker's shared_input guards a different mechanism (a shared input path that forces agreement absent any cross-fit).
