refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
Every leg of the claim fails against the actual files.

(1) NO SCOPE DIVERGENCE. The auditor says CLAUDE.md states the exemption at track scope while "the canon scopes it to the SE–SE face only". False. docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md:200 opens with the track-scope headline "⚠ **Phase A 는 영향 없다** (근거):" and :202 gives the per-face ground. CLAUDE.md:433-434 has the identical two-part structure and carries the same ground clause in the same sentence ("⇒ SE–SE 면에 전자 전류가 없다"). The auditor quoted :202 (the ground) and omitted :200 (the headline) — the exact sentence they allege is absent from the canon.

(2) THE LEDGER IS VERBATIM THE SAME. docs/reviews/claims.json CL-81 (status "live", the binding registry; repo rule: 원장이 정본) ends its verdict with: "⚠ **Phase A 는 영향 없다** — `--no-ion` 전자 전용이고 `electronic_sigma_table()` 의 `SE(6)` 기본 0.0, `sid 9 (SE_blk)` 고정 0 ⇒ SE–SE 면에 전자 전류가 흐르지 않는다.  ⛔ 그러나 이 면제를 **이온 축으로 옮기지 말 것**." CLAUDE.md:433-434 is a faithful compression of that, ⛔-guard scope included. Applying the proposed rewrite would create the divergence that does not currently exist, putting CLAUDE.md out of sync with both the canon doc and the ledger.

(3) THE CENTRAL PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG, AND IT DISSOLVES THE CONTRADICTION. "Phase A" is not the σ_e track; it is a named campaign — docs/reviews/phase_a_6mah_order_prereg_20260907.md, "6 mAh **VGCF+PTFE** 조성 순서 (Phase A, STEP3)", primary estimand = VGCF 1→2→3→4 wt% at fixed PTFE 1 wt%, 96 arms (4 조성 × 3 격자 × 8 origin, --no-ion). Those beds contain NO SDCP: grep finds SDCP once in that prereg (L607) and it is an unrelated CL-70 throughput benchmark ("28.8 min/solve"). So the exemption cannot be "carried onto an SDCP-bearing σ_e comparison" — Phase A has no SDCP phase, and the L427-429 SDCP fusion-deficit bullet has nothing to contradict. The action item's assertion that Phase A "is exactly what the manuscript headline is" misidentifies the campaign.

(4) THE FLAGGED TEXT IS THE CORRECTION, NOT THE ERROR. docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md:11 is an explicit self-correction banner: "⚠ 첫 답변이 *"Phase A 는 σ_e 라 무관합니다"* 였다. **회피였다** — 무관한 것은 Phase A 뿐이고, σ_ion 축에는 실재하는 결손이다." The corrected form the doc endorses is "only Phase A is exempt" plus the ionic-axis ⛔ guard — precisely what CLAUDE.md:433-434 now says. The auditor read the post-correction wording as the pre-correction evasion (a listed failure mode).

(5) SUBJECT MISMATCH within the paragraph. L433's subject is the SE–SE face interfacial term (CL-81's core, ionic axis); L427-429's subject is the fusion deficit on the carbon phases (fiber/particle contact resistance lumped into σ, CL-47(ii) vs CL-61). The canon separates these per-phase in its §4 table, and CLAUDE.md separates them into distinct bullets. Reading L433 as retracting L427-429 requires ignoring the ground clause present in the same sentence.

Only the code ground checks out, and the auditor already concedes it: step3_sigma.py:97 has sigma_se=0.0 as the default, and sid 9 (SE_blk) is fixed 0 (:107, :120, :2407 "9: 0.0"). That confirms the exemption is true, not that it is misscoped.

summary: This is the oldest continuously-untouched stratum of CLAUDE.md: ~840 lines written 2026-05-27 → 2026-06-05, of which only three edits have landed since (the CL-12 thermal banner 2026-08-12, the A1 σ_S/σ_P annotation 2026-06-30, the φ_AM<0.3 validity guard 2026-08-11). The science in it is mostly sound and the frozen forms still match production code — SE_CN_EXP=2.0 / SE_COV_EXP=0.5, _STAGE_FORM_VERSION=22.5, _STAGE_22_5_DROP_COLS={3,7,12,13} all confirm the T1 and Stage-22.5 DO-NOTs are still binding. The ban sweep is clean here (no retracted-string leak). What has rotted is the epistemic framing, and it has rotted in exactly the way CLAUDE.md rule ④ predicts. Three ledger claims — CDX-09, CDX-10, CDX-11 — are `rejected` and their `location` fields literally cite these line ranges; I resolved those line numbers against the 2026-08-12 tree and the text they point at is verbatim unchanged, with no banner anywhere. The thermal section got a CL-12 banner but the banner does not reach the two quotable lines below it (a "Paper claim:" sentence asserting the very narrative CL-12 quotation-banned, and a DO-NOT that CL-12 explicitly put on hold) — the SELF-07 failure mode, banner-explains-file-but-not-the-cell. Outside CLAUDE.md the damage is worse: `scripts/generate_fitting_report.py` is wired to a live webapp route (`webapp/app.py:10419`) and still emits, into a downloadable report, the exact "σ_S = 10 mS/cm LOCKED (Trevisanello 2021)" mis-attribution that commit 29375b2 claimed to fix on 2026-06-30 — the commit touched two other files and missed this one. Four mutually inconsistent renderings of "the production σ_ionic form" coexist inside the scope and only one matches the code; the canon derivation doc the section names is itself pre-T1; and the webapp predictor still runs the pre-T1 v12-clean v3 form while the section says T1 is production. Finally the whole triad is unreproducible from this repo (zero `full_metrics.json` committed) even though a 163-case aggregate with every needed column sits in `docs/data/case_master.csv`, and the corpus has grown ~60-100% since the forms were frozen by the very mechanism (corpus growth) the Stage-22.5 section documents as what exposed Stage 21's over-fit.

findings.claim: The locked-exponent 'paper-grade strong narrative' calls all five exponents literature-locked and zero-DOF, but its own Source column says φ_AM^4 was picked by nested CV on this corpus, and two of the five verdicts are 'within noise' — a likelihood-ratio-1 outcome being reported as confirmation.
findings.evidence: Offending text, CLAUDE.md:2202-2205 `LOCKED-EXPONENT VALIDATION … All 5 literature-anchored locked exponents independently validated against the n=76 corpus.  Pure validation — 0 additional DOF per test`; L2211-2212 `| φ_AM^a (Bruggeman) | a = 4 | Stauffer-Bruggeman bkbn + Stage 14 nested CV | ★ exact lock |`; L2219-2220 `| Bimodal (p(1-p))^a | a = 1 | symmetric mixing | ★ within noise (±0.0003 floor)|`; L2217-2218 `| C(τ) poly degree | logpoly2 (3) | σ_ionic T1 mirror | best |`; L2231-2237 the Paper claim. Contradicting sources: (a) the same table — 'Stage 14 nested CV' is corpus selection, and 'symmetric mixing' / 'σ_ionic T1 mirror' are internal conventions, not literature, so at most 3 of 5 have an external anchor; (b) the standing convention that a number is evidence only if the competing hypothesis predicts something different (claims.json rule D1; CDX-09's `expected_violations: ['C_EQUAL_PREDICTION']` applied to this same section); a 'within noise' verdict is the exact case where the test had no discriminating power; (c) 'Stage 14' has no committed derivation anywhere — `grep -rn 'Stage 14'` returns only CLAUDE.md and scripts/generate_fitting_report.py restating it.
findings.proposed_action: Split the table into 'literature-anchored' (Holm 0.5) vs 'convention' (bimodal a=1, poly degree) vs 'corpus-selected' (φ_AM^4 via Stage 14, NCM β=1.5 per the A1 close-out), report the two 'within noise' rows as no-discrimination rather than confirmation, and rewrite the Paper claim accordingly. Whether φ_AM^4 has any genuine Stauffer-Bruggeman backing (the standard 3D percolation conductivity exponent is not 4) is a physics call for outside review, and 'Stage 14' needs a committed record or the citation should be dropped.

summary: This region is 1,770 of CLAUDE.md's 2,288 lines and it is overwhelmingly CLOSED HISTORY that is still typeset as LIVE GUIDANCE. Two things are genuinely healthy: every file, script and commit SHA it points at exists (33/33 analysis scripts, 31/31 docs, 12/12 commits verified), and the production code still matches the parameter blocks it documents (mpm3d defaults E=1.53/ν=0.49/σ_y=0.30/wallP; Stage 22.5 drop-cols {3,7,12,13}; thermal 14 features at α=0.05; STEP4 x100=0.9084). The quotation-ban sweep is clean. The rot is elsewhere and it is systematic: the 2026-08-12 Codex adversarial sweep rejected eight claims whose `location` fields point straight into this region — CDX-12 (1.35≡1.5 identical regime), CDX-13 (Heckel 46 MPa as a material quantity), CDX-16 (MPM 49.6/48.2 vs DEM 48.3/51.8 coverage as independent cross-validation), CDX-17 (the same 18× softening independently required by DEM and MPM), CDX-18 (the dip cross-validated by two independent tools), CDX-09/10/11 (the three LOOCV values as generalization certificates), CDX-25 (target-conditioned 2D rendering) — and **not one of them has been marked in the text**. Worse, three of those rejections are additionally contradicted by code that is live today: `mpm_input_from_case.py` maps the DEM's `e_se_eff_gpa` into the MPM shear modulus and `mpm_dem_match.py:491` sets the per-case MPM modulus to 1.53·(E_dem/1.35) by default, so the "never calibrated to each other" frame[4] declaration is false at the tool level; and `mpm3d_compaction.py:3414-3415` records that legacy target-driven runs reach `settled_over_target` = 0.021 (real_14) and 0.009–0.049 (P:S kits), so the scaffold "@300 MPa cross-validation" was never at 300 MPa. Three further blocks state results whose ledger has since flipped underneath them (the 2C CCCV +0.7 %p sits 45 lines *above* its own HISTORICAL banner and cites a DO-NOT-CITE ledger; A14 is "CLOSED" while CL-63 forbids any headline on it; the reliability "76 %" disagrees with the CSV it cites, which now says 73.5 %). The correction discipline that does exist is applied at bullet granularity, so a banner in one bullet leaves the invalidated sentence standing two bullets away (thermal CL-12 banner vs the unmarked DO-NOT 84 lines later; scaffold porosity 정정 vs the untouched coverage claim four lines above). Finally, the ledger's own pointers into this region are all broken — every `location: CLAUDE.md:NNN` in claims.json now lands on unrelated text, and no checker validates them. This region is the right extraction candidate, but extraction must carry the constraint paragraphs verbatim (the ε_sphere convention, the frozen-form DO-NOTs, "NEVER re-screen φc", "NEVER report coverage_AM_*_mpm_pct", the four AM-freeze reasons) and must re-anchor the ledger locators in the same commit, or the move will silently amputate exactly the qualifiers this apparatus exists to protect.

Coverage is then measured purely by adjacency ... with no pinning"). So "the synthesis promotes pixels until the supplied target is met" is not true of the synthesis Phase 4 references.

(2) THE CONTRADICTING SOURCE IS A MALFORMED-CLAIM SPECIMEN, NOT A LIVE VERDICT. claims.json `_status_vocab` defines `rejected` as "★ 역사적 실패 표본 — 검사가 **반드시 거부해야 한다**" (historical failure specimen the checker MUST reject; check_method_discipline.py:733-761 errors if such an entry ever passes). CDX-25 is one of twenty CDX-09…CDX-25 entries, every one carrying `expected_violations: ["C_EQUAL_PREDICTION"]`, i.e. registered because h0_predicts and h1_predicts are the SAME string ("coverage_2d approaches the supplied coverage target") → likelihood ratio 1 → zero evidence. Its own `measured.value` is null with reason "no single frozen current scalar is cited". CDX-25 appears nowhere else in the repo (grep across .md/.json/.py) and is absent from `quotation_ban` (22 entries, no match), so no repo rule obliges CLAUDE.md to carry it.

(3) PHASE 4 MAKES NO VALIDATION CLAIM TO CONTRADICT. CLAUDE.md L1512-1514 is a single build task inside a section headed "### 5-phase plan (agreed order: sequential 1→5)": add a targets-only entry point "so predictor output drives the 2D synth." It never states or implies that 2D/3D agreement validates or falsifies the predictor. A "missing caveat" finding requires the text to invite the rejected inference; this text does not.

The second proposed action is already satisfied by the section's own convention: delivered items are explicitly tagged ("**Phase 1 COMPLETE (2026-06-04)**", "**Phase 1 (grade_engine expose) — DONE** (commit 9785bbf)"); Phases 2-5 carry no completion marker. The auditor's own sub-observation is correct on its face — `synthesize_microstructure` does return None when meta.json is absent (L568-569, verified) — but that is what an unbuilt plan item looks like, not a defect in the plan.

Honest residual (not what was filed): `synthesize_calibrated` (L1031) IS a closed generate→measure→nudge loop that drives per-phase coverage to the supplied 3D targets within cov_tol, and `_best_gap_for_case` (L1072) searches gap to hit phi_AM. So "the 2D synth pipeline is target-conditioned" has a real kernel — but by parameter control in a wrapper Phase 4 does not name, not by pixel promotion, and it would at most justify an optional annotation on an unbuilt roadmap line, not a P1 missing-caveat contradicting the ledger.

summary: This scope holds the repo's compaction epistemology, and it has split into two halves with opposite health. The live half — `mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md` (rev7, 2026-09-03) and `se_curve_transfer_verdict_20260806.md` (2026-08-11) — is disciplined, self-correcting, and reproducible: I re-ran the d_h collapse fits from the committed archive and reproduced −0.563/R² 0.910 (192) and −0.575/R² 0.926 (288, φ0.75) exactly. The dormant half — nine files last touched between 2026-06-06 and 2026-08-11 — was never updated after the platen defect was proved, and it still carries as live the three claims that defect killed: that scaffold porosity is an emergent output, that DEM↔MPM porosity agreement is a validity certificate, and that the residual 1.2 %p is a converged model-trust bound. `mpm3d_calibration.md` is the worst case: the platen canon lists it twice (§11 line 383, §37 line 847) as needing correction, and both flagged blocks stand verbatim and unmarked seven weeks later. Two structural failures amplify this. First, a false-green: the platen doc's head banner satisfies the ban-sweep's file-level exemption, so the entire 975-line file is exempt from all 22 quotation bans — and `+52.0 %` (CL-24, ban pattern #1) sits inside it at line 304 graded "B = survives", passing the checker with zero problems (verified by calling `ban_sweep` directly). Second, the same banner asserts the file is "stuck at rev6" while rev7 is 840 lines below it, so the one signpost that would send a reader to the current answer sends them away instead. Beyond staleness there are three hard arithmetic/verification errors: the wallP doc's "90.6 % (106/117) reliable (|gap|≤4)" is actually 73.5 % under the criterion it states (106 = 117 − 11 catastrophic, a different criterion — recomputed from the CSV it cites); the reliability doc uses the sign of `gap` in two opposite senses and gives the corner discriminator backwards in its own follow-up section; and the DPC cap cross-check's entire data table was produced by the `mean(prs)` readout that the code itself now labels "RESOLUTION-BIASED; KEPT to demonstrate the resolution bias".

findings.claim: The two canon docs map the same physical distance to opposite Stage-E regimes, and the coverage doc's agreement sentence compares its Hertz-band number against the DEM Tabor value.

Consequence: the coverage doc's line 126 compares `MPM rigid 46/70` (46 = the 0.13 band) against `DEM Stage-E Tabor ~48–52`. Further, the DEM side is not a distance band at all: `scripts/network_conductivity.py:287-291` defines Hertz vs Tabor as contact-AREA regimes (`A_hertz` vs the `A_tabor = F/H` cap), so "the same two distances the DEM Stage-E uses" is not literally true.

findings.locator: LOCKED parameter table line 13; fix (2) line 40; physical reading line 52
findings.claim: The production parameter table labels 24 GPa the real LPSC bulk modulus and calls K_SE = 25.5 a match to it; 24 GPa is the Young's modulus, and our own DFT bulk modulus is B₀ = 26.23.
findings.evidence: Offending text, line 13: `| **ν_SE** | **0.49** | → **K_SE = 25.5 GPa ≈ real LPSC bulk (24)**; μ_SE = 0.51 GPa (soft shear) |`; line 40 `(real LPSC K ≈ 24 GPa, near-incompressible at 0.3 GPa)`; line 52 `SE bulk = REAL (24 GPa)`. Contradicting source: CLAUDE.md, 3D MPM section: `⚠ **K↔B₀ 로만 비교할 것** — 구 표기 "K 25.5 ≈ real LPSC bulk 24" 의 24는 **영률 E** (Sakuda 2013) 라 비교 대상이 틀렸다 (값이 우연히 가까웠을 뿐). 우리 DFT 의 (E_VRH 22.06, B₀ 26.23) 쌍은 **ν = 0.360** 을 함축하고 그때 실제 μ = 8.11 GPa → 우리 μ 0.5134 는 **15.8배 연화**`. The same mislabel is propagated into code at `scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py:532` (`K_CHAMP = ... # 25.5 GPa (real LPSC bulk)`), into `docs/mpm_wallP_conditional_troubleshooting.md:469` (`nu0.49(K=25.5≈real LPSC 24)`), and into `docs/mpm_dpc_cap_crosscheck.md:17` (`SE (Li₆PS₅Cl) is a solid with bulk modulus ≈ 24 GPa`). CLAUDE.md notes this exact conflation already reached an SI table.
findings.proposed_action: Compare K only to B₀ = 26.23 (25.5 is a −2.8 % match, which is a better result than the one being claimed), and state the softening as 15.8× on the shear modulus against the DFT pair. Fix the same string at the three other sites and the code comment in one commit.

surface_worthy.why: This is the first-principles explanation of why every frozen-AM scaffold run over-compresses, and it makes the behaviour predictable rather than mysterious — but it sits at line 898 of a 975-line file, behind a head banner that tells the reader the file is stale and the answer is elsewhere.
surface_worthy.one_line: σ_y(SE) = 0.30 GPa is exactly the platen target, so a J2 material on its yield surface flows isochorically until geometric jamming — with frozen AM carrying zero load, the SE can only reach 300 MPa by full densification; ε_sphere 1.13 % is the necessary consequence, not an anomaly (rev7 §7-3).

surface_worthy.why: The single most consequential correction in the whole compaction canon: it dissolves the repo's most-cited cross-validation into a bookkeeping identity, and it is the reason three other documents in this scope are wrong. It is buried at line 746 in rev6.
surface_worthy.one_line: DEM reports ε_sphere and MPM reports a union porosity; the difference decomposes exactly (SE–SE 0.402 + AM–SE 0.848 = 1.251 %p predicted vs 1.251 %p measured), scales as 1/h, and is grid-independent by definition — so the only falsifiable MPM output on the scaffold path is the stress-stop thickness (rev6 §31).

surface_worthy.why: A hard, cheap, universally applicable gate that every future scaffold MPM run should pass through, computable from the scaffold CSV with no GPU — and it is currently reachable only by reading to line 340 of a 655-line verdict document.
surface_worthy.one_line: d_h/dx = (V_free/S_AM)/dx ≳ 3.5 is the minimum resolution at which SE stress is trustworthy; below it, unresolved constrictions vanish from the grid and σ reads low (measured: +4.0 % change at 3.43 cells vs +23.8 % at 1.18 cells under the same 2.25× refinement).

surface_worthy.why: A methodological rule discovered by being burned: the same five beds at the same grid flip between "collapse holds" and "collapse weak" purely on the choice of common φ. I reproduced both outcomes from the committed archive. Anyone re-fitting anything indexed at a common state needs this.
surface_worthy.one_line: Set the common φ to the median landing point of the single-point beds, so every bed receives the same magnitude of correction — at φ0.72 the 288 five-bed fit gives R² 0.844, at φ0.75 it gives 0.926, from identical data (§⑩).

surface_worthy.why: A reusable design for testing any geometric-stop heuristic without circularity — the repo keeps rediscovering that a statistic fitted on one bed reproduces that bed's own input. Currently readable only inside a quantile-rejection section.
surface_worthy.one_line: The only non-circular validation of a geometric stop criterion: a single preregistered quantile must reproduce all three thicknesses from one bed's 100/300/600 MPa dumps, with held-out cases, tolerance at least one platen step (0.27 µm), and the explicit note that passing validates a thickness predictor, not a porosity model (§32).

surface_worthy.why: This is the live replacement for the forbidden f_AM path, and the number the platen track has been blocked on since August. It is at line 487, after 480 lines of superseded fix attempts, and the docs that need it still quote the retired estimator.
surface_worthy.one_line: f_AM measured directly from LIGGGHTS contact forces at four pressures — AM-AM 0.517 / 0.598 / 0.675 / 0.620 at 100/200/300/600 MPa, with SE-SE carrying only 6.6–9.5 % of the normal stress; the Hertz reconstruction over-reads by 1.30–1.36× and cannot be tuned, because hooke/hysteresis history cannot be recovered from a static snapshot.

surface_worthy.why: The canonical explanation behind a standing repo-wide ban that is enforced in the data layer (MPM_FORBIDDEN) and re-checked by the Phase A runner — but the reasoning lives only here, and the ban is easy to violate because the field name looks legitimate.
surface_worthy.one_line: Report the all-points deformed (PLASTIC) and analytic geometric (RIGID) coverages only; the voxel-adjacency `coverage_AM_*_mpm_pct` (~26 %) is density- and n_vox-bound, does not converge, and must never enter a corpus or an ML feature set.

surface_worthy.why: The strongest external grounding in this scope — it converts the awkward 'MPM fails in a corner' story into 'the corner is outside the manufactured envelope', with named papers and numbers. Buried in §16-lit at line 409.
surface_worthy.one_line: The unreliable corner (87–92 wt% AM, SE/solid 16–26 vol%, 15–20 µm) is outside the fabricated envelope on two axes — every real sulfide cathode in the surveyed literature is 40–157 µm at 5–10 mAh/cm², and high-AM cathodes are deliberately bimodal — while the composition axis sits at the SE-starvation edge bracketed by Choi 2024 (85 wt%, works) and Park 2020 / Kim 2024 (90 wt%, ionic-percolation failure).

surface_worthy.why: The four reasons AM is frozen are untouched by everything that retracted the rest of this document, and they are the answer to a question that keeps returning ("why not just give the AM physics?"). They deserve to survive the document that carries them.
surface_worthy.one_line: AM stays frozen for four independent reasons — rigid point-contact load bearing is a contact-network phenomenon the continuum cannot represent, mobile rigid AM re-introduces 36–41 % over-shielding, AM as material blows CFL/OOM above n_grid 384, and unfreezing drifts off the measured 300 MPa skeleton — and §15 records six GPU rounds that each died against one of them.

surface_worthy.why: Two hard constraints that will be rediscovered expensively otherwise: a memory ceiling that recurs across every 100 µm bed, and a convergence order that tells you extrapolation is not available on this axis.
surface_worthy.one_line: A ~105 µm bed at n_grid 384 needs ≈35 GB (measured CUDA OOM on a 32 GB V100), so 100 µm-class beds cannot be run at 384; and the three-point ladder 128/192/288 gives apparent order p ≈ 0.10, i.e. effectively no convergence, so Richardson extrapolation on this axis is meaningless.

surface_worthy.why: A ready-made checklist for anyone about to write the compaction Methods section — the one place that collects sentences already proven wrong. It only needs the rev4/rev6/rev7 entries appended to be complete.
surface_worthy.one_line: §13 lists the sentences that must not appear in the paper (eight from rev1–rev2, e.g. "integer stop frames prove kinematic stopping", "real_14 did not trigger the defect"), and §11 lists the nine downstream documents and code comments each retraction still has to be pushed into.

refuted_p0p1.claim: The document gives opposite verdicts for the same cases in two of its own sections, and the CSV it cites carries the later section's numbers under the earlier section's decision.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The quotes are accurate but the provenance chain is inverted, and the two headline sub-claims fail on the actual files.

(1) §3 and §8 are not the same measurement. §8's header reads `## §8 ★ wallP-조건부 재실행 … (2026-06-26, 진행중)` and its table column header is `MPM(재실행)` — a re-run under the §6-option-5 wallP conditional, marked in-progress. The CSV verdict strings record the transition explicitly (`wallP cond 15.9->21.78`, `wallP cond 9.7->22.2`, `MPM 20.2 (wallP cond., f_AM-insensitive)`). §3's 0.0 is the pure run; §8's 20.2 is the conditional run. The auditor quoted the cells but not the section/column labels stating the configuration changed, so this is a labelled method-change experiment, not an unmarked self-contradiction.

(2) The CSV's decision columns are the NEWEST layer, not "the earlier section's decision". `git show ee709f8a5` (2026-06-28) is the commit that ADDED `regime, use_source, use_porosity_pct` — one day after `docs/mpm_wallP_conditional_troubleshooting.md` §17-A (2026-06-27) removed the wallP conditional from production and §17-B ruled that the out-of-envelope corners use `porosity는 DEM 사용, MPM 신뢰 X, |gap|=certificate`. §17-B enumerates 13 corner cases; the CSV contains exactly 13 rows with `regime=SE-poor-corner(out-of-envelope)` and `use_source=DEM` (104 rows are `use_source=MPM`). So `use_source=DEM` implements the layer that SUPERSEDES §8. §8's "MPM 신뢰" is the abandoned branch — the opposite polarity to the finding, which asks to reconcile §3/§4 toward §8.

(3) The CSV does not carry §3's decision. §3 line 119/124 classified 1mAh_100_15 as `trust = DEM (COLLAPSE, n=1)`. The CSV row says `trust = bracket`, i.e. §4's rule re-evaluated on the new value (line 151: `MPM ≥ 3% → BRACKET [MPM 아래끝, DEM 위끝] → DEM을 primary`). `bracket` + `use_source DEM` is precisely §4's prescription; no CSV row carries `trust=DEM` at all.

(4) The proposed action already exists. The `cond_status` column stamps provenance per row: `OFF/overcompact (MPM 20.2<floor 27.8; true~anchor)` on the 13 corners, `ok (MPM>=floor; cond moot)` on 48, `SE-rich n/a (MPM>DEM, DEM-side)` on 59.

(5) The CLAUDE.md citation is misread: `use_porosity_pct` is banned as an ML feature/target (nested R² 0.397, because the gate swaps porosity to MPM while leaving φ from DEM), not condemned as bookkeeping to be dropped.

The "verdict text calls 32.8 an outlier while use_porosity_pct = 32.8" tension is literally present, but it is the documented conservative regime-gate for rows already flagged out-of-envelope, applied uniformly to all 13 corners.

Residual real issue, far smaller than claimed: the reliability doc has no pointer to §17-A (grep for `conditional|§17|troubleshooting` in it returns nothing), so §8 read alone looks like the standing verdict. That is a one-line doc-freshness annotation, P3.

refuted_p0p1.claim: §⑥'s headline five-bed 288 fit no longer reproduces from the committed archive — the same configuration now returns "접힘 약함" — and §⑨ states a data gap that the committed files disprove.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
REFUTED on the load-bearing sub-claim, and the "discovery" is the document's own next section.

**1. "−0.596 is the four-bed number, not the five-bed number §⑥ presents" — demonstrably FALSE.** Refitting §⑥'s own table (docs/se_curve_transfer_verdict_20260806.md:366-371) with numpy:
- 5-bed: slope −0.5956 · R² 0.9682 · res_sd(n−2) 0.0509
- 4-bed (drop ps_7_3): slope −0.5962 · R² 0.9670 · res_sd 0.0623

Line 373 reads `기울기 −0.596 · R² 0.968 · 잔차sd 0.051`. R² and 잔차sd discriminate the two fits cleanly, and both match the **five-bed** fit to every printed digit. §⑥'s headline is the five-bed number and is internally exact. The slopes coincide at 3 dp only because ps_7_3's residual is +0.0020 — which §⑥ itself flags in §(b) ("잔차 ~0, 지렛대 ~0"). The auditor mistook a coincidence of slope for an identity of fit.

**2. The reproduction is not "the same configuration."** I ran it (unpack_kit_scaffolds.py → fit_dh_collapse.py --mach 0.03 --n-grid 288 --phi 0.72) and got 5-bed −0.649/0.844/0.132 and 4-bed −0.596/0.967/0.062. Every non-ps_7_3 row reproduces §⑥ **exactly** (0.8508/0.7533/500.7, 0.6400/0.6013/620.3, 0.5840/0.5349/744.5, 0.4037/0.3847/1458.1). Only ps_7_3 moved, and the tool prints why: 방법 flipped from `최근접` (+g192 보정 → 0.4964, dlnσ/dφ 2.16) to `보간` (0.3893). Cause: `git log` shows commit cd7b95a90 (2026-08-12) added `xfer_kit_ps_7_3_g288_e742/e1497.json`, giving ps_7_3 three 288 points. §⑥ is a dated 2026-08-07 snapshot in an append-only verdict log; the archive gained data afterwards.

**3. The −0.649/0.844 result is already documented, verbatim, as the doc's own finding.** §⑩ (line 579, "288 5침대 완성 + **공통 φ 선택이 결론을 바꾼다**", 2026-08-11 저녁) tabulates `288 | 0.72 | −0.649 | 0.844 | 0.132 | 0.405`, diagnoses it (외삽 규모 → 보정 방식 혼합), and issues the standing rule "공통 φ 는 단일점 침대들의 착지 중앙값에 둔다". CLAUDE.md:659 carries the same row as governing canon. The auditor re-derived a documented result and reported it as an undocumented regression.

**4. The §⑨ line 575 point is superseded by the very next line, and the proposed fix is wrong.** §⑩ opens at line 581 by quoting and closing it: "§⑨ 말미의 '288 5침대는 미완' 이 채워졌다 — kit_ps_7_3 288@0.03 (ε 7.42) 완주" (= the e742 file). This is the correction-banner pattern, read as the error it corrects. Worse, the proposed edit ("say 192@0.03 rather than 288@0.03") would contradict §⑨'s own headline — §⑨ *is* the section that filled the 192@0.03 gap ("192 5침대 정식 인용 완성 — ps_7_3 0.03 런 실측", φ 0.66/0.72/0.81). Applying it would break the document.

**Residual nit (not P1, not the finding as filed):** line 575's parenthetical *reason* is loose — `xfer_res_kit_ps_7_3_g288_e1173.json` (mach 0.03, n_grid 288) was committed 2026-08-07 in 986fa7bcb, so a single 288@0.03 point did exist; §⑧:537 states the precise version ("g192 보정 불가"). But "미완" was substantively true (one point at φ 0.7475 needs a 0.0275 correction = 5.5× the 0.005 threshold), and §⑩ closes the sentence explicitly. Not actionable as stale text.

surface_worthy.why: Brand new (2026-09-08) and it changes how every STEP3 ionic number must be read, but nothing else in the repo links to it yet. Its two-deficit split is the single most reusable idea in this scope: one deficit shrinks with refinement, the other is structurally absent and stays zero at h -> 0, so 'just use a finer grid' answers only half the question.
surface_worthy.one_line: The voxel STEP3 solve sits on the contact-network's own CONTACT_FREE branch; the gap was already stored in case_master.csv as R_brug_over_full (median 4.04x Hertz / 6.69x Physics, n=157, spread 2.3-13.6x).

surface_worthy.why: A sharp, currently-true, non-obvious rule buried in the last third of a report: it decides where a sigma-axis conclusion may legitimately be drawn, and it is stated nowhere else. Anyone tempted to test a doping or material change through the scaling law would waste the run.
surface_worthy.one_line: Feeding sigma_grain into the scaling law is a no-op — the C_blend(tau) intercept absorbs the multiplier exactly (repo selftest, atol=1e-12) — so sigma-axis conclusions can only come from the STEP3 voxel solve.

surface_worthy.why: This is CL-81 stated correctly weeks before CL-81 was written, in a positioning document nobody would search for a solver limitation. It is the proof that the knowledge existed and only the index was missing — exactly the failure the hub rebuild is meant to fix.
surface_worthy.one_line: Continuum FV (GeoDict and our own voxel alike) returns only the contact-free upper bound, which is why production sigma_ionic stays with the DEM contact network.

surface_worthy.why: CL-81 lists the voxel-divided-by-contact-network comparison as its number-one unrun task, but this file already contains that measurement on a real case with the mechanism explained. surface_worthy.one_line: On input_1mAh_8_AMS_S1 the voxel ionic solve returns 0.250 mS/cm against the DEM full 0.0436 — it lands on the contact-free bound because the SE neck (0.065 um^2) is sub-voxel, while the electronic channel matches because AM-AM necks are many voxels wide.

surface_worthy.why: The clearest general statement in the repo of when a multiplicative prefactor cancels and when it does not, written for sigma_grain but reusable for every 'does this cancel?' argument — including the ones CL-81 says must stop being made without evidence. It is buried inside a temperature audit as a mitigation subsection.
surface_worthy.one_line: A pure multiplicative prefactor cancels in same-temperature relative comparison, does not cancel in absolute overpotential or in a temperature-axis comparison, and only partially cancels across compositions whose phases have different activation energies.

surface_worthy.why: A measured, mechanism-level result about how the voxel raster mangles fibres, sitting in a paper-adoption planning document where nobody debugging grid non-convergence would look. It is a live candidate for the unexplained Q-B2 residual grid dependence, alongside SELF-11's SDCP contact quantization.
surface_worthy.one_line: A 10 um straight fibre fragments into ~4.3 pieces at vox 0.4 (91.7% fragmented), 99.7% at 0.2 and 100% at 0.141 — so the sigma_e grid bias has two large competing channels and its net sign is UNCERTAIN, moving toward under-estimation as the grid tightens.

surface_worthy.why: An independent discretization reproducing the same class of non-convergence that CL-41 found on the voxel side, documented in a COMSOL export pipeline that nobody would consult when debugging the grid sweep. It suggests the non-convergence is a property of unresolved contacts rather than of the voxel implementation.
surface_worthy.one_line: In the FEM track, snapping near-contacts creates point-contact singularities whose conductance scales with element size, so sigma_e drifts down without converging as the mesh tightens — 'runs without error' is not 'sigma has converged'.

surface_worthy.why: The record of the plate-coupling defect that made sigma swing by 7.7x under a sub-voxel bed shift, and of the reformulation that fixed it — directly relevant to the live p1/p2 plate-rule hold that currently bans a whole family of ratios, yet it sits in the middle of a review-history section.
surface_worthy.one_line: Coupling the top plate to a single AM layer made sigma_e swing x7.7 with sub-voxel bed motion; the continuous-plane reformulation with distance-weighted per-column coupling fixed it, leaving a residual ~x2 quantization only for crown-sparse floating beds.

surface_worthy.why: A literature threshold that lands exactly on the live Phase A composition axis, recorded in a degradation document where the Phase A prereg would never find it. If the threshold is real, the registered ordering may not be monotone across the four compositions.
surface_worthy.one_line: Reisacher 2023 puts the carbon electronic percolation threshold at p_c ~ 4 wt%, which is the top end of Phase A's registered VGCF 1/2/3/4 wt% axis.

refuted_p0p1.claim: This file declares a FINAL PRODUCTION MODEL whose two network exponents differ from what production fits today, with no banner; CLAUDE.md flagged it in May as needing a label fix and it was never done.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
The quoted strings are all real (line 122 heading, line 125 formula, β=1.50/γ=0.40 at 133-134, no banner, file untouched since import 660600a44, CLAUDE.md:1597-1600 names it) — but the load-bearing assertion, that these two exponents "differ from what production fits today", is false. They are exactly what two live production paths compute now.

(1) webapp/predictor_engine.py:79-83 `_v12_base_log` = 0.5*log(phi_ex) + 1.5*log(cn) + 0.4*log(cov) + 3.0*log(fp) with PHI_C_V12 = 0.20 — identical to the doc's α=0.50, β=1.50, γ=0.40, δ=3.00, φc=0.20. Line 66 cites this doc as its normative spec; line 608 marks it "v12-clean v3 — primary when available" and it is consumed at 733-734. The module was maintained AFTER T1 (commit f5570a10b moved C_blend to logpoly2 on 2026-05-28) and these exponents were deliberately retained.

(2) Inside the auditor's own cited file, scripts/generate_comparison_plots.py:1901-1903, `_formx_v29_predict` computes `phi_ex**0.5 * cn**1.5 * coverage**0.4 * f_perc**3` under the comment "Base Kirkpatrick scaling (α=1/2, β=3/2, γ=2/5, δ=3, φc=0.20)", with SIGMA_BULK=3.0, PHI_C=0.20 (line 1875) — the doc's table reproduced symbol-for-symbol. It is live (registered plot at 3579; used at 1504, 2059, 2098).

(3) SE_CN_EXP=2.0 / SE_COV_EXP=0.5 at line 4263 belongs to `_sat_baselog` (4359) — a separate, COEXISTING form (T1 Stage-E/physics: Cronau × φ_eff SAT-blend × β_P2 × β_F, fitted to the Stage-E target), not a replacement of v12-clean v3 in the same function. The auditor compared the doc against the wrong function in the file.

So this is not a stale doc with a dead model; it is the accurate spec of a form two production consumers still implement, coexisting with a later Stage-E form. The proposed action would be actively harmful: retitling the section "(historical)" and asserting "production uses CN² and cov_Hertz^½" would write a false statement into the document that predictor_engine.py:66 points at as its reference, while that module keeps computing 1.5/0.4.

Residual genuine defect, opposite in direction and located in code rather than the doc (belongs in a separate finding): commit 3b64137b8 ("ionic 라벨 통일", claiming to install the "실 production 식") pasted the doc's CN^(3/2)/cov^(2/5) string into PLOT_REGISTRY at generate_comparison_plots.py:3589 and :3597, but plot_formx_decomposition actually computes with SE_CN_EXP/SE_COV_EXP plus Cronau/φ_eff/P2 (lines 2318-2325, "Fit T1 production form globally" at 2327). Also not covered by claims.json quotation_ban, which contains none of these values.

refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
Both core assertions fail against the actual sources.

(1) "Names itself the single source of truth" is an inverted reading. Lines 3-5 read "구현 single source of truth: scripts/generate_comparison_plots.py의 _formx_v29_predict() 및 _fit_at()" — i.e. it designates THE CODE as the implementation SSOT and points at it, then subordinates itself ("이 문서는 코드 재검증 완료" = this document was re-verified against the code). The doc never claims that status for itself. The wording mirrors the code's own docstring at generate_comparison_plots.py:1887 ("Single source of truth for v29 FORM X prediction"). The proposed action would delete a correct pointer.

(2) "States exponents the implementation no longer uses" is false. I imported the module and measured the live function the doc names. G._formx_v29_predict() yields exponents exactly CN=1.5, cov=0.4, f_perc=3.0, (phi-0.20)=0.5, with SIGMA_BULK=3.0 and PHI_C=0.20 — every value in the doc's constant table (lines 19-27) and its formula (line 12). (3) The premise "the code moved and this document did not follow it" is wrong: _sat_baselog did not replace the v29 form, it was added alongside it. Both are live, registered production plots in the same file's PLOT_REGISTRY — v29 drives ionic_scaling_fit / multiscale_sigma / formx_decomposition; the T1 Stage-E form drives ionic_perconfig_physics / ionic_outliers_stage_e / ionic_decomp_physics (all six confirmed present). summary: This scope is a large, high-quality literature layer that has been frozen since late June 2026 while the ledger moved on for two and a half months — only one file (lit_bazzoun2026) has been touched since 2026-06-26, and the three `literature_coverage/*.json` databases date from 2026-04-24. Two structural problems dominate. First, **27 of the 33 `docs/lit_*.md` files are byte-identical duplicates of canon `litdb/papers/` cards** (zero real content difference; only the canon frontmatter block differs), in violation of the 2026-07-16 single-drawer rule, and **not one of the 33 files carries a pointer to canon** — so divergence is silent and has already happened: canon's `koo2026` card grew from 597 to 1012 lines on 2026-09-03 with a §11 that stamps ⛔ on three production `scripts/additives.py` parameters, none of which the docs/ copy knows about. The remaining six files (bazzoun2026, varkey2026, bielefeld2019, kim2025, lee2025, koo2026) are genuine comparison records and carry real unique value. Second, the "our value" comparison sections are calibrated against a June-2026 canon and now restate several things the ledger has since retracted or re-labelled: the voxel σ_ion pair 0.0168/0.0298 mS/cm is tabled beside experimental σ_ion in five files and verdicted "CONFIRMED"/"EXPERIMENTAL PROOF" without the `CONTACT_FREE` label that CL-81 made binding today; `porosity 15.93 % EMERGE`, `DEM 15.6 % / MPM 16.7 %`, `Heckel P_y = 138 MPa`, and `LOOCV 0.975/0.953/0.90` are all quoted in their pre-correction sense; and `literature_coverage/README.md` still tells the reader our coverage is a 3–3.6× under-estimate needing k_spread 1.55–1.90, which the repo's own geometric ground truth (Tabor 52 % ≈ Bielefeld 49 %) refutes. Against that, the scope also contains three of the sharpest adversarial documents in the repo — the Trevisanello, Cronau and Bazzoun digests each caught a provenance error before Codex did, and the Cronau one is still un-propagated: canon writes "Cronau 2022 single-crystal, HIGH literature" for a factor the digest graded "loose, year is 2021, breakpoints not in the paper". No banned quotation-registry string appears anywhere in scope, and no model identifiers.

surviving_p0p1.claim: The README's headline conclusion — that our DEM coverage is a 3-3.6x under-estimate and k_spread should be raised to 1.55-1.90 — is refuted by the repo's own geometric coverage ground truth, and the knob it targets is now labelled legacy in code.
surviving_p0p1.evidence: README:135-138 'Our 22% DEM is **3-3.6x under-estimate** at this porosity. **Revised k_spread range: 1.55-1.90** (up from earlier 1.30-1.50)'; README:13-14 'DEM plastic-capped coverage: 22%'. CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md, SE-DUMP scaffold section (2026-06-17): 'COVERAGE ground-truth (geometric, MPM-independent - Fibonacci AM-surface + SE-centre KDTree): SE touching AM (gap<=0)=**16%~Hertz 18**; within 0.14 um (1 vox)=**49%~Tabor 52**. BOTH DEM values validated ... Report 16 (Hertz) / 52 (Tabor), NOT 26.' Our Tabor 52% vs the README's own Bielefeld 49% @20% porosity is agreement, not a 3-3.6x shortfall. Also scripts/plastic_coverage.py:219 "'capped' - geometric cap a^2 <= R_min^2. k_spread scales pre-cap (legacy)." and :225 'k_spread: only applies to capped mode (legacy post-hoc calibration).'
surviving_p0p1.proposed_action: Add a dated banner at the top of README.md: the k_spread calibration programme is CLOSED, superseded by the 2026-06-17 geometric ground truth (Hertz 16 / Tabor 52) and by Stage-E; k_spread is a legacy knob fixed at 1.0. Keep the literature entries (they are still the best coverage corpus) but strike the 'Our baseline 22%', the '3-3.6x under-estimate' line, and the 'Revised k_spread range 1.55-1.90' recommendation.
surviving_p0p1.corrected: The README's "3-3.6x under-estimate" / "k_spread 1.55-1.90" headline IS stale and should be banner-corrected, because it compares conventions rather than numbers: 22% is the contact-band (capped/Hertz) coverage, while the literature rows it is measured against (Bielefeld 49% @20%, 60.2% @15%, ~65% @13%; Hlushkou ~80% UB) are interface-area quantities whose DEM counterpart is the Tabor/physics value (CLAUDE.md geometric ground truth Tabor ~52; repo-measured physics 60.53% per lhs_design_dataset.py:441) — i.e. 1.15-1.3x, not 3-3.6x. FOUR corrections to the finding as written: (1) "now labelled legacy" is wrong — `git show 660600a44` shows the "legacy post-hoc calibration" docstring and the README's "Revised k_spread range: 1.55-1.90" landed in the SAME 2026-04-24 import commit; the label never superseded the README. (2) The proposed banner text "k_spread is a legacy knob fixed at 1.0" is factually wrong: 1.0 is only the function default, `sweep_all_cases` defaults to the sweep [1.0, 1.3, 1.5, 1.65, 1.8] (plastic_coverage.py:498) and :226 actively recommends 1.65 for capped mode — and 1.65 lies INSIDE the README's 1.55-1.90 range, so the code corroborates that range rather than contradicting it. The correct, stronger reason the recommendation is dead is that production never runs capped mode at all: network_conductivity.py:302 calls `mode='physics'`, which takes no k_spread. (3) The rebuttal pairs "our Tabor 52%" with "Bielefeld 49% @20% porosity", but the README's 3-3.6x line is anchored at 13% porosity (Bielefeld ~65% / Hlushkou ~80%), which is the README's line 88-93 anchor, not the headline's. The refutation survives either way, but the arithmetic should be stated against the 13% row. (4) "Strike the 'Our baseline 22%'" is over-broad — 22% is a genuine measured DEM datum in the Hertz/contact convention (repo measures 22.25%), and CLAUDE.md instructs reporting Hertz 16/18 ALONGSIDE Tabor 52. The fix is to label its convention and add the Tabor/physics counterpart, not delete it (deleting it re-creates the single-convention error in the opposite direction).

refuted_p0p1.claim: 'DEM 15.6 % / MPM 16.7 %' is quoted as two conventions-compatible measurements agreeing to ~1 %p, but that gap was shown on 2026-08-12 to be a pure bookkeeping offset, and canon now requires all porosity to be reported in one convention.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
REFUTED on its central premise, plus four independent detail failures.

(1) THE PREMISE IS FALSE — 16.7 % IS ALREADY ε_sphere. The claim rests on "DEM 15.6 (ε_sphere) vs MPM 16.7 (union) = mixed conventions." Canon says otherwise. docs/reviews/fam_platen_prereg_20260812.md §10-3 (added 2026-08-12, commit 40d0e53ea): "cell-fill(`--se-frac`) 경로는 비AM 셀에 채우므로 SE–SE·AM–SE 겹침이 원리적으로 0 이고, 그 런의 porosity 는 **이미 ε_sphere** 다. 검산: ε_sphere(h=30.71) = 16.808 % vs 보고 16.80 (Δ 0.008 %p) / ε_union = 18.148 (1.35 %p 빗나감)." The 16.7/16.80 numbers come from the cell-fill se_frac=0.27 path. DEM 15.6 is also ε_sphere (platen §31: "ε_sphere @ 30.28 µm = 15.626 % = DEM 정본 15.6"). ⇒ the pair is ALREADY in the single convention canon demands. Nothing to convert.

(2) THE CONTRADICTING SOURCE IS THE OUTDATED ONE (a listed refutation pattern). §10-3 explicitly voids the exact attribution the auditor cites: "정본 rev6 §31 결론 1('384↔512 의 +1.2 %p = 관례 오프셋 1.251')은 **cell-fill 런**을 대상으로 하므로 **무효**다 — 두 수는 우연히 같다." The CLAUDE.md 512-grid-convergence banner quoted as EVIDENCE derives entirely from that now-void rev6 §31 conclusion 1. Authority is settled: docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md's own header banner (2026-08-20) says "최신 상태는 ... fam_platen_prereg_20260812.md §0 배너 · §10-2 · §11-1 ... **충돌 시 그쪽이 이긴다**", and CLAUDE.md track 2 itself labels the prereg "(**이쪽이 최신**)". The banner also independently retracts the 1.251 %p constant: "상수가 아니다ㆍ∝1/h ㆍ**`--se-dump` 경로 전용**."

(3) THE PROPOSED ACTION IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL. §10-3: "⇒ **cell-fill 런에 −1.251(또는 1/h) 을 적용하면 이중계상이다.**" Executing "convert every MPM 16.7 % to its ε_sphere value" would subtract an offset that is provably zero on this path, manufacturing a ~1.25 %p error in a number that is currently correct.

(4) FOUR OF FIVE "MIRROR" LOCATIONS DO NOT CONTAIN THE QUOTE. grep -n '16\.7' returns "(no match anywhere in file)" for lit_bielefeld2019, lit_bielefeld2020, lit_minnmann2021 and lit_oh2026. Verbatim: bielefeld2019:317 "우리 측정 porosity(15.6%·~10%)와 *동일시 금지*"; bielefeld2020:365 "우리 15.6%·~10% = *측정 결과*"; minnmann2021:287 "pure-SE ~10 % / real_14 15.6 % @300 MPa"; :303 "우리 real_14 15.6 %"; oh2026:649 "real_14 15.6%". Every one already reports a single ε_sphere number — precisely the auditor's own PROPOSED ACTION. They were cited as violations of the rule they satisfy.

(5) THE lee2025 LINES ASSERT THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT IS ALLEGED. The claim says the pair is "quoted as two conventions-compatible measurements agreeing to ~1 %p." No such framing exists: :342 lists our anchors as things Lee's data is "**직접 비교 불가**"; :447 is inside §10 "주의 / 한계 (over-claim 방지)" and reads "우리 DEM 15.6 % / MPM 16.7 % 와 **직접 비교 금지**"; :390 is a table cell contrasting Lee's "없음" with our quantitative porosity. The words agree/±1 %p/cross-validation/model-trust bound appear nowhere at these lines. Two of the three are explicit prohibitions on comparison.

(6) CDX-16 IS MISAPPLIED. Its claim field is about COVERAGE — "MPM coverage 49.6/48.2% agreeing with DEM Physics 48.3/51.8% is independent cross-validation" — not porosity. Its verdict retains "same-geometry consistency."

Also checked and negative: the pair is not in claims.json quotation_ban (only 22 entries; the porosity-adjacent bans are on "준정적 답은 ~9.4" and "9.4 % vs 실험 15.6", both CL-04, neither implicating 15.6/16.7). The only residual imperfection canon notes is unrelated and immaterial: "두 경로 모두 AM–AM 겹침 0.108 %p 는 여전히 이중계상 중" — 0.1 %p, applying to both paths, and not what was alleged.

refuted_p0p1.claim: A machine-readable database records the superseded FORM X scaling law as FINAL, with exponents and fit statistics that the frozen T1 production form replaced in May 2026, including an outlier list containing cases that were later deleted from disk.
refuted_p0p1.why_refuted:
Refuted on three independent grounds.

(1) The aggravating specific is FALSE. `remaining_outliers_7` lists input_1mAh_9, input_1mAh_8_AMP, input_1mAh_6, input_8mAh_real40_9, input_1mAh_5_AMS, input_6mAh_real_5, input_6mAh_real_10. The only cases deleted from disk on 2026-05-28 were input_1mAh_9_S5 and input_particulate_12_S2 — neither appears in the list. The case cited, input_1mAh_9, is explicitly KEPT: CLAUDE.md:1707-8 "Older anomalies (input_1mAh_9 base + input_particulate_12_S3) remain on disk but stay in _EXCLUDED_NAMES", and scripts/nested_cv_sat.py:50-53 "input_1mAh_9: ... FILE KEPT on disk -> must remain in _EXCLUDED_NAMES" with _EXCLUDED_NAMES = {'input_particulate_12_S3', 'input_1mAh_9'}. Corpus CSVs confirm the base row present and _S5 absent. The auditor conflated the base case with its deleted sibling.

(2) The cited contradicting source says the opposite. CLAUDE.md:1579-85 explicitly distinguishes two different models: `v12-clean v3 == v29_FINAL` (the CN^(3/2)/cov^(2/5) formula) is called the CURRENT-BEST, while "FORM X (v4++)" is a DIFFERENT formula, C*sigma_grain*(phi-0.185)^(3/4)*CN*sqrt(cov)/sqrt(tau), which is the "OLDER, inferior model - kept only as a legacy toggle". The auditor quoted the v4++ sentence as if it described v29_FINAL. That reconciliation section is also dated 2026-05-27, one day BEFORE T1, so as of that section v29_FINAL was current.

(3) The text sits in an explicitly-labelled running history log that internally supersedes itself. scaling_law_evolution.description: "Running log of the FORM X scaling-law refinement. Each section below records one version with its motivation, formula, fit statistics, remaining outliers, and insights that feed the next version." v29_FINAL is entry 1 of 9, followed by dated later entries (v32_in_progress 2026-04-21, v33_structure_d_executed with verdict "INFERIOR to v32. Do not adopt as published form.", a v32 integration-bug post-mortem) and next_refit_candidates_E_F_G stating "Keep exploring alternative forms while v32 stands as current best." So the file never presents v29 as its terminal answer. "v29_FINAL" is a version-slot name corroborated by the _naming_note slot registry, scripts/fit_v29_physics.py, and CLAUDE.md's own note that plot titles read "FORM X v32 / v29_FINAL".

The P1 severity rationale ("no script or reader can pick the old exponents up as current") is unfounded: nothing machine-reads the file — the only Python reference is a docstring line in scripts/plastic_impact_on_params.py, with no json.load anywhere. The file is a single frozen commit (2026-04-24) with entries dated 2026-04-21, i.e. it predates the T1 finalization (2026-05-28) by over a month; it is a dated exploration journal, not a maintained doc that drifted. The repo's own retired-value enforcement (docs/reviews/claims.json quotation_ban, 22 entries) does not cover 0.983, 0.979, v29, CN^(3/2) or cov^(2/5).

The proposed action is additionally harmful: renaming v29_FINAL -> v29_historical would break the version identifier used by scripts/fit_v29_physics.py and the plot titles, and CLAUDE.md already logs label-unification as a known cosmetic item. This repo's discipline explicitly preserves dated failure/exploration history verbatim.

Residual (optional, not a defect): the April log carries no forward pointer to the T1 form finalized a month later. If anything is wanted at all, it is a one-line dated pointer added alongside — never a key rename and never edits to the recorded values.

summary: This scope holds the paper-facing layer: the v7 Methods replacement text (markdown + a co-author DOCX rebuilt 2026-09-08), an older parallel "DEM methodology" Word draft with its JavaScript generator, the verbatim manuscript body snapshot plus its transcript recovery source, two August seminar decks with their extracted JSON and a weekly slide-text file, and four standalone reference/anchor documents. Health is bimodal. The v7 markdown draft and its DOCX are current, heavily qualified, and traceable to canon (`table_s3_data_20260827.md`, W4 arms with `plate_rule = p2-occupied-surface-first`) — but they carry three unfinished CL-86 items and, more seriously, they still justify blanking the σ_ion row with a defect the ledger closed on 2026-08-31 (CL-59 measured the PTFE-centerline ionic cohort, declared the asymmetry resolved, said σ_ion should be reported as a convention span rather than omitted, and declared the D13/8-arm ionic work unnecessary). Everything in `docs/manuscript_draft/` is worse: the committed Word deliverable is a stale build of a generator that changed four days later, so it still ships "paired mean with its standard error", "the two models were calibrated independently", "reconstructed", "compacted to 300 MPa", additives "seeded into the pore space" afterwards, and a false-provenance calibration sentence — while the generator itself still stamps a red banner declaring p2 values to be p1 and on hold, labels the VGCF row "compressed powder", collapses four distinct roles into "Calibrated", and instructs readers to treat the ratio as a lower bound (CL-72 refuted that on 2026-09-07). `sdcp_manuscript_anchors.md` carries a ready-to-paste SI paragraph whose three load-bearing clauses are each refuted (CL-48 h1, R20-04, CL-49), states the manuscript beds were never recompacted when the reported arms show ADD_E_SET, and keys the citation guard to reference [35] after the body snapshot established the numbering shifted by one. `References_and_Methodology.md` predates the entire 2026-05→09 canon and still presents FORM X as the ionic law. The seminar decks are correctly banner-first in presentation order and pass the retracted-string sweep, but the main deck's banner scope covers only the SDCP gain numbers while the deck's central trust narratives (±1.1 %p cross-validation, the triple-confirmed 18× softening, Holm constriction attributed to the voxel solver) are refuted by different ledger entries — and the deck's sibling, presented the same day, already retracts one of them on its own slide 6.

The docx §A still reads 'conductivity ratios are reported as the paired mean with its standard error' and 'The two models were calibrated independently against the same experimental porosity rather than against each other' and 'microstructures were reconstructed in two stages' and 'compacted under displacement control to 300 MPa' and 'VGCF fibres, PTFE fibrils and SDCP particles were then seeded into the pore space at the experimental weight fractions'. CONTRADICTED BY methods_simulation_v7_draft.md line 30 ('paired mean with its standard error' → 'origin-phase spread + range, SE·CI 명시 부정 — 8 origin 은 한 침대의 완전 factorial, 복제 오차 자유도 0'), by claims.json CDX-17 (rejected: the kit maps DEM e_se_eff_gpa into MPM shear, so the two models are not independently calibrated), by CL-86 ⓒ (additives are material points receiving J2 updates, only AM is frozen), by v7 line 405 ('reconstructed 는 tomography 재구성을 암시한다'), and by CL-80 (the platen stops kinematically, short of target stress). build.js has already fixed every one of these.

findings.claim: The shipped Word draft presents both the ~10 % porosity target and the 11-12 % contact overlap as measured literature values for cold-pressed LPSCl at 300 MPa; neither is.
findings.evidence: DOCX §A: 'the contact Young's modulus of LPSCl was softened from the dense-material value of 24 GPa[34] to 1.35 GPa, which reproduces the ~10 % porosity and 11–12 % contact overlap reported for cold-pressed LPSCl at 300 MPa.[9]' CONTRADICTED BY methods_simulation_v7_draft.md lines 99-102 (and the identical DOCX v7 Stage 1 text): 'The ~10 % target is derived from composite and glass literature rather than measured directly on pure LPSCl at 300 MPa, and the 11–12 % contact overlap is a pure-SE simulation consistency result rather than a measured calibration target.' The v7 release-condition table records this as condition ② ('1.35 GPa 의 출처를 정확히 서술 — 해소').
findings.proposed_action: Regenerate from build.js (which already carries the corrected sentence) and verify the shipped file no longer attributes either figure to a measurement on pure LPSCl.

findings.claim: The A2-factorial slide tells the audience that voxel size has a negligible effect and that once the PTFE convention is fixed nothing else needs revisiting; grid non-convergence is the track's largest open problem.
findings.evidence: Lines 22-23: '• 격자 크기·SDCP 접촉 보정은 영향 미미 / ⇒ PTFE 표현만 정하면 결과가 안정, 나머지는 다시 안 만져도 됨'. CONTRADICTED BY methods_simulation_v7_draft.md lines 163-166 ('The ratio is not grid-converged: refining the voxel edge increases it monotonically without following a power law … neither a continuum extrapolation nor a global bound is established'), by claims.json CL-41 (incremental ratio 1.773 against a 2.187 floor ⇒ no p > 0 fits, Richardson extrapolation meaningless), and by CL-72 (behaviour below 0.15 µm and the sign of the continuum error remain unknown). CLAUDE.md lists the mechanism of the residual grid dependence (Q-B2) as having no candidate.
findings.proposed_action: Restate the factorial result as 'within the axes and ranges tested, the PTFE representation dominates', and add the standing caveat that the grid axis is confounded with the diameter-preserving sigma_VGCF rescale (findings DR3-05) and that grid convergence is not demonstrated.

findings.claim: The slide text presents the two PTFE conventions as co-equal reported values bracketing the experiment, which is both the dual-reporting format rejected on 2026-08-29 and the proximity-to-experiment justification the v7 draft explicitly forbids.

CONTRADICTED BY methods_simulation_v7_draft.md lines 59-60 ('★★ 보고 규약 = centerline (사용자 결정 2026-08-29). 본문은 값 하나를 쓰고, 규약 민감도는 Table S3c 에 둔다') and lines 71-72 ('⛔ "centerline 이 참값에 가깝다" · "부피를 더 그리니 전도가 더 맞다" · "실험에 더 가까워서 골랐다" 는 셋 다 쓰지 않는다'), and by the v7 Values paragraph ('neither is a calibrated representation of it'), which means the two settings are not bounds and cannot bracket anything. The figure generator scripts/fig4b_sigma_conventions.py still enforces the rejected co-equal format in its own docstring ('어느 쪽도 먼저 오거나 굵게 그리지 않는다').
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite to the nominal-convention format: one value in the headline (centerline), the alternative named as a sensitivity point, and no bracketing claim. Decide in the same pass whether Figure 4b should be redrawn to match the body's nominal convention, since a main-text figure showing both co-equally contradicts a body that reports one.

findings.claim: The defense record labels the contact-network solver as STEP3 and uses Bazzoun's EIS/FEM validation of that solver to certify the transport triad; the manuscript's conductivities come from a different solver on a different pipeline whose constriction term is exactly zero.
findings.evidence: Line 19: 'STEP3 (`network_conductivity.py`) = 정당한 Kirchhoff 전도 solver (그래프 Laplacian + Holm/Mikic 수축) = COMSOL 전도 모듈과 같은 PDE'; lines 22 and 78: '★ Bazzoun 2026 독립 입증: 같은 재료·코드·접촉물리를 실측 EIS + COMSOL FEM 에 검증(RNM≈FEM≈실험) … 우리는 같은 급 + e/열 삼중' / '전기화학 시스템이 σ-삼중 전송(Bazzoun 입증) … 에서 COMSOL 을 진짜 대체'. CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md §5 (correction 2026-08-11): 'network_conductivity.py = 웹앱 파이프라인 / voxel_conductivity.py · step3_sigma.py (STEP3) = MPM 킷 … ⚠ 둘은 다른 파이프라인이다'; and by claims.json CL-81 / docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md: 'STEP3 복셀 FV 는 면을 harmonic mean 으로만 잇는다 ⇒ 계면 저항 항이 정확히 0' and the code names that branch CONTACT_FREE — upper bound, ideal contact limit. A validation of the Holm-constriction resistor network therefore does not transfer to the solver that produces the manuscript's sigma values.
findings.proposed_action: Add a dated correction block naming the two solvers separately, restrict the Bazzoun claim to the contact-network solver, and record CL-81's binding citation rule: any STEP3 sigma_ion absolute quoted next to experiment must carry 'constriction/GB not included = CONTACT_FREE upper bound'.

findings.claim: The Key Equations Summary presents the superseded FORM X as the ionic scaling law, with a percolation threshold that production froze at different values.

findings.claim: The deck's retraction banner covers only the SDCP electronic and ionic gain numbers, while the deck's central trust narratives — a 1.1 %p DEM/MPM cross-validation presented as the error bar, and a triple-confirmed 18x softening — were refuted by different ledger entries the banner does not name.
findings.evidence: Banner (presentation slide 1): '이 덱의 SDCP 전자·이온 이득 수치는 이후 철회됐다. 정본 = docs/reviews/claims.json (CL-24 · CL-33 · CL-41).' surface_worthy.why: The Limitations paragraph is the single most complete, currently-true statement of what this project can and cannot claim — no interfacial contact resistance anywhere, no grid convergence and no power law, the sigma_VGCF conditionality that reverses the ordering at the single-filament value, non-quasi-static compaction with no cancellation in the ratio, and unestablished SDCP specimen provenance. It sits at line 159, below 80 lines of Korean editorial apparatus, and is the paragraph any new reader of this project should meet first.
surface_worthy.one_line: The five-sentence Limitations paragraph that states every live caveat on the reported conductivities in publishable English.

surface_worthy.why: Note D13 contains the derivation that turned the author's own Figure 2h into a phase-level calibration: PTFE at 9.17 vol% predicts 3.09 mS/cm by inert dilution against 0.97 measured (ratio 0.31), while SDCP at 14.60 vol% predicts 2.82 against 2.86 measured (ratio 1.02), cross-checked with Maxwell-Garnett and robust to the SDCP density proxy over 1.1-1.7 g/cm3. This is the empirical origin of the 'SDCP is ionically inert, PTFE blocks beyond volume' thread that CL-59 and sdcp_inert_prereg_20260903 now rest on, and it is buried inside a JavaScript string literal.
surface_worthy.one_line: Figure 2h re-derived: SDCP behaves as an inert ionic filler (1.02x dilution prediction) while PTFE blocks 3.2x beyond its volume.

surface_worthy.why: Note D10 carries the replacement mechanism sentence in finished English: 'SDCP raises the electronic conductivity mainly by converting electronically insulating volume — electrolyte and pore — into conducting volume, which reroutes current around bottlenecks in the existing carbon network, rather than by carrying a proportional share of the current itself.' That is the CL-44 h1 and CL-45 result stated as manuscript prose, and it replaces the retracted high-conductivity-bridge narrative. Nothing in the v7 package carries it.
surface_worthy.one_line: The publishable one-sentence mechanism: SDCP works by converting insulating volume to conducting volume, not by carrying current.

surface_worthy.why: Note D14 (i) raises a checkable, unresolved input question that nothing else in the repo tracks: this bed's NCM811 was stamped entirely as the AM_S (single-crystal) class and given 10 mS/cm, while the manuscript describes the powder as polycrystalline NCM811 at r = 2.5 um, which this project's own convention puts at AM_P = 5 mS/cm. AM carries roughly 12 % of the current in the SBE, so it moves the absolute sigma_e. It is a two-fold input discrepancy sitting in a co-author note.
surface_worthy.one_line: The bed's active material was stamped single-crystal (10 mS/cm) while the manuscript calls the powder polycrystalline (our convention: 5 mS/cm).

surface_worthy.why: Note D14 (ii) records that the VGCF Young's modulus of 10 GPa is an unanchored placeholder against a literature axial modulus of order 100 GPa, that it enters MPM compaction geometry (not the sigma solve), and that a one-arm sensitivity check bolted onto an existing recompaction would close it — including the CFL cost if the literature value were used. This is the kind of cheap, decisive check the project's own discipline rules favour, and it is invisible outside this file.
surface_worthy.one_line: VGCF E = 10 GPa is an unanchored placeholder against a ~100 GPa literature value; one extra compaction arm would close it.

surface_worthy.why: Section 1 of the inter-version diff records that the author independently weakened the FT-IR interpretation from 'predominantly deprotonated / establishing' to 'partially dissociated / consistent with', which moves the manuscript toward the Patil ESR result (1 spin per 1500 monomers) that CL-61 had logged as a tension with our own sdcp_master.md. It is the one documented case in this scope where the manuscript is ahead of the repo's canon rather than behind it, and it carries a direct implication for sigma_SDCP = 250.
surface_worthy.one_line: The manuscript itself downgraded the self-doping claim to 'partially dissociated', resolving a tension our documents still record the other way.

surface_worthy.why: The areal-capacity note proves arithmetically that SI v6's 3.11 and 3.07 mAh/cm2 cannot both hold, because the two electrodes share one AM scaffold (n_AM = 1271, seed_AM_frac_pct = 45.68) and one stopping thickness (72.534 um); it pins the areal loading at 0.015904 g/cm2 for both and shows the two v6 values imply different specific capacities (195.5 vs 193.0 mAh/g). This is a finished question to put to the collaborators, currently buried mid-file.
surface_worthy.one_line: The two electrodes share one scaffold and one thickness, so SI v6's differing areal capacities cannot both be right; the loading is pinned at 0.015904 g/cm2.

surface_worthy.why: Section 9 is the only place in the repository that records the provenance of the reported numbers as a sentence: the 2026-08-27 bed, vox 0.15 um, SDCP stamped as a true-diameter sphere, two PTFE conventions at eight origins each for sixteen arms, machine-checked to differ in no unregistered factor, with table_s3_data_20260827.md named as canon. CL-86 flags precisely this configuration as needing a permanent home because the code default reproduces 1.124 while the paper reports 1.308.
surface_worthy.one_line: The nominal run configuration behind every reported number, in one paragraph — and the answer to CL-86's open Q3.

surface_worthy.why: Slide 6 is a presentation-ready statement of why the DEM/MPM porosity agreement is not an independent cross-validation — different state variables and solvers, but a one-way transfer of DEM geometry, SE seeds and case-derived parameters, plus the stop defect making the agreement circular — with an explicit list of what remains defensible. It settles in one slide a question that CDX-16, CDX-17 and CDX-21 all touch, and it is reachable only inside a deck marked HISTORICAL.

The evening user decision (line 107 ff.) changed only WHICH number the manuscript body quotes, and explicitly mandated dual reporting: line 142 — "⇒ 원고는 **두 값을 다 싣고**, centerline 을 본문 값으로 쓰되 0.43 / 0.00 을 함께 적는다" (the form Codex R11 A1 required). The v7 draft itself does exactly this: its Values paragraph (lines 150-157) prints 54.0/70.6→1.308 AND 72.3/81.3→**1.124** in the same paragraph. The auditor quotes v7 lines 59-60 ("본문은 값 하나") as banning dual reporting, but that sentence governs which value the body's headline sentence quotes, not whether both appear.

LIMB B — the "proximity-to-experiment justification" is not present. v7 lines 71-72 forbid three specific sentences: "centerline 이 참값에 가깝다", "부피를 더 그리니 전도가 더 맞다", "실험에 더 가까워서 골랐다". All three justify a CHOICE by proximity. The slide selects nothing — line 66 says "어느 쪽이 참인지 정하지 않았고" (we have not decided which is true), which is the absence of the forbidden justification, not an instance of it.

Positively, the straddling statement is permitted and was RE-APPROVED after the slide. codex_r8_verdict_20260827.md §Q2 (accepted) anticipates it verbatim: "실험값이 그 사이에 있어도 **numerical straddling** 이지 물리적 상·하한이 아니다" — only the physical-bound reading was retracted. And the live edit sheet docs/reviews/ms_si_v7_edit_sheet_20260901.md (2026-09-01, i.e. AFTER the 08-31 slide; last touched 09-03; header states it transcribes settled decisions and supersedes the v6 sheet) writes the same statement into the proposed manuscript text at line 183 — "The simulated ratio **brackets** this value (1.12 with the binder omitted from the electronic grid, 1.31 with its centerline voxels excluded)" — and at line 359 — "✅ 비(比)는 이미 정직하게 쓸 수 있다 — 실험 1.2310 이 우리 1.1237(PTFE 미표현) ↔ 1.3078(centerline) 사이에 든다."

THE SCRIPT CLAIM IS INVERTED. scripts/fig4b_sigma_conventions.py's docstring does not "still enforce a rejected format" — it quotes a LIVE rule. v7 line 339 (present in the current 2026-09-08 draft) reads "⚠ **두 규약을 같은 서식으로 적는다** — 굵은 글씨·`reported`·`resolved` 금지 (R10 재판정 1)", and codex_r10_verdict_20260829.md 부록 C bans the strings `reported)`, `— reported`, `resolved as blocking` while mandating the two neutral labels the script uses verbatim (LABEL_OFF / LABEL_CTR). The script's CAPTION already names centerline as the main-text value ("The value quoted in the main text uses the centerline convention; that is a reporting choice…"), so it is not co-equal in the sense alleged.

SCOPE. The file is a 주간보고 internal weekly-seminar script, not the manuscript. No document extends the manuscript nominal-convention rule to seminar decks (grep over docs/reviews and docs/manuscript returns nothing), and the slide's own ⛔ list (lines 51-60) enumerates the slide prohibitions — dual conventions is not among them. The repo's own enforcement gate passes it: `python3 scripts/check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` → "철회값 누수 없음 ✓" over 844 files.

THE PROPOSED ACTION WOULD CAUSE THE DEFECT IT CLAIMS TO FIX. Rewriting to "one value in the headline, the alternative as a sensitivity point" and redrawing Fig 4b to a nominal-convention format would violate v7 line 339 and R10 재판정 1 directly, i.e. reintroduce the bolded/primary presentation that R10 Q1 rejected on procedure grounds.

Residual (not the claimed finding): the slide headline verb "괄호로 가둠" carries the bracket framing without R8 Q2's "numerical straddling, not a physical bound" qualifier — but line 66 already supplies the operative qualifier, and the 09-01 edit sheet uses the English word "brackets" itself. At most a P3 wording nit on an internal deck, not a P1 contradiction.

summary: The prereg layer is the healthiest part of this repo's documentation: 23 documents, and in every single case where a decision line moved I could reconstruct from git and from the document's own text whether it moved before or after unblinding — the cardinal sin (moving a window after seeing results) was NOT committed anywhere. Several files are exemplary (ptfe_convention, where the registration beat the author's stated preference; ion_r_sensitivity, corrected by an editor's note that explicitly leaves the registered text untouched; sdcp_bridge A1→A3, where a self-favouring estimator was caught and reverted to the original absolute-value definition before the second grid was opened; phase_a W4, where two of the author's own pre-run forecasts missed — one by 43× — and the window still stayed put). The real damage is elsewhere and it is systematic: **six registrations whose runs are finished and whose data sits committed in the repo have never been scored against their own registered rule** (oat_seed, ion_8arm, ion_ptfe_sign — whose quantity I computed at 1.00829 ⇒ h1 — sdcp_bridge amendment A2, amendment A4's host parity, and sigma_closure §8-3/§8-4). Two ledger entries actively contradict their own preregistration (CL-68 says thresholds were never registered when oat_seed registered them six days earlier, and uses the exact phrasing that prereg forbids). Four preregs carry unmarked quotation-banned values, and they survive `--ban-sweep` for two independent reasons: the values (`+51.07 %`, `0.0277`, `1/5.41`, `×35.8`) have no pattern in `quotation_ban`, and the whole-file banner heuristic exempts four preregs outright because the standard boilerplate sentence "결과를 보고 창을 옮기면 무효다" contains the word 무효. Finally, three superseded v1 documents (sdcp_gain v1, d13 v1) lack the in-place retirement banner that lhs_extension v1 demonstrates is the house standard — and a downstream planning document still routes readers to d13 v1 as the live registration.

findings.claim: This prereg carries four values that repo canon explicitly forbids quoting — `+51.07 %` (twice), `0.0277` as the 'true-value ceiling', and `1/5.41` — with no file banner and no adjacent retraction marker, and it cites the retired CL-17 as if it were a standing result.
findings.evidence: Offending text — L25: "원고의 헤드라인 **+51.07 %** 는 전부 **점 스탬프**에서 나왔다"; L69: "참고로 2026-08-12 값은 **1.5107 (+51.07 %)**"; L18: "σ_e 는 참값 천장의 1/5.41 로 나온다"; L46: "참값 천장(0.0277)의 **6.6배 위**다 (CL-17)". Contradicting sources: docs/manuscript_sdcp_sigma_e_mechanism.md:21 and docs/sdcp_318_base_sbe_dbe_comparison.md:21 both read "> **인용 금지**: `+52.0 %` · `+51.07 %` · `+45.4 %` · `+5.6 %` · `+42.15 %` ·"; CLAUDE.md's ban list names `0.0277 = 참값 천장` and `점 → 참값 [×0.112, ×5.41]`; docs/reviews/claims.json CL-17 has status `retired` with claim "SR-01 브래킷을 실측으로 닫았다 — 참값 천장 0.0277, 점에서의 상한 배수 ×5.41". The file was edited on 2026-08-20 (commit 1da6cbdaf) — a week after CL-17 was retired — and that edit added a retraction marker to only one line (§4 f_artifact), leaving these four untouched.
findings.proposed_action: Add a file-head banner naming claims.json + CL-17/CL-19 (which also makes the ban-sweep's banner rule fire honestly), and strike or mark the four values in place, exactly as the §4 f_artifact line was marked. Do not delete: the registered text is the record of what was predicted.

findings.claim: `check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep` reports '철회값 누수 없음 ✓' while unmarked canon-banned values sit in docs/reviews, because several values named as 인용 금지 in prose have no registry pattern and rounded variants evade the ones that exist.

Yet `+51.07 %` (sr01_gate5 L25/L69), `0.0277`/`5.41` (sr01_gate5 L18/L46) have no pattern at all, and `×35.8` (fam_platen L179) is the registered `×35.79` rounded one digit. findings.claim: The ban sweep's whole-file banner exemption fires on the standard preregistration integrity sentence, so four preregs are silently exempt from the retracted-value sweep — the exemption was designed for HISTORICAL documents, not for live contracts.
findings.evidence: `_has_banner` requires a marker from BAN_BANNER_MARKS and an anchor from BAN_BANNER_ANCHORS in the first 12 lines. Probing every prereg: sdcp_next_prereg_v3 exempt on marks=['무효'] anchors=['claims.json','CL-']; sdcp_bridge_prereg_20260825 on marks=['⛔','무효']; sdcp_ion_calib_prereg_20260825 on marks=['⛔','무효']; phase_a_6mah_order_prereg_20260907 on marks=['폐기'] anchors=['CL-']. The triggering text in each case is the boilerplate "결과를 보고 (보고) 창을 옮기면 **무효**다" plus a routine ledger citation — i.e. every well-formed prereg in this repo will be exempt by construction. CLAUDE.md rule ⑤ names this exact failure mode.
findings.proposed_action: Tighten the banner rule so a live prereg cannot self-exempt — e.g. require the marker to be on the same line as the anchor, or require an explicit `HISTORICAL`/`⛔ 인용 금지` header token rather than any occurrence of 무효/폐기, and add a negative control that a prereg with the standard boilerplate plus a banned string still fails.

surviving_p0p1.claim: The ban sweep's whole-file banner exemption fires on the standard preregistration integrity sentence, so four preregs are silently exempt from the retracted-value sweep — the exemption was designed for HISTORICAL documents, not for live contracts.
surviving_p0p1.evidence: `_has_banner` requires a marker from BAN_BANNER_MARKS and an anchor from BAN_BANNER_ANCHORS in the first 12 lines. surviving_p0p1.proposed_action: Tighten the banner rule so a live prereg cannot self-exempt — e.g. require the marker to be on the same line as the anchor, or require an explicit `HISTORICAL`/`⛔ 인용 금지` header token rather than any occurrence of 무효/폐기, and add a negative control that a prereg with the standard boilerplate plus a banned string still fails.
surviving_p0p1.corrected: The whole-file banner exemption in `_has_banner` (scripts/check_review_findings.py:316-320) can be tripped by ordinary prereg header text, and in one live contract it silently suppresses four real quotation_ban violations.
