summary: This is the repo's adversarial-review corpus: 61 documents recording ~24 numbered rounds of external (Codex), semi-external (fable), and self-adversarial review between 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-08, plus the two ledgers they feed. The chronology runs RC5/RC6 (webapp provenance) → the SR-01 raster-fidelity collapse (08-12/13, which retired CL-17/18/19/20 and killed the +52 %/+42 % headline family) → CDX-01~14 and the four 08-16/08-18 deep reviews → doping + everything-else + CDX-IJ (08-19/20, which produced the ban-sweep) → the PTFE 8-arm cross-review (08-24) → four consecutive absorb NO-GOs and R5 (08-25, which created the p1/p2 protocol split and the standing quotation ban) → R7–R20 on the manuscript track (08-27 → 09-02) → the 6 mAh / Phase A / Methods rounds (09-07/08). The corpus is unusually healthy in its mechanised layer: `--ban-sweep` is clean over 844 files, `check_doc_refs` reports zero broken paths and zero unreachable commits, and CI now runs the three checkers on every push. The rot is concentrated where the machine cannot reach: (a) the two newest review *requests* (09-07 and 09-08) still assert numbers their own verdicts refuted days or hours later, including a wrong voxel grid and an inverted conductivity ratio pointed straight at a submission; (b) verdict documents for rounds R6, R11–R15, R17 and R20 were never written, so `codex_r17_verdict_20260831.md` is cited as canon by a preregistration while not existing, and `check_doc_refs` silently files that as "unsure"; (c) several disposition tables ("미착수") went stale when the work was actually completed; and (d) the second half of the 08-20 fable audit's own structural prescription — a positive `prose_canon` field so a live claim can require its derived documents to carry the *current* number — was never implemented, which is exactly the gap R10's Appendix C proved fatal ("grep 0 was a false zero"). The recurring failure patterns Codex blocked over and over are, in frequency order: **false-green checkers** (a test that passes while the thing it certifies is broken — R3-CX-01's typo'd fixture, R4's `ideal_R0` rename, R5's schema downgrade, CDXIJ-05's self-reporting Rule J, R9's fail-open replay gate, CL-74's end-leak onset); **counting arguments with likelihood ratio 1** (CL-01/02/03, "four independent readouts" that were one); **anchor and convention laundering** (σ_VGCF=100 relabelled three times, σ_SDCP=250's literature anchor retracted, ×35.79 turned from "correction factor" into "convention difference"); **statistics on a complete factorial treated as replicates** (R8 Q1, killed five times and still leaking into tool labels); **post-hoc window movement** (R7 Q2's 0.17 nominal, R16 Q2's §7 revision after the run started); and **mirror documents drifting** (Full ↔ Compact ↔ build.js ↔ build_methods_docx.py, five instances in one day per R10 Appendix C).

surface_worthy.why: This is the contract governing the only live GPU campaign in the repo (Phase A, 96 arms), buried in a 300-line Korean verdict; it holds the decision rule that replaced the arbitrary origin-spread threshold, the pre-fixed numerical deadband, and the measurement that makes the two coarse grids suspect.
surface_worthy.one_line: Phase A judges the worst arm directly — d(h,o,k) = log σ(w_{k+1}) − log σ(w_k) > δ_num = 0.04 % for every (grid, origin, adjacent pair) — and at h = 0.20/0.25 the SE necks are 85.6 %/97.4 % unresolved, so those arms are a different bed, not a coarser one.

surface_worthy.why: Q1 is the most reused statistical convention in the corpus — cited as 'R8 Q1' by at least five documents and two amendments — yet it sits inside a verdict about one specific run, and the verdict tool's own output still prints the retracted label.
surface_worthy.one_line: Eight origin shifts are a complete {0,½}³ factorial of one bed, so replication degrees of freedom are zero: sd/√8 is not a standard error, no CI may be stated, and the canonical estimator is the mean of the eight paired ratios.

surface_worthy.why: Q7 supplies the exact, ready-to-paste maximum sentence the manuscript may say about the PTFE pellet result and the reasoning that forbids anything stronger; it is the only place in the corpus where the allowed wording is written out in full English.
surface_worthy.one_line: The 0.717–1.518 mS cm⁻¹ span is a deterministic resolution/model-form bracket between two adjacent representable shell states of a binary EDT operator — neither a confidence interval nor a bound on physical fibril size, so no blocking thickness was selected and the PTFE correction is not calibrated.

surface_worthy.why: R5-CX-06 and minimum exit condition #10 are the origin of the p1/p2 protocol split and of the standing quotation ban that still holds CL-33, CL-41 and CL-58; anyone asking 'why can't I cite that ratio' has to reach this document and nothing points them here.
surface_worthy.one_line: p1 and p2 outputs are never mixed — the plate rule is part of the protocol hash, old arms are `p1-` and new arms `p2-`, and every p1 quantitative value stays quotation-banned until an eight-arm p2 re-measurement exists.

surface_worthy.why: Appendix C is the most transferable process lesson in the corpus and is appended after 110 lines of manuscript-specific adjudication, so it reads as a footnote to a closed round rather than as a standing rule.
surface_worthy.one_line: A grep written from the phrasing you just fixed returns zero and certifies nothing — check retractions with a paired banned/approved phrase list and read the two mirror versions side by side, because 'the same claim in different words' is not string-matchable.

surface_worthy.why: Four NO-GO rounds in a single day produced the corpus's four deepest engineering lessons, each marked ★★★, but they sit inside a 402-line document whose top-level table is about absorb/HOLD status.
surface_worthy.one_line: Fixtures that encode the bug defend the bug (75/75 green while every real arm was rejected); renaming a quantity does not hide it (ideal_R0 was σ_e); 'skip if absent' is disabled by deletion, so absence itself must be a violation; and type coercion rewrites the record (bool("false") is True).

surface_worthy.why: The four REFUTED premises here are still-live constraints on the Phase A campaign and on how its results may be described, and three of them contradict statements that remain unmarked in the request document next door.
surface_worthy.one_line: Mach is not common-mode across compositions (dilate-z 1.0214→1.1085 drives V/c_P 0.427→0.461), d_h/dx and SE-neck gate different quantities, the angular screen is not transferable and its own artifact is marked code_dirty, and the porosity gap closes on known terms with no residual for extra densification.

surface_worthy.why: CDXIJ-2 and CDXIJ-5 are still-open P1s describing the largest remaining structural gap in the verdict machinery — the judge does not enforce the causal-input contract, exact eight arms, origin pairing or preregistered nominal values, and pairs arms by filename sort.
surface_worthy.one_line: With two arms per bed and no origin fields the judge still returns h0, and with disjoint origin sets it reports a paired SE of 0.0 % — pairing must be by pair_id = bed digest + origin shift + fixed-contract digest, not by sorted filename.

surface_worthy.why: Item 1-1 is the cleanest instance in the repo of CLAUDE.md discipline rule ⑤ ('the code that selects candidates is the blind spot'), committed knowingly after the rule existed, and it is buried under a round-specific heading.
surface_worthy.one_line: The same raw data returned h0 or h1 depending on which scenario subset the caller passed, so the registered scenario set is now frozen in a file and compared exhaustively by name and value, with four subset regressions resident.

surface_worthy.why: Sections 15 and 16-2 contain the methodology devices that became repo-wide rules (discriminating-power field, known-answer rungs, disk-first, two-graph adjacency invariant, contamination tags, anchor scale-matching, threshold-proximity gate), but the file's correct HISTORICAL banner discourages readers from opening it at all.
surface_worthy.one_line: The rules born here still bind: cite a number as evidence only with the competing hypothesis's prediction on the same line; diagnostics must use the solver's own adjacency and grid; and near a percolation threshold, common-mode cancellation does not license relative comparison.

summary: `claims.json` is the repo's declared canon and it is in better shape than the prose around it: 104 records, no duplicate ids, no dangling `quotation_ban` claim pointers, no missing `allowed_in` paths, all 16 claim references in `findings.json` resolve, and both checkers currently run green. The numbering is intact (CL-01…CL-87 with only CL-09 absent, documented as renamed to CLP-01; CDX-09…CDX-25 complete). The census matches the brief exactly: 74 live / 20 rejected / 6 hold / 4 retired. What is wrong is concentrated in three places. **(1) The enforcement arm has a self-defeating escape hatch**: `BAN_NEAR_MARKS` includes the bare string `'CL-'`, so any banned value sitting within ±2 lines of a claim id is exempt — 21 occurrences across CLAUDE.md, the manuscript generator, a wiki page and an absorb map pass the sweep for that reason alone, and the code comment directly above that list says the near-exemption was deliberately narrowed to "retraction-only vocabulary." **(2) The 2026-08-25 p1 plate-rule hold was applied to the three claims Codex named (CL-33/41/58) but not to their siblings**: the banned strings `1.1232` / `1.123191` / `+12.3 %` are registered under CL-33 yet are actually produced and headlined by **CL-34, which is `live`**, and the p1 σ_e *absolute* values (0.07302 / 0.08224 / 0.072651) — which the hold_reason says change *first* under p2 — are not registered at all and circulate freely in CLAUDE.md. **(3) Retractions stop at the claim that issued them**: CL-72 retracted the "monotone ⇒ lower bound" reading on 2026-09-07, but CL-41, CL-65, CLAUDE.md:95, `manuscript_draft/build.js` and the wiki all still assert it, and neither CL-41 nor CL-72 cross-references the other. Secondary issues: three of six `hold` claims carry no release condition and the checker skips `hold` records entirely; CL-59's string-typed `resolution` is a latent unhandled `ValueError` inside a fail-closed gate that has already blocked a GPU run once; four claims still carry pre-run "미측정" framing after being measured; and the wiki map layer has an entity page for `findings.json` but none for `claims.json`, so the declared canon is unreachable from the designated entry point.

findings.claim: The quotation ban can be defeated by citing the ledger: `BAN_NEAR_MARKS` treats the bare string `'CL-'` as a retraction marker, so any banned value with a claim id within ±2 lines is silently exempt. 21 occurrences in the repo pass the sweep for that reason alone.
findings.evidence: Offending code: `BAN_NEAR_MARKS = ('인용 금지', '철회', '반증', '폐기', '무효', '~~', 'CL-')`. Contradicted by its own comment three lines above (check_review_findings.py:150-153): "⚠⚠ 2026-08-20 (Codex 재검증 IJ-04, 2차) — 줄-근처 면제도 **철회 전용 어휘**만 인정한다. … 그 둘은 문서 머리 배너 어휘이지 '이 값은 철회됐다' 는 진술이 아니다. ⇒ 근처 면제에서 뺀다 (⛔ 도 뺀다 — 그 기호 하나로는 무엇이 철회됐는지 말하지 않는다)." A claim id is weaker than ⛔, which was removed for exactly this reason. Measured impact (re-ran the sweep logic with `'CL-'` removed from the marker tuple): 21 occurrences flip from exempt to ERROR, including `CLAUDE.md:186` ("= 헤드라인 +12.3 % 가 이 축에 **하한**이라는 CL-46 서술이 실측으로 뒷받침됐다"), `CLAUDE.md:195`, `docs/manuscript_draft/build.js:383-386` ("비 1.1232 도 격자와 함께 **단조 증가**한다 (0.15 → 0.125 → 0.115 에서 1.1232 → 1.1438 → 1.1554) 이므로 **하한**으로 읽어야 한다"), `docs/report_mpm_and_sigma_usability_20260819.md:80`, `docs/reviews/absorb_map_stoic_20260825.md:68,70`, `wiki/questions/sr01-delta-sigma-sign.md:33`. Marker introduced in commit `1da6cbdaf`.
findings.proposed_action: Remove `'CL-'` from `BAN_NEAR_MARKS` and re-run `--ban-sweep`; triage the 21 revealed occurrences (most need either a real `철회`/`인용 금지` word on the line or the value removed). Add a selftest fixture that is a ledger-style table row (`| **CL-41** | live | … 1.123191 …|`) and assert it FAILS — this is the exact shape the current rule lets through.

findings.locator: quotation_ban entries at lines 2333/2341/2357/2365/2373 (`claim: "CL-33"`) vs claim record CL-34 at line 1235
findings.claim: The four banned strings `1.1232`, `1.123191`, `+12.3 %`, `+12.32` are registered as belonging to CL-33 (`hold`), but the claim that produced and headlines those numbers is CL-34 — whose status is `live`, with no `hold_reason`, no `hold_since`, no `superseded_by_protocol` and no p1/plate-rule banner anywhere in its body. A reader following the registry lands on a held claim and concludes the live one is a separate, citable result.
findings.evidence: Registry: `{"pattern": "1.123191", "claim": "CL-33", "why": "같은 값의 정밀 표기"}` and `{"pattern": "+12.3 %", "claim": "CL-33", "why": "1.1232 의 백분율 표기 — 같은 p1 산물"}`. But CL-33's own `measured.value` is the POINT-stamp result ("σ_e SBE 0.072651 … DBE 0.073835 → 비 **1.0163**") — the string `1.1232` does not appear in CL-33 at all. It appears in CL-34, whose `claim` field reads: "SDCP 를 **참 직경 구**로 그리면 σ_e 이득이 **+12.3 %**" and whose `measured.value` reads "비 **1.123191 (+12.32 %)**". Programmatic check across all 104 records: `1.123191` occurs in CL-34(live), CL-41(hold), CL-58(hold) — never in CL-33. Contradicting canon: CL-33's `hold_reason` ("이 값들은 전부 **p1 plate rule** … ★ **비도 안전하지 않다** … ⇒ 재측정(새 p2 GPU 8팔) 전까지 **인용 금지**") plainly covers the same 8-arm vox-0.15 run CL-34 reports. Rule G in check_method_discipline.py:717 only fires on `superseded_by` + live, which CL-34 does not have, so nothing catches it.
findings.proposed_action: Either move CL-34 to `hold` with the same `hold_reason`/`hold_since`/`superseded_by_protocol` as CL-33/41/58, or repoint the four registry entries to `CL-34` and add an explicit p1 banner block to CL-34. findings.claim: Three of the six `hold` claims carry no stated release condition — no `hold_reason`, no `hold_since`, no `superseded_by_protocol` — and the checker skips every `hold` record without validating anything, so a hold can sit indefinitely with no machine-readable way to know what would lift it.
findings.evidence: Field audit of all hold records: CL-33, CL-41, CL-58 each carry `hold_reason` + `hold_since: 2026-08-25` + `superseded_by_protocol: p2-occupied-surface-first`; CL-23, CL-30, CL-31 carry none of the three. The checker prints them anyway: `if st == 'hold': print(f'  HOLD    {c["id"]}: {str(c.get("hold_reason", ""))[:66]}'); continue` — live output confirms three bare lines, "HOLD    CL-23: ", "HOLD    CL-30: ", "HOLD    CL-31: ". The `continue` means no required-field, rule-C, rule-D or rule-G check runs on any hold record. Contradicting canon: `_status_vocab` defines hold as "증거가 재측정 대기 — **인용 금지**" (evidence awaiting RE-MEASUREMENT), which presupposes a stated measurement that would release it. The three release conditions do exist in prose but only inside the claim bodies (CL-23: `couple_to_voxel_grid` does not exist; CL-30: superseded by CL-74's onset fix; CL-31: "다시 재려면 vox ≤ 0.15 에서만, … 0.15/0.125/0.10 이 필요하다").
findings.proposed_action: Add `hold_reason` + `hold_since` to CL-23/30/31 (text already exists in their bodies), and make `check_claim` require both fields for `status == 'hold'` instead of skipping the record. Keep the rest of the hold exemption.

findings.claim: CL-10 is `live` and its verdict concludes that the retracted +52 % headline is robust. Four claims from the 2026-08-12 cohort (CL-10/11/13/14) were built on the vox-0.4 point-stamp σ_e family and none of them carries any retraction banner or pointer to CL-24/CL-33, unlike CL-21/22/24/25 which all received dated downgrade blocks the next day.
findings.evidence: CL-10 verdict: "h0 채택 — 관측 Δ비 = 0.93 %p ≪ 4.0.  ⇒ **원고 +52 % 는 파이프라인 드리프트에 강건**." `+52 %` is registered in `quotation_ban` (`{"pattern": "+52 %", "claim": "CL-24", "why": "같은 철회 헤드라인의 표기 변형"}`). Contradicted by CL-24 (live): "원고의 '전자 +52 % · 이온 +5.6 %' 는 0.4 µm 격자의 산물이다" and by CL-33: "⇒ **+52 % · +42 % 헤드라인 최종 철회**." Programmatic string check on CL-10, CL-13, CL-14: none contains any of 철회 / 인용 금지 / 하향 / 반증 / ⛔ / HISTORICAL / CL-24 / CL-33. CL-11 contains 인용 금지 but only about an unrelated ionic-axis aside. CL-11 and CL-13 additionally still treat σ_e 2.056 / 3.106 S/cm and the derived HS realization fractions as current. `claims.json` is in `BAN_ALLOW_ALWAYS`, so the ban sweep cannot catch this.
findings.proposed_action: Append a dated downgrade block to CL-10/11/13/14 in the style already used on CL-21/22/24 ("── 2026-08-13 Codex 적대 리뷰 반영 ──"), stating which part survives (CL-10: the common-mode-cancellation measurement; CL-11: the sub-linear exponent 0.32; CL-13: the topology-realization argument; CL-14: the electronic-ohmic-drop bound) and which is retracted (the +52 % magnitude in all four).

findings.claim: The registry bans the p1 σ_e *ratios* but not the p1 σ_e *absolute values* from the same runs, even though CL-33/41/58's own hold_reason says the p2 change alters the absolutes first. 0.07302 / 0.08224 / 0.072651 circulate unmarked in CLAUDE.md and five review documents.
findings.evidence: hold_reason (identical in CL-33, CL-41, CL-58): "p2(`p2-occupied-surface-first`) 는 판에 붙는 셀 집합을 바꾸므로 **σ_e 절대값이 달라진다**. ★ **비도 안전하지 않다**…" — i.e. absolutes are the primary affected quantity and ratios are the secondary concern. Yet none of the 22 registered patterns is an absolute; all are ratios, percentages, or the `f_artifact` / `×35.79` / `9.4 %` strings. Live occurrences of the unregistered absolutes: `CLAUDE.md:129` ("★ 회귀도 통과 (2a 가 0.07302/0.08224 재현)"), `CLAUDE.md:133` ("음성 대조 통과 (SBE no-op, 0.07302 동일)"), `docs/reviews/sdcp_phase_displacement_20260818.md:127-128`, `docs/reviews/sdcp_next_prereg_v3_20260818.md:56`, `docs/reviews/deep_review_20260816_discipline.md:28,144`, `docs/reviews/deep_review_20260816_stats.md:9,33`. All three carrying claims (CL-32, CL-39, CL-44) are `live`.
findings.proposed_action: Decide whether the p1 absolutes are quotation-banned. If yes, register `0.07302`, `0.08224`, `0.072651`, `0.081601` (each is distinctive enough not to false-positive) and mark the CLAUDE.md/doc occurrences. If no, say so explicitly in the three `hold_reason` texts so the asymmetry is a stated decision rather than an omission.

findings.claim: CL-59's `resolution` is a free-text string where every other claim uses a number. It is a latent unhandled `ValueError` in `check_method_discipline.py`; the checker survives today only because an unrelated early-return fires first, and this checker is a fail-closed gate that has already blocked a GPU run once.
findings.evidence: Offending value: `"resolution": "판정선은 두 조건의 곱이고 사전등록 §4 에서 동결됐다"`. All other 35 non-null resolutions are int/float. Consuming code (check_method_discipline.py, `_reject_reasons`): `res = c.get('resolution'); if res is not None and len(n0) == 1 and len(n1) == 1: if abs(n0[0] - n1[0]) < float(res):`. CL-59 escapes only because its `h0_predicts` ("부호 갈림 또는 W ≥ 0.30") and `h1_predicts` ("같은 부호 ∧ W ≤ 0.10") trip the complementary-inequality early return above it. Reproduced directly: importing the checker and calling `check_claim` on CL-59 with only the two predict strings rewritten as point predictions raises `ValueError: could not convert string to float: '판정선은 두 조건의 곱이고 사전등록 §4 에서 동결됐다'`. Contradicting canon on the consequence: CLAUDE.md — "⚠ 두 번째는 러너의 fail-closed 게이트라 **사용자의 GPU 런을 막았다** … 원장 오타 하나가 계산을 세운다."
findings.proposed_action: Move the sentence to a new key (e.g. `resolution_note`) and set `resolution` to the numeric threshold or `null`; add a type check in `check_claim` so a non-numeric `resolution` is a reported ledger error rather than a traceback.

findings.claim: The merge map's §4 table — whose stated purpose is "흡수 시 이 판정들이 살아남아야 한다" — records CL-41 and CL-58 as `live` when both have been `hold` since the same day, quotes all four of their quotation-banned values verbatim, and repeats the lower-bound reading CL-72 later retracted. The file has no head banner and passes the sweep only via the `'CL-'` near-mark.
findings.evidence: Offending rows: "| **CL-41** | live | 세 점 완주 (0.15/0.125/0.115 → 1.123191/1.143817/1.155448). … Richardson 무의미, 보고값은 전부 **하한** |" and "| **CL-58** | live · measurement_record | 도핑 baseline — σ_e **1.123214** · σ_ion **0.992720** … **전자 +12.3 % / 이온 −0.73 %** |". Contradicted by claims.json: CL-41 and CL-58 both carry `"status": "hold"` with `"hold_since": "2026-08-25"`; `1.123191`, `1.143817`, `1.155448`, `1.123214` and `+12.3 %` are all registered `quotation_ban` patterns; and the lower-bound reading is retracted by CL-72. Sweep behaviour verified programmatically: `_has_banner()` returns False for this file and `ban_sweep()` returns 0 problems, because the rows contain the literal `CL-`. File last modified 2026-08-25 02:21 (`a5c0a9bf3`), i.e. hours before the R5-CX-06 hold.
findings.proposed_action: Add a head banner pointing at `docs/reviews/claims.json` (which makes the file legitimately exempt as a frozen merge-time snapshot), or update the two status cells to `hold` and replace the values with `—`. Do not leave it exempt by accident of the `CL-` marker.

findings.locator: CL-34 (line 1235), CL-38 (line 1312), CL-48 (line 1526) — first line of `verdict`
findings.claim: Three live claims open their `verdict` field with a status line that their `status` field contradicts: CL-34 and CL-38 begin "★ **status = hold…**" while both are `live`; CL-48 begins "★ **미실행.**" while its `measured.value` is `-0.1084` and it has a judged h1 verdict. Any reader or tool taking the first line of `verdict` gets the opposite of the record's state.
findings.evidence: CL-34 `status: live`, verdict opens: "★ **status = hold.  이 +12.6 % 를 인용하지 말 것** — 두 가지가 미해결이다" (the release is 60 lines further down, "── 2026-08-18 **hold 해제 (8/8 완주)** ── ★ **status = live.**"). CL-38 `status: live`, verdict opens: "★ **status = hold.  이 값을 σ_e 검증 앵커로 인용하지 말 것**" (released at "══════ 2026-09-02 · **HOLD 해제** — SI v6 Table S4 가 가른다 ══════"). CL-48 `status: live`, verdict opens "★ **미실행.**" while `measured` reads `{"value": -0.1084}` and the body records "── 2026-09-02 **2차 실행 = 판정 h1 (두 팔 수렴)** ──". The stale CL-38 label has already propagated outward: CL-49's body says "CL-38[hold] ↔ '+23.1 % 샌드위치'" and `docs/report_mpm_and_sigma_usability_20260819.md:81` says "⚠ **필수 단서 (CL-38 [hold], 2026-08-20 화해 기록)**".
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite the first line of each `verdict` to the current state and move the superseded opening into the dated history block below it, following the pattern CL-31 already uses ("⛔ **헤드라인 철회** (2026-08-18) —" as the leading text). Then fix the two downstream `CL-38 [hold]` labels.

findings.locator: lines 19-24, the SR-01 ★★ 인용 금지 목록
findings.claim: CLAUDE.md declares its 14-item prohibition list to be the prose twin of the machine registry, but 8 of the 14 items have no matching pattern in `quotation_ban` and therefore cannot be enforced by `--ban-sweep`.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md's own framing: "(아래 문자열은 **등록부 본문**이다 — `claims.json` `quotation_ban` 의 산문 쌍둥이.  인용 금지)". Programmatic comparison of the 14 prose items against the 22 registered patterns: covered = `+52.0 %`, `+5.6 %`, `+42.15 %`, `f_artifact = 0.147`, `×35.79`. NOT covered = `14.7 % 인공물 / 85.3 % 물리`, `0.0277 = 참값 천장`, `브래킷 [0.000574, 0.0277] 폭 48.2배`, `점 → 참값 [×0.112, ×5.41]`, `σ_e 절대값 2.67~4.62배 과대`, `규약 민감도 ≈ 7.4 % × VGCF wt%`, `직경-보존 σ 는 하한`, `1D 망 = 격자 의존의 근본 해법`, `실험의 3.6배`. Live consequence: `docs/reviews/sr01_gate5_prereg_20260813.md:46` states "참값 천장(0.0277)의 **6.6배 위**다 (CL-17)" with no head banner and no nearby retraction word, and the sweep reports zero leaks. Note the registry's own `_quotation_ban_why` explains the tension: "⚠ pattern 은 **문맥 포함 문자열**로 쓴다 — 맨 숫자는 오탐이 폭발한다" — and a bare `0.0277` would indeed false-positive on the legitimate raw measurement on CLAUDE.md:217.
findings.proposed_action: Either register context-bearing patterns for the 8 uncovered items (e.g. `참값 천장`, `폭 48.2배`, `[×0.112, ×5.41]`, `2.67~4.62배`, `7.4 % × VGCF`, `실험의 3.6배`) or delete the 'prose twin' framing and label the CLAUDE.md list as human-only, stating which subset the machine enforces.

findings.claim: CL-50's appended correction block is a byte-identical copy of CL-47's and anchors itself to a "범주 비대칭" paragraph that does not exist in CL-50; the phrase it retracts actually lives in CL-50's "표기 규약" bullet.
findings.evidence: Both blocks read verbatim: "★ 위 '범주 비대칭' 문단의 *\"σ_SDCP 250 = **재료 앵커**(S-PEDOT 벌크)\"* 는 **철회한다**…" — programmatic comparison of the two blocks returns `IDENTICAL: True`. Programmatic search for the anchor string: `'범주 비대칭' in CL-47 body before the block` → True; `'범주 비대칭' in CL-50 body before the block` → False. In CL-50 the retracted phrase appears instead in the bullet "· 표기 규약: 상별 σ 를 비교할 때 **\"이 규약 안에서\"** 를 반드시 붙인다 — σ_SDCP 250 = 재료 앵커 · σ_VGCF 100 = 유효 망 상수(CL-47) · σ_AM 10/5 = 적합 endpoint(CL-50)." A reader searching CL-50 for the named paragraph finds nothing and may conclude the correction was misfiled.
findings.proposed_action: Retarget CL-50's block to name the '표기 규약' bullet, or strike the retracted label in place (`~~재료 앵커~~ → Assumed (저자 지정)`) so the correction lands on the text it corrects.

findings.claim: Four measured claims still carry pre-run framing in their `claim` field — the one field a summary or index would read first. Each says "런 전 등록 (미측정)" while carrying a full `measured.value` and a judged verdict.
findings.evidence: CL-44 `claim`: "**사전등록 v3 STEP 5 (런 전 등록, 미측정)** — SDCP 이득이…" vs `measured.value`: "생산 규약  SBE 0.07302 · DBE 0.08224 · R 1.126267 · G **+0.12627** …". CL-45 `claim`: "**런 전 등록 (미측정)** — vox 0.4 에서도…" vs `measured.value`: "**완주 2026-08-20 (두 팔).**…" and `date_resolved: 2026-08-20`. CL-48 `claim`: "**런 전 등록 (미측정)** — σ_VGCF 를…" vs `measured.value`: `-0.1084`. CL-49 `claim`: "**런 전 등록 (미측정)** — PTFE 를…" vs `measured.value`: "SBE 0.07302 → **0.05463** S/cm (−25.2 %)…". Contradicted by CLAUDE.md, which already reports all four as complete: "⑤ ~~σ-치환 판별 팔~~ **완료 = h1** (CL-44) · ~~후속 CL-45~~ **완료 = `BOTH_REJECTED`**" and "⑨ ~~CL-49 PTFE 스탬프 팔~~ **완료 = BOTH_REJECTED**".
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite the four `claim` fields to state the measured result, and move the pre-run registration language into the `prereg`/`asserted` fields where it belongs. CLAUDE.md's strikethrough convention (`~~…~~ **완료 = h1**`) is the pattern to copy.

findings.claim: The wiki RQ card presents CL-34/CL-41 as "the currently valid route" and quotes both quotation-banned ratios, and it attributes CL-23's unimplemented-coupling gap to CL-21.
findings.evidence: Line 32-34: "> * **CL-34/CL-41** — 지금 유효한 노선은 **구(球) 스탬프**다 … σ_e 비 = 1.1232(vox 0.15) · 1.1438(0.125), **아직 미수렴**." Contradicted by claims.json: CL-41 `"status": "hold"`, `"hold_since": "2026-08-25"`, and `1.1232` is a registered `quotation_ban` pattern. Line 30: "> * **CL-21** — 선분(1D 저항망)도 **수렴하지 않았고** `couple_to_voxel_grid` 가 없어 실침대 σ_e 를 내지 못한다." Programmatic check: `'couple_to_voxel_grid' in CL-21` → False and `'1D' in CL-21` → False; the missing-coupling statement is CL-23's ("복셀 FV(AM·SE·SDCP)와의 결합은 미구현 — … 그때까지 이 모듈은 실침대 σ_e 를 못 낸다", status `hold`). Card frontmatter `updated: 2026-08-20`, i.e. five days before the hold.
findings.proposed_action: Update the card: mark CL-41 as `hold`, replace the two ratios with a pointer to the ledger, and reattribute the `couple_to_voxel_grid` line to CL-23. Bump `updated`.

findings.claim: The `CDX-` prefix carries two incompatible meanings. CDX-09…CDX-25 are claim ids in this ledger, while CDX-01…CDX-08 appearing inside claim bodies are 2026-08-13 Codex *review-finding* numbers from a different document. Following a body citation into the ledger lands on an unrelated claim.
findings.evidence: `_id_policy`: "Codex 스윕 추가안(claims_codex_sweep_additions_20260812.json)의 ID 도 CL-09~CL-25 라 **충돌한다** — 병합 시 그쪽을 CDX-* 로 접두어를 붙여 넣는다" — this documents the CL→CDX renaming but not the resulting collision with the review-finding series. Concrete collision: CL-24's body says "── 2026-08-13 Codex 적대 리뷰 반영 ── **하향** (Codex CDX-03/13)", where CDX-13 means `docs/reviews/codex_review_response_20260816.md:41` ("| CDX-13 | 정량 h1 이 사후 적합 |"); but `CDX-13` in this same ledger is "The four-pressure DEM Heckel fit establishes granular yield pressure P_y=137.8 MPa…" — a different subject entirely. Same pattern for CDX-01 (cited in CL-17/21/22/25 meaning the SDCP one-cell-per-point finding, vs claim CDX-01 which does not exist) through CDX-08. Repo-wide grep confirms CDX-01…CDX-08 appear only in `codex_review_response_20260816.md`, `review_request_20260816.md`, three scripts, and claim bodies — never as ledger ids.
findings.proposed_action: Rename the in-body review-finding citations to a distinct prefix (e.g. `CDXR1-01`, matching the existing `CDX-R2-xx` and `R5-CX-xx` conventions) or spell them as "Codex 2026-08-13 #3", and record the resolved namespace in `_id_policy`.

findings.claim: Five `live` claims are referenced nowhere outside `claims.json` — no doc, script, wiki page or CLAUDE.md line points at them — so nothing would notice if they went stale, and two of them carry results other claims depend on.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide `git grep -oh -E '(CL|CDX|CLP)-[0-9]+' -- . ':!docs/reviews/claims.json'` gives reference count 0 for CL-37, CL-64, CL-65, CL-84 and CDX-19 (compare CL-33 at 91 refs, CL-41 at 84, CL-24 at 75). Load-bearing content sitting in them: CL-37 is the real-bed phase-volume ledger that closes three separate caveats ("★ 세 가지가 이 원장으로 닫힌다: ① CL-25 의 '실침대는 상한' 캐비엇 — 해소 ② CL-34 의 우선순위 결함 크기 — **정확히 0 셀** ③ SBE 음성 대조 — 셀 단위 완전 동일로 승격") — yet CL-25 and CL-34 cite the numbers inline rather than pointing at CL-37. CDX-19 is the single live claim from the entire Codex sweep ("KEEP for this bed as a discriminating pressure series"). The other ten unreferenced CDX records (CDX-15/16/17/18/20/22/23/24/25) are not true orphans — they are exercised every run as rejected-specimen fixtures by `check_claims_ledger`, though only CL-01/02/03 are pinned by `_REQUIRED_REJECTED`.
findings.proposed_action: Cite CL-37 from CL-25 and CL-34 where their numbers come from it; give CL-64/CL-65 a pointer from the litdb application backlog or the wiki; and either reference CDX-19 from `docs/mpm_wallP_conditional_troubleshooting.md` (its own `location` field) or note that it is deliberately archival.

findings.locator: CL-04, CL-06, CL-07, CLP-01, CDX-19, CL-39, CL-40, CL-41, CL-57 — field `provenance`
findings.claim: Nine live-or-hold claims carry no `provenance` field. The checker requires it only for non-hypothesis kinds, so hypothesis claims that have since been *measured* keep their results with no machine-readable pointer to the run that produced them — including CL-41, a `hold` record whose p1 values are the ones under quotation ban.
findings.evidence: Field audit: 76 of 104 records have `provenance`; the nine above are `live`/`hold` and lack it. Enforcement gap in check_method_discipline.py:706-711 — `provenance` is demanded only in the `else` branch, i.e. `if c.get('kind','hypothesis') == 'hypothesis': [require h0/h1/...] else: if not c.get('provenance'): error`. CL-39, CL-40 and CL-41 are all `kind: hypothesis` with completed measurements (CL-39: "── 2026-08-18 **실측 · 판정 = h0** ──", CL-40: "**완주 2026-08-20**", CL-41: "★★ **8팔 완주 (2026-08-19)**") whose run pointers exist only as free text inside `measured.value` (e.g. CL-39's "원자료: kgy prereg_v2_vox015_sph_b048_lean · prereg_v2_vox015_sph_b048_sg113097_lean"). Contradicted by the standing rule CL-75 established: "⇒ **상주 규칙 신설: 측정 JSON 은 그것을 만든 커밋 SHA 를 자기 안에 적는다.  없으면 인용하지 않는다.**"
findings.proposed_action: Require `provenance` on any claim that has a non-empty `measured.value`, regardless of `kind`, and backfill the nine — CL-41 first, since its values are the ones a p2 re-measurement must be able to locate and compare against.

findings.claim: Claim records have a `date` (registration) but no last-amended date, while bodies are amended for weeks afterwards. Freshness is therefore not machine-readable, which is exactly what a newest-first hub needs.
findings.evidence: Field-frequency audit across all 104 records shows the full key set: id, date, status, claim, measured, asserted, verdict, bridge, kind, provenance, h0, h1, h0_predicts, h1_predicts, shared_input, resolution, reviews_work_dated, location, expected_violations, origin, codex_review, prereg, date_resolved, hold_reason, hold_since, superseded_by_protocol, sign_correction, superseded_by, causal_hypothesis, artifact_state, evidence_state, legacy_measurement, date_partial, shared_input_note. No `updated`. Concrete divergence: CL-38 carries `"date": "2026-08-18"` yet its body contains blocks dated 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-03; CL-34 is dated 2026-08-16 with blocks through 2026-08-20; CL-25 is dated 2026-08-16 with a 2026-08-18 grid-sweep table. `reviews_work_dated` exists on 42 records but means something different (the date of the review being responded to) — e.g. CL-25/26/27/28/29 all carry `reviews_work_dated: 2026-08-13` while `date` is 2026-08-16.
findings.proposed_action: Add an `updated` key set on every amendment, and have `check_claim` require it whenever the body contains a dated block later than `date`. This is the single cheapest change for a newest-first hub view.

findings.locator: line 22 (the ledger entry) and the whole `wiki/entities/` set
findings.claim: The wiki map layer has an entity page and an index entry for `findings.json` but nothing at all for `claims.json`. Since CLAUDE.md designates the wiki index as the 'what was X again' entry point and designates claims.json as canon, the canonical ledger is unreachable from the map.

summary: Every checker in scope is currently GREEN — check_review_findings 36/36 selftest + ledger self-consistent + ban-sweep "누수 없음", check_method_discipline 128/128 selftest + 0 errors on the repo, check_selftest_inventory 21/21 + "전부 분류돼 있다", and check_all's repo-real lane passes. That green is the problem: the audit's findings are almost entirely things the green lights hide. Three structural defects dominate. (1) The retracted-value sweep's line-near exemption still accepts the bare token `CL-`, the single most common incidental string in this repo; I proved by mutation that removing one unrelated `CL-49` reference from an adjacent line in `docs/manuscript_draft/build.js` immediately exposes three occurrences of the quotation-banned `1.1232`, and repo-wide 21 ban hits ride on `CL-` alone — including CLAUDE.md quoting `+12.3 %` twice as a live headline. This is the same self-authorizing hole the checker's own comment claims to have closed in August by removing HISTORICAL/retired/⛔. (2) `check_claims_ledger` `continue`s on `status: hold` before scoring anything, so the six quotation-banned hold claims bypass required-field, `kind`, `status` and rule-G validation entirely — I verified an empty hold claim and a hold claim with `kind: NOT_A_KIND` both produce zero errors, which is exactly the defect class (invalid `kind` in claims.json) that CLAUDE.md records as having blocked the user's GPU runs. (3) findings.json has not been touched since 2026-09-02 while claims.json advanced to CL-87 on 2026-09-08; seven review documents dated 09-07/09-08, including a Codex verdict carrying two P0 tool defects and a Methods SUBMISSION HOLD carrying five P1s, have zero entries in the findings ledger. Consequently at least six of the nineteen "open" items are wholly or largely discharged (R20-05 by CL-70, R5CX-09 by the step3_sigma production-helper selftest, CDXIJ-2 by CDXIJ-10, R20-06 by the network_conductivity relabel, DR3-05 by CL-39, R20-03's digest edit) and several carry notes that are now factually false — CDXIJ-2 still states "paired 통계가 파일명 정렬 zip 이다" although origin-key join landed at sdcp_gain_verdict.py:958-963, and SELF-13 still recommends switching σ_VGCF to 83, which R20-04 in the same review refutes as a category error. Conversely R5CX-06 is marked `claimed_fixed` while the exact contradiction it names ("인용 금지 선언과 정본 원장이 반대다") is still live in CL-34, CLAUDE.md and build.js. Coverage of the checkers themselves is narrower than advertised: rule O scans one of two manuscript generators and misses the one that already contains six British spellings in co-author prose; rule A scores the grid axis against an unverified static literal `vox_um: 0.4` while production runs at 0.15; `check_undefined_names.py` never runs against the repo in either lane and exits 1 with 1,553 hits; and lanes drift in both directions (`webapp/test_seminar_dom.mjs` is CI-only, `check_cohort_packages.py` repo-real is check_all-only) with nothing able to detect it, contradicting check_all.sh's closing promise that "CI 가 같은 것을 다시 돈다".

findings.claim: The retracted-value sweep's line-near exemption accepts the bare token `CL-`, so any incidental claim reference on an adjacent line silently authorises a banned value two lines away — the exact self-authorising hole the checker's own comment says it closed. Proven by mutation: removing one unrelated `CL-49` from a neighbouring line exposes three hidden occurrences of the banned `1.1232`.
findings.evidence: Offending code: `BAN_NEAR_MARKS = ('인용 금지', '철회', '반증', '폐기', '무효', '~~', 'CL-')` (check_review_findings.py:154). Contradicted by the comment immediately above it (lines 150-153): "줄-근처 면제도 **철회 전용 어휘**만 인정한다. 실측: 근처에 *무관한* 'HISTORICAL'/'retired' 한 단어만 있어도 면제됐다. 그 둘은 문서 머리 **배너** 어휘이지 '이 값은 철회됐다' 는 진술이 아니다." Measured: `ban_sweep('.')` returns 0 leaks; the same sweep on a scratchpad copy of docs/manuscript_draft/build.js with only the string `(CL-49)` on line 384 replaced by `(see ledger)` returns 3 leaks at lines 383/385/386 for pattern `1.1232`. Repo-wide, dropping 'CL-' from BAN_NEAR_MARKS turns 0 leaks into 21, including CLAUDE.md:186 and :195.
findings.proposed_action: Remove 'CL-' from BAN_NEAR_MARKS and require a retraction verb ('인용 금지', '철회', '반증', '폐기', '무효', '~~'). If a claim id must remain an exemption token, require it to be adjacent to a retraction verb on the same line (e.g. regex `CL-\d+\s*(?:hold|철회|인용 금지)`). Add a negative control to _selftest mirroring the mutation above: an unrelated `CL-nn` near a banned value must NOT exempt it.

Also contradicted by check_review_findings.py:121-123: "★ 생성기에는 **파일 전체 면제를 주지 않는다** — 출력이 배너로 면제되는 이상, 표 셀을 실제로 지키는 자리는 여기뿐이다." findings.claim: Claims with status `hold` bypass every check in check_claim — required fields, status/kind vocabulary, rule G, and all reject patterns — because the loop computes `bad = check_claim(c)` and then discards it. The exact defect class CLAUDE.md records as having blocked the user's GPU runs (an invalid `kind` in claims.json) is now invisible for the six hold claims, which are precisely the quotation-banned ones.
findings.evidence: Offending code: `for c in claims:  bad = check_claim(c);  st = c.get('status');  if st == 'hold': ... continue`. Contradicted by CLAUDE.md: "같은 실수를 두 번 했다 (CLAUDE.md 에 철회값 인용 · `claims.json` 에 유효하지 않은 `kind`) — 둘 다 selftest 는 초록이었고 CI 가 60 초 뒤 빨간불을 냈다. ⚠ 두 번째는 러너의 fail-closed 게이트라 **사용자의 GPU 런을 막았다**." findings.claim: The static NameError gate built specifically after a run died on `NameError: _zt3` never runs against the repo in either lane. findings.evidence: Offending state: inventory row `scripts/check_undefined_names.py\t--selftest\tfast\tnone\tclaude\t초록 0.4s (실측)`; grep for 'check_undefined_names' in scripts/check_all.sh and .github/workflows/discipline.yml returns nothing. summary: The wiki is structurally immaculate and epistemically frozen. Every machine gate is green — lint reports 0 errors / 0 warnings, all 28 tool selftests pass, and the repo-wide quotation-ban sweep reports zero leaks — yet `git log` shows 19 of 21 pages have not been touched since the day they were created (2026-08-11, commit d92d42534), and the only two later commits (4c7351212, 1da6cbdaf, both 2026-08-20) edited exactly the three lines the ban sweep forced them to. The wiki therefore stops one day before the 2026-08-13 Codex adversarial review that retired CL-17/18/19/20 and rejected the entire "independent cross-validation" family of arguments (CDX-16/17/18/21/23/24), and it contains nothing at all from the 08-16→09-08 work: sphere stamping, prereg v2/v3, the p1 plate-rule quotation hold (R5-CX-06), CL-61's retraction of the σ_SDCP anchor, the 2026-09-03 litdb multi-INDEX incident, Phase A, the manuscript SUBMISSION HOLD, or CL-81's finding that the voxel solver sits on the contact-network's own `CONTACT_FREE` branch. The result is that five pages now assert things the ledger has explicitly refuted, three pages prescribe procedures that have since caused documented incidents, one page cites the wrong CSV column for the defect it exists to describe, and one page presents two `hold`-status p1 plate-rule ratios as the currently-valid answer — passing the ban sweep only because a bare `CL-` string two lines above satisfies the proximity exemption. The green lint is itself the diagnosis: the wiki's checker validates frontmatter shape, link resolution and index arithmetic, but never cross-checks a page against `claims.json` status, never re-reads the numbers it copied, and — unlike every other checker in the repo — is wired into neither `scripts/check_all.sh` nor `.github/workflows/discipline.yml`, which is precisely the "검사기가 수동이면 없는 것과 같다" failure CLAUDE.md rule ④ was written to stop. Beneath the staleness the design is genuinely good and worth keeping: the five orthogonal quality axes, the litdb boundary rule, the model-ID lint error and the counter-argument-preservation convention are all sound; what is missing is (a) honest use of the `updated`/`confidence`/`verificationStatus` fields — 17 of 21 pages claim `confidence: high` while 21 of 21 have never been through `/wiki-verify` and 21 of 21 remain `explored: false` — and (b) any page at all for the layers canon calls authoritative: `claims.json`, the `quotation_ban` registry, the preregistration contract, the discipline checkers, and the live scientific tracks. As a hub for a future session, the wiki today would route that session confidently into five retracted positions and would never mention that a quotation ban exists.

findings.locator: lines 32-34, inside the retraction banner blockquote
findings.claim: The page presents two quotation-banned, `hold`-status p1 plate-rule ratios as the currently-valid answer, and the ban sweep passes only because a bare `CL-` string on the preceding line satisfies the proximity exemption — the numbers themselves carry no retraction marker.
findings.evidence: Page text: "* **CL-34/CL-41** — 지금 유효한 노선은 **구(球) 스탬프**다 (SDCP 를 참 직경 구로). / 실침대 표현부피가 참값의 0.986배로 제자리를 찾았고 σ_e 비 = **1.1232**(vox 0.15) · / **1.1438**(0.125), **아직 미수렴**." CONTRADICTED BY: `docs/reviews/claims.json` — CL-33 `status: hold`, CL-41 `status: hold`; `quotation_ban` pattern #13 is the literal string `1.1232`, claim CL-33, why: "p1 plate rule 산물, p2 재측정까지 인용 금지 (R5-CX-06)", allowed_in only `docs/data/prereg_v2/raw_sigma.json`. CLAUDE.md: "⛔ **그 비의 값은 인용 금지** — p1 plate rule 산물이다. 값은 원장 CL-33 (status `hold`) 에만 있고 `quotation_ban` 이 강제한다 (R5-CX-06)." MECHANISM PROVED by instrumenting the sweep: `BAN_NEAR_LINES = 2 | NEAR_MARKS = ('인용 금지','철회','반증','폐기','무효','~~','CL-')` → "line 25: pattern ×35.79 -> exempted_by=['철회','CL-']" and "line 43: ... exempted_by=['철회','CL-']" (both correctly retracted) but "**line 33: pattern 1.1232 -> exempted_by=['CL-']**" — the only marker is the `CL-34/CL-41` reference on line 32, which introduces the value affirmatively. Separately, `1.1438` (line 34) matches no registry pattern at all — the registry stores the full-precision `1.143817` — and `×35.8` at lines 69 and 79 escapes the `×35.79` pattern for the same truncation reason (verified: 4 undetected occurrences, of which lines 69/79 have no retraction word). Corroboration that these are guarded elsewhere: `scripts/build_methods_docx.py:498-499` keeps its own banned list `["1.1232","1.123191","+12.3 %",...,"1.143817","1.155448",...,"×35.79"]`.

Rewrite lines 69 and 79 to drop `×35.8` (see the separate finding on the 파급 section). Then report the two registry holes upstream: add truncated variants (`1.1438`, `1.1554`, `×35.8`) to `quotation_ban`, and tighten `BAN_NEAR_MARKS` so a bare `CL-` reference is not by itself a retraction marker (it is the weakest member of that tuple and is the only thing that fired here).

findings.locator: lines 36-39 (## 결론) and line 34 (table row 고유 약점)
findings.claim: The page's whole conclusion — that the two sigma solvers are independent measurements whose agreement constitutes frame[4] cross-validation — is refuted: the voxel solver sits on the contact-network solver's own `CONTACT_FREE` branch, and the repo has explicitly rejected reading agreement between them as independent validation.
findings.evidence: Page text: "둘은 **다른 이산화의 독립 측정** — 한쪽이 다른 쪽의 근사가 아니다. 일치하면 frame[4] 교차검증, 갈라지면 정량화된 이산화 한계"; table row "고유 약점 | 구 형상 고정 | 래스터 아티팩트". CONTRADICTED BY: (1) `docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md` (created 2026-09-08), §0: "DEM 접촉망은 접촉마다 **Holm/Maxwell 협착 `R = 1/(2σa)`** 를 직렬로 넣고 그것을 뺀 가지를 코드 주석이 **`CONTACT_FREE — upper bound, ideal contact limit`** 이라 부른다. **복셀 FV(STEP3)는 그 가지 위에 있다** — 라벨만 안 붙어 있었다." Verified in code: `scripts/network_conductivity.py:16` "2. CONTACT_FREE: R_constriction=0 → σ_cf (upper bound, ideal contact limit)" and :954, :1023, :1110. (2) `claims.json` CL-81 (`status: live`), which also records the gap size already stored as `R_brug_over_full` — median 4.04x (Hertz) / 6.69x (Physics) over n=157, range 2.3-13.6x. (3) `claims.json` CDX-23 `status: rejected`: "Voxel electronic extrapolation 11.76 mS/cm matching DEM 11.75 mS/cm independently validates both solvers → REJECT as independent physical validation; retain as one-case representation/code consistency." (4) CDX-24 `rejected`: "REJECT independent-confirmation wording; retain ... the explicit warning that voxel ionic is an upper bound."
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite the conclusion: the two are not independent estimands on the ionic axis — the voxel FV is the contact-network's `CONTACT_FREE` limit with the constriction term identically zero, so agreement is expected by construction and is not evidence. Add the measured multiplier (4.04x / 6.69x median, n=157, 6x scatter) and the two-component prescription (geometric constriction improves with refinement; the intrinsic interfacial term does not exist at all and stays zero as h->0). Add to the table's voxel weakness cell: "계면/협착 저항 항이 정확히 0 = CONTACT_FREE 상한". Carry CLAUDE.md's binding citation rule verbatim: any STEP3 sigma_ion absolute quoted next to experiment must say "협착 미포함 = CONTACT_FREE 상한", and "σ_ion 상대비교에 '공통모드 상쇄' 를 근거 없이 쓰지 않는다" (the multiplier scatters 6x across the corpus). Note the CL-81 exemption that Phase A (sigma_e, `--no-ion`) is unaffected, and that the exemption must not be carried to the ionic axis.

findings.claim: Two tags outside the schema's taxonomy were introduced by a single page, below the schema's own promotion threshold, and lint does not check tags.
findings.evidence: Page frontmatter: "tags: [**workflow, tooling**]". CONTRADICTED BY SCHEMA.md line 87-89: "## Tag Taxonomy (**3페이지 이상 모일 주제만 승격**) 시드: `pipeline` `epistemology` `calibration` `transport` `mpm` `dem` `electrochem` `review` `environment` `ml` `wiki` `additive`". Measured across all 21 pages: mpm 11, transport 9, pipeline 9, dem 7, review 7, calibration 6, epistemology 4, additive 3, wiki 3, electrochem 2, environment 2, **workflow 1, tooling 1**; seed tag `ml` is used by zero pages despite the repo carrying a large ML track (`scripts/ml_design_structure.py`, `docs/ml_v3_surrogate_cycling.md`, the frozen predictor). `lint.py`'s `REQ`/`ENUMS` do not include `tags` beyond requiring the key to exist.
findings.proposed_action: Either fold `workflow`/`tooling` into `environment` (or `wiki`), or promote them properly once three pages want them. Add a lint warning for tags outside the seed list so the taxonomy is enforced rather than aspirational. Separately, the unused `ml` seed tag marks a real coverage hole: the frozen predictor forms and their DO-NOT rules (do not re-screen phi_c, do not re-add the four dropped Stage 22.5 terms, do not re-fit the five locked exponents, do not push thermal higher) are among the highest-value do-not rules in CLAUDE.md and have no wiki page.

findings.claim: The schema's update policy and quality axes are prose-only with no machine backing, and the schema has no rule requiring a page that cites a ledger claim to record that claim's status — which is what let a `hold` value onto a page.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA.md:82-85: "새 정보가 기존 페이지와 충돌하면: 날짜/출처 확인 → 양쪽 입장 기록(덮어쓰기 금지) → confidence 하향 또는 양쪽 `disputed` → **lint 가 표면화**." But lint surfaces nothing of the kind — it has no ledger check, no numeric re-verification, and no `disputed` trigger; the only conflict-adjacent check is the `single-source` + `high` error. Meanwhile SCHEMA.md:15 lists the immutable-evidence layer without `claims.json`, and no boundary rule mentions the quotation ban even though `scripts/check_review_findings.py:104` puts `'wiki/**/*.md'` inside `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS`. CONTRADICTED BY CLAUDE.md rule ④: "**정본은 밖으로 강제되지 않으면 새어나간다** ... ⇒ 두 규칙이 상주한다: **`check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep`** ... · **`check_method_discipline.py` 규칙 J**" — i.e. the repo's own conclusion is that a prose policy is not a policy.
findings.proposed_action: Add a sixth boundary rule to SCHEMA: a page that cites a ledger claim must record the claim's status, and may not state a `hold`/`rejected`/`retired` number affirmatively — with the corresponding lint check (see the lint finding). Add `docs/reviews/claims.json` to the layer-1 evidence list. Make the Update Policy name its enforcer honestly: today it names lint, which does not implement it.

surface_worthy.why: Created 2026-09-08, canon for CL-81, referenced by no wiki page — and the existing comparison page asserts the opposite. It resolves a question that had been asked and mis-answered ('Phase A is sigma_e so it does not matter' was a dodge, per the doc's own opening). It also recovers a quantity that was already sitting in the corpus unlabelled.
surface_worthy.one_line: The voxel STEP3 solver is the contact-network's own `CONTACT_FREE` branch — the Holm/Maxwell constriction term R = 1/(2σa) is exactly zero — and the gap was already stored as `R_brug_over_full`: median 4.04x (Hertz) / 6.69x (Physics) over n=157, range 2.3-13.6x, triangulating with kim2025's GB-only 3.75x to within 8 %.

surface_worthy.why: 104 claims with a four-value status vocabulary plus a 22-entry `quotation_ban` registry that governs what may be written anywhere in the repo — including `wiki/**/*.md` — yet `grep -rn claims.json wiki/` finds it only in the one card the sweep forced. This is the single thing a future session most needs before writing a number, and the wiki currently does not mention it exists.
surface_worthy.one_line: claims.json is canon over prose: 74 live / 20 rejected / 6 hold / 4 retired, plus a 22-pattern quotation ban whose exemptions are allowed_in, a head banner carrying both a marker and a ledger anchor, or a retraction word within two lines.

surface_worthy.why: The 20 `rejected` CDX claims form a reusable catalogue of arguments that do not work, and six of them (CDX-16/17/18/21/23/24) reject the same move — calling two things independent when they share a scaffold, a modulus, a trajectory or a solver branch. Three wiki pages currently make that exact move. A page listing them would be the highest-leverage single addition to the hub.
surface_worthy.one_line: The word *independent* has been rejected six times: shared-scaffold coverage (CDX-16), DEM-to-MPM modulus import (CDX-17), the Furnas dip's two tools (CDX-18), three correlated extrapolations (CDX-21), and the voxel-vs-DEM sigma agreements (CDX-23, CDX-24).

surface_worthy.why: The live experiment. Four beds are done, 96 arms are pending, and the immediate gate is a 4-arm bridge sensitivity check whose thresholds were written before the run. The wiki has no live-experiment page at all, so a new session cannot find out what is in flight.
surface_worthy.one_line: Phase A: 6 mAh VGCF 1/2/3/4 wt% ordering, 96 STEP3 arms (4 compositions x 3 grids x 8 origins, `--no-ion`) at fixed Mach 0.03, Grade B (ordering conditional on the convention), gated on a ~1.5 h bridge check with |Δd| <= 0.05 proceed / 0.05-0.20 caveat / > 0.20 stop-and-re-register.

surface_worthy.why: CL-80 and CL-82 kill a reading that appears throughout the older material: that scaffold-run porosity says something about compaction. The measurement is unusually clean — a 9.6x change in reached stress moved porosity by 0.15 %p and made the bed 0.2 µm *thicker* — and it is buried inside a prereg body rather than stated as a rule.
surface_worthy.one_line: Reached pressure and bed state are decoupled in scaffold runs: `solid_vol` is fixed at seed time and `wall_z` is the only MPM output, so porosity is arithmetic, not evidence — never read scaffold porosity as proof of successful compaction.

surface_worthy.why: CL-72 and CL-74 retire an entire class of argument the wiki still leans on ('it moves monotonically, so the reported value is a bound'), and CL-74 records a judge that leaked at the last grid because `all(...)` over an empty tail is vacuously true. Both are general-purpose lessons, not SDCP-specific ones.
surface_worthy.one_line: Monotonicity across three grids does not bound the limit — R(h) = R∞ + h − 4h² is an elementary counterexample — and a convergence judge whose onset lands on the last row has confirmed nothing; report per spacing, never extrapolate, never call it a bound.

surface_worthy.why: CL-70 is the current answer on the sigma_SDCP axis and it replaces the retracted vox-0.4 sweep the wiki still cites in `anchor-waitlist.md`. Its structure is the interesting part: an anchor-free defense built from a sensitivity sweep, which is exactly the prescription CL-47/CL-61 called for after the literature anchor was withdrawn.
surface_worthy.one_line: The closure sweep is direction-robust at all nine grid points (min R̄ − 3·SD = 1.0522 vs threshold 1.01), and sigma_SDCP is asymmetric — x100 changes the gain by +3.5 % (saturated) while ÷100 removes 78 % and still leaves R > 1 — so the SDCP defense now rests on sensitivity, not on literature.

surface_worthy.why: CL-61 retracts a label the repo used for months and, more importantly, blocks a transfer of reasoning: the band argument that legitimises sigma_VGCF = 100 does not apply to SDCP. The wiki's `anchor-waitlist` still lists SDCP's open anchor as E_bind, which is no longer the biggest gap on that axis.
surface_worthy.one_line: sigma_SDCP = 250 S/cm has no literature anchor — reference [35] (Patil 1987) is 3-substituted polythiophene, not EDOT-class — so the canonical label is `Assumed (specified by the authors, S-PEDOT class)`, and CL-47's band defense of sigma_VGCF does not transfer because SDCP has no band.

surface_worthy.why: Rules 4 and 5 of the work-discipline block are the repo's two hardest-won operating lessons, and they are buried inside a ~41k-token file that the wiki was explicitly built to save people from reading end-to-end. Neither appears anywhere in the wiki, and the second one (subset filters) describes precisely how this wiki's own green lint misleads.
surface_worthy.one_line: Canon leaks unless enforced from outside (a value refuted on 08-12 was re-asserted on 08-19 and an independent review passed it against the stale canon), and the code that picks candidates is the blind spot — never filter by name fragment or file subset; run the real parser and enumerate the real manifest.

surface_worthy.why: The pre-commit gate exists, its header documents two repeat failures including one where a ledger typo blocked the user's GPU run, and it is named in no wiki page — while the wiki's own linter is one of the few checkers it does not call.
surface_worthy.one_line: `bash scripts/check_all.sh` before every commit: `--selftest` asks whether the checkers are right, the bare run asks whether the repo is right, and neither substitutes for the other — a ledger typo in this path is a fail-closed gate that stops GPU runs.

surface_worthy.why: 181 commits of manuscript work spread across ~20 documents, now on submission hold with five P1s, and the wiki has no entry point to any of it. The nominal run configuration that produced the reported numbers is, by the ledger's own account, recorded nowhere — which makes it exactly the kind of thing the wiki should hold.
surface_worthy.one_line: The Methods/SI package is on SUBMISSION HOLD (CL-86): the reported ratio 1.308 is DBE/SBE and was written inverted, the grid is 334x334x490 at vox 0.15, 'only the electrolyte densifies' is refuted by the code, and the nominal configuration (`VOX=.15`, `SDCP_SPHERE_D=.30`, `PTFE_STAMP=centerline`, 8 origins) needs a home.

surface_worthy.why: This is live track 2 and the wiki covers only its loading-rate half. The doc itself now demonstrates the freshness problem the wiki is supposed to solve: a rev7 section landed at line 855 on 2026-09-02, while the file-head banner still tells readers the file stopped at rev6.

summary: This scope holds 642 files under docs/data/, 56 under docs/figures/, and 167 top-level docs/*.md. The machine ban-sweep (`check_review_findings.py --ban-sweep`, 22 patterns × 844 files) reports "누수 없음 ✓", and the two seminar decks are correctly handled (retraction banner inserted as presentation slide 1, originals untouched — verified with the repo's own presentation-order reader). But the sweep's clean bill is partly false: I reproduced two exemption holes with the checker's own functions. (a) `docs/digest_model_application_backlog.md` line 18 carries the retracted `+52.0%` / `+45.4%` / `+5.6%` / `+18%` SDCP headline inside one giant table cell, exempted only because that same line coincidentally contains `무효` (about E_bind) and `폐기` (about a conformal-film proxy); the file has no file-level banner. (b) `docs/data/sdcp318_sigma_sdcp_sweep/sweep_summary.csv` carries the whole retracted σ_SDCP sweep (3.002 S/cm, `vs_SBE_pct` 52.0, annotated "★앵커 확정") and is invisible to the registry because the numbers are written undecorated. A third class — p1 plate-rule ratios `1.1232`/`1.1438`/`+12.3 %` in `docs/report_mpm_and_sigma_usability_20260819.md` — passes only because ±2-line markers retract *different* claims. The single most serious finding is not a number leak: `docs/data/phase_a_6mah/README.md` declares the Phase A bed a "new realization" because the old campaign's coordinates were lost, yet its committed `am_scaffold.csv.gz` / `se_scaffold.csv.gz` are byte-identical (body sha256 `bf138fbe3ab5af2f` / `45b978f1793ab6bf`) to `docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/kit_ps_7_3__*.csv.gz`, which have been in git since 2026-08-07 — and the two `angular_risk` JSONs derived from them are identical to 17 decimal places while carrying different bed labels. That mistake traces directly to `docs/data_inventory_20260825.md`, which states only real14 carries particle coordinates when five kit_ps beds do. Structurally: 17 of 18 docs/data subdirectories have no README (only `phase_a_6mah`; `sdcp_runs/_scan.txt` is the one other index), and docs/figures/README.md (2026-05-07) documents one figure and describes a panel workflow the repo no longer uses, leaving the current manuscript figures (sigma_e_bars, cbd_contacts, fig4b) entirely undocumented. Across docs/*.md the dominant pattern is calibration/validation documents from June–July that still assert claims the Codex round rejected (CDX-12/16/17/18/23/24) with no banner: `mpm3d_calibration.md`, `voxel_conductivity_crossvalidation.md`, `mpm_scaffold_reliability_and_am_freeze.md`, `mpm_dip_resolution_invariance.md`, `esse_calibration_2mAh_real_9.md`. The April-era formula docs (`thermal_conductivity_derivation.md`, `electronic_conductivity_derivation.md`, `Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md`, `v29_formula_terms.md`) still present superseded forms as "Final". Overall health: the machinery and the newest canon (voxel_contact_free_gap.md, phase_a_6mah kit runbook) are excellent; the derived layer from June–August is where canon has leaked.

findings.locator: Ionic conductivity table, row 'single-crystal / grain-interior (project value)'
findings.claim: The file labels σ = 3.0 mS/cm as a single-crystal LPSCl value attributed to Cronau and still carries an unresolved 'verify before manuscript' flag — but the repo's own Cronau digest proves the paper contains no single-crystal measurement and no LPSCl measurement at all, and says it closes this exact flag.
findings.evidence: docs/data/lpscl_electrolyte_params.md: '| single-crystal / grain-interior (project value) | 3.0 mS/cm (Cronau adopted) | Cronau 2021 ACS Energy Lett. doi:10.1021/acsenergylett.1c01299 ⚠ exact single-crystal digit NOT verified (proxy) — verify from ACS PDF before manuscript |'. docs/lit_cronau2021_stack_pressure_ionic_conductivity.md §0: '3.0 mS/cm 이 본문/그림/표에 직접 나오는가? ✗ 아니오 … single-crystal Li₆PS₅Cl 을 측정했는가? ✗ 아니오 … 측정한 argyrodite 는 Li₆PS₅Br (Br!) 이다' and 'lpscl_electrolyte_params.md 가 이미 단 플래그("exact single-crystal digit NOT verified (proxy)")를 확정해준다 — 본 정독으로 그 플래그는 "확인됨: 단결정값 아님" 으로 닫힌다.' The digest's recommended re-attribution text has not been applied to the data file (digest dated 2026-06-26; data file unchanged since 2026-06-24).
findings.proposed_action: Apply the digest's recommended label verbatim: 'σ_grain = 3.0 mS/cm — LPSCl grain-interior project value; basis: Cronau 2021 µC-Li₆PS₅Br high-pressure plateau ~2.0–2.4 mS/cm plus cold-press/sintered LPSCl literature 1–6 mS/cm. ⚠ not a direct single-crystal LPSCl measurement', and close the verify flag. Note the same 'single-crystal grain-interior' phrasing has already propagated into CL-81, so check that line too.

findings.locator: '## Final Formula' block, σ_th = 286 × σ_ion^{3/4} × φ_AM² × CN_SE^{-1}
findings.claim: Three April-era derivation documents present superseded transport formulas as 'Final' with no supersession banner: the single-constant thermal power law, the early electronic power law, and FORM X for ionic.
findings.evidence: docs/thermal_conductivity_derivation.md: 'σ_th = 286 × σ_ion^{3/4} × φ_AM² × CN_SE^{-1}' with '286 | Fitted constant (유일한 free parameter)'. CLAUDE.md Stage T1: 'A. Pure power-law (κ = ∏ feature^c …): LOOCV ceiling 0.59 … C. Ridge regression (14 structural features): LOOCV 0.85-0.90 … Ridge is the irreducible representation; pure power-law and 2-phase EMT both fail.' docs/electronic_conductivity_derivation.md: 'σ_el = 0.015 × σ_AM × φ_AM^{3/2} × CN_AM² × exp(π/(T/d_AM))' with 'σ_AM (NCM811) | 0.05 S/cm', vs the production Stage 22.5 form and its LOCKED endpoints σ_S = 10 / σ_P = 5 mS/cm. docs/Scaling_Law_Report_Full.md: '**Final Formula**: FORM X — σ = C × σ_grain × (φ_SE - φc)^¾ × CN × √cov / √τ', vs CLAUDE.md 'FORM X (v4++) … is the OLDER, inferior model — kept only as a legacy toggle / predictor fallback.' None of the three carries a banner (grep for supersede/deprecat/HISTORICAL/철회/폐기 returns nothing).
findings.proposed_action: Add a one-line head banner to each of the three files naming the current production form and the CLAUDE.md section that owns it, so a reader hitting the word 'Final' is redirected before copying an exponent into a paper.

findings.claim: A submission-ready LaTeX caption describes a superseded porosity model on a superseded corpus, with no marker; the current porosity canon reports a different target, a different n, and different scores.
findings.evidence: Caption: '2D porosity surface ε(f_AM, λ_eff) for the 82-case DEM corpus, fitted with the v4 physics model … R² = 0.674, RMSE = 2.27 %p (trust = 1.70) … v4 uses 6 physical-principle groups with 23 parameters total.' docs/porosity_regression_final.md (2026-06-30) is headed '✅ CLOSED (stage2 종료, 2026-06-30) — n_collection=153' and reports 'gated best (plastic 포함, 생산형) LOOCV 0.583 · R² 0.637 · RMSE 2.32 %p · n=129' and 'rigid ε_sphere (DEM native) 0.769 / 0.830 / 2.45 %p'. The v4 figure assets (_porosity_v4_bootstrap.npz, porosity_v4_*.png) are all 2026-05-19.
findings.proposed_action: Mark the caption file and the v4 figure family as superseded by the CLOSED n=153 regression, or move them to an archive subdirectory so they are not picked up as a paper-ready caption.

findings.claim: Four committed figure files are referenced by no document, script default, or index — their generator writes to a different default filename, so nothing in the repo records what bed or recipe they show.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep for each basename (excluding .git, __pycache__, litdb_cache) returns zero hits outside docs/figures itself. The plausible generator, scripts/validate_additive_seeding.py, defaults to a different name: "ap.add_argument('--out', default='docs/figures/additive_seed_check.png')" and its usage example writes additive_seed_check.png, which does not exist in the directory. All four files date to 2026-06-24. By contrast the cbd_contacts_* and sigma_e_bars_* families also return zero literal hits but are provably generated by `--out` base + extension in plot_cbd_contacts.py / plot_sigma_e_bars.py, so they are not orphans.
findings.proposed_action: Record each of the four in the rewritten docs/figures README with the command that produced it, or delete them; they are the only figure assets with no recoverable provenance.

findings.claim: A tracked data file lives inside a directory the repository ignores, so any regenerated or additional file in that directory will be silently untracked while this one stays.
findings.evidence: .gitignore line 25 is 'docs/db/'; `git ls-files docs/db/` returns docs/db/section7_10case_sweep.csv (tracked, so the ignore rule does not apply to it); `git check-ignore -v docs/db/section7_10case_sweep.csv` returns nothing for the tracked path. The file is consumed by scripts/plot_section7_design_rules.py, which feeds docs/figures/section7_design_rules.png and docs/paper/main.tex. docs/TODO_post_stage_e_rerun.md also names 'docs/db/.mtime_cache.json' as a purge target, i.e. the directory doubles as a cache.
findings.proposed_action: Either move section7_10case_sweep.csv into docs/data/ (where its siblings live and where the inventory can see it) or add a negation rule '!docs/db/section7_10case_sweep.csv' so the intent is explicit.

findings.claim: One file declares two different final models: its header freezes v9 BLEND at n=57 and line 121 declares v12-clean v3 the final production model — and neither is the current production form.
findings.evidence: Header: 'Dataset: n=57 (Ionic v9 BLEND) … Final model: **v9 BLEND** (R²=0.9806, LOOCV=0.9764)'. Line 121: '## 🏆 FINAL PRODUCTION MODEL: v12-clean v3 (2026-04-18)' with 'σ_ionic = C_blend(τ) × σ_grain × √(φ-0.2) × CN^(3/2) × cov^(2/5) × f_p³'. CLAUDE.md cites this file for the second declaration ('docs/ionic_scaling_law_experiments.md (line 122 declares v12-clean v3 FINAL)') and states the current production form separately as the T1 form with CN², cov_Hertz^½, the power gate, P2 and f_intact at LOOCV ≈ 0.975 on n=88.
findings.proposed_action: Retitle the file as a troubleshooting log (which is what it is), delete or date-stamp both 'final' declarations, and point to CLAUDE.md's T1 section for the production form.

surface_worthy.why: Newest canon (2026-09-08, CL-81) and the binding citation rule for every STEP3 σ_ion absolute quoted next to experiment; created after most other docs and therefore invisible to anyone browsing by filename or date-in-title
surface_worthy.one_line: The voxel solver sits on the CONTACT_FREE branch — the Holm/GB constriction term is exactly zero, the gap is 4.04×/6.69× median over n=157, and it scatters 6× across the corpus so σ_ion ratios are not automatically common-mode safe.

surface_worthy.one_line: Repeated-cycle MPM cannot be a fade engine: frozen AM cannot push SE back, isochoric J2 forbids permanent contact loss, and voxel-adjacency coverage quantises the signal — rejected at design review.
